changes.what: New module that counts spawned helper processes by kind and starts a Windows machine-wide tasklist census every ten minutes.
New shared model that owns the live count by kind and reports floods via a per-kind, per-scope rate-limited callback.

Adds inspectWindowsWatchdogMarkers scanning WATCHDOG_FILE_PREFIX files for active, orphaned, and legacy-stale watchdogs, plus admitWindowsWatchdog that reports and refuses arming past MAX_CONCURRENT_WINDOWS_WATCHDOGS.
Adds reportCliProcessHealth that attaches version, platform, arch, and freebuff context to helper-process flood and outlived-parent reports.
Calls trackHelperProcess on launcher probes in renderer-cleanup.ts, clipboard children in clipboard.ts, and terminal_command children in terminal-command-broker.ts.
Defines cli.helper_process_flood and cli.helper_outlived_parent event constants.

3b3d023eea37cbdbaadeafc904eb4179aa444efc.text: Engineers added three new tracking labels so they can measure how the paid-ad pricing leg (COD-654) is performing when a first-party ad is fetched. The labels record the verdict (whether it led to an ad showing or not), the mode it ran in, and which advertised campaign was involved, but only when that pricing step actually ran. You do not see this yourself; it does not change your experience and needs no action from you. This is internal telemetry work for the Freebuff team.

4a8b060def270c1beedad8f4d70b9233fdaa50eb.text: This release expands Freebuff to Windows Desktop so eligible ad-sponsored coding sessions can run there, and it upgrades the set of AI models available to provisioned (early-access) accounts, adding per-account tiers such as GPT-6 Sol and Luna Pro, o3 Pro, Claude Opus 5.5 and 4.8, Qwen3.8, Grok 4.7, Gemini 3.7 Flash, Kimi K3, GLM 5.3, Mistral Large, Codestral, and Llama 4 Maverick. Windows sponsored runs now use the OS-native file layer with proper Windows path and symlink handling plus a macOS fix so git commits reach the real developer-folder git instead of Apple's xcode-select shim. The BYOK (bring-your-own-key) model flow now gives a specific, model-named error when you supply an unrecognized model ID instead of a generic 'request failed' message, and the sponsored file tools pin directories directly in the process rather than through a brokered shell helper. Two new privacy decision limits let the service flag suspicious egress (tunnels or datacenter anonymizers and cross-country clock mismatches) without immediately blocking it, so the restricted free-model picker can explain the smaller set of available models. Helper-process tracking now watches clipboard, terminal, launcher, and watchdog helpers in the CLI, and first-party ad telemetry gains the CPM leg fields needed for the new pricing measurement. Upgrading gives you an expanded, account-specific model roster, Windows Desktop availability for sponsored runs, clearer BYOK model errors, and stronger privacy and process-health observability while leaving existing workflows intact.

bd83e63a1780109930f5c221b1f2ed09b2cb91e2.text: The assistant now keeps a quiet watch over the little helper programs it opens (like the clipboard tool and terminal commands) and, on Windows, over how many system programs are running in total. If it sees far too many of a single kind at once, or notices a helper still running after the main program has exited, it logs that situation so the team can spot a runaway process. This is internal reliability work: it lets Freebuff fix stuck or multiplying programs before they slow your machine, but you won't see a new feature or notice any change in how you work.

647b60fcacc407c79c5d661abd8fe28bf89c445d.title: Per-OS sponsored agentic switches for Windows and Linux desktop
647b60fcacc407c79c5d661abd8fe28bf89c445d.summary: Adds `common/src/ads/sponsored-os-policy.ts` as the shared table and reader for per-Desktop-OS rollout switches, introducing env knobs `FREEBUFF_SPONSORED_WINDOWS` (surface `desktop_windows`) and `FREEBUFF_SPONSORED_LINUX` (surface `desktop_linux`), each opened only by the exact value `on`. Refactors `common/src/ads/sponsored-windows.ts` so its Windows policy, surface, switch state, and execution-capability predicate delegate to the generic machinery, keeping the same public names and behavior. Linux serving is additionally gated by the client proving a `bwrap` sandbox, so a missing `bwrap` means no capability is reported.
647b60fcacc407c79c5d661abd8fe28bf89c445d.evidence: New file `common/src/ads/sponsored-os-policy.ts` adds `SPONSORED_OS_SWITCHES` mapping `windows` to env `FREEBUFF_SPONSORED_WINDOWS` and `linux` to env `FREEBUFF_SPONSORED_LINUX`, with surfaces `desktop_windows` and `desktop_linux`, plus `readSponsoredOsPolicy` returning non-null `SPONSORED_OS_ON` only when the env value is the exact string `on`. Modified file `common/src/ads/sponsored-windows.ts` now imports `SPONSORED_OS_SWITCHES`, `SPONSORED_OS_ON`, `sponsoredOsSwitchState`, `sponsoredOsExecutionCapable`, and `readSponsoredOsPolicy` from `./sponsored-os-policy`, redefining `SPONSORED_WINDOWS_ON`, `SPONSORED_WINDOWS_EXECUTION_SURFACE`, and `readSponsoredWindowsPolicy` as aliases over the shared policy.
647b60fcacc407c79c5d661abd8fe28bf89c445d.migration: If you operate Freebuff sponsorship, set `FREEBUFF_SPONSORED_WINDOWS=on` and `FREEBUFF_SPONSORED_LINUX=on` (exact value) to open paid Desktop agentic serving on Windows and Linux respectively.

647b60fcacc407c79c5d661abd8fe28bf89c445d.text: Freebuff has added independent on/off switches that control whether paid AI coding tasks can be offered on Windows and Linux desktop computers, separate from the macOS experience. This is an internal configuration change affecting only the operators who run the Freebuff service, not individual users. No action is required by users today, since the switches start disabled and nothing changes in the assistant's behavior unless an operator turns them on.

3180425d0b41feb1359a31abcf39ab569f241c95.title: SDK guards git and gh spawns against synchronous throws on Windows
3180425d0b41feb1359a31abcf39ab569f241c95.summary: `getGitChanges` in `sdk/src/run-state.ts` now wraps `git` and `gh` spawns with `spawnSafely`, a local helper that calls `consume(spawn(...))` inside a try/catch and rejects on failure before passing the child to `childProcessToPromise`, so a synchronous throw from a Windows .cmd/.bat shim is caught by the same `.catch` that handles rejected promises instead of escaping past every `.catch` and aborting the turn. The fix addresses the crash in PR #1341 (handle cyclic run-state on session resume) that surfaced while testing /undo and /redo, where a spawn throwing synchronously on Windows killed the CLI on the second interaction of a resumed session. `getGitChanges` is shared across the SDK and CLI for git and gh invocations, so any caller of the run-state module benefits from the guarded spawn path.
3180425d0b41feb1359a31abcf39ab569f241c95.evidence: sdk/src/run-state.ts adds a `spawnSafely` wrapper around `spawn` inside `getGitChanges`, routing `git` and `gh` invocations through `childProcessToPromise`; an adjacent comment states spawn throws synchronously on Windows .cmd/.bat shims due to cmd.exe special characters like %, and the new test title reads "survives a spawn that throws synchronously (Windows .cmd git shim)".
3180425d0b41feb1359a31abcf39ab569f241c95.unknowns: The diff shows the spawn guard but the notes attribute the change to #1341 while the hunks only cover getGitChanges; whether the cyclic-state clone fix lives in a separate hunk not shown is not visible in this snapshot.

ef7e96ccccc4622bd69833efea93f8cb9a6a9794.title: Windows floor broker and surface pairing for COD-642 sponsored runs
ef7e96ccccc4622bd69833efea93f8cb9a6a9794.summary: The sponsored runtime gains a Windows floor arm (`'floor'`) selected by `sponsoredBrokerArm` only when platform is `win32` and the server grant names `desktop_windows` with containment: 'floor', which is then run through an absolute-path `powershell.exe` with `SPONSORED_POWERSHELL_ARGS` and the `ownsShell` broker path in `run-terminal-command`. The CLI and capability layer now refuse Windows entirely (`'windows_no_containment'` and `file_layer_unavailable` for file tools too large), while the accept pairing in `sponsored-compute-contract.ts` only admits a `desktop_windows` row to a `desktop_windows` client via `acceptClientSurfacePairsWithRow`. The model is told which shell it has through `RunOptions.terminalShell` applied by `applyTerminalShell`, which swaps in `powershellNote` on the system prompt when `systemInfo.shell === 'powershell'`. This spans more than 4000 added lines and touches CLI, shared core, agent-runtime and SDK surfaces per the analysis notes, so the surface pairing, floor broker and prompt note are the user-relevant faces of a broader COD-642 change set.
ef7e96ccccc4622bd69833efea93f8cb9a6a9794.evidence: The diff adds COD-642's Windows floor path across `common/src/ads/sponsored-local-execution.ts` (new `SponsoredLocalFloorContainment`, `SPONSORED_LOCAL_FLOOR_GRANT`, `SPONSORED_WINDOWS_ENV_ALLOWLIST`, `scrubSponsoredWindowsEnv` reading `HOMEDRIVE`/`HOMEPATH`/`GCM_INTERACTIVE`), `sdk/src/tools/sponsored-sandbox.ts` (`sponsoredBrokerArm` returning `'floor'`, `createWindowsFloorBroker`, `SPONSORED_POWERSHELL_ARGS`, absolute-path `powershell.exe`), `sdk/src/run.ts` (`RunOptions.terminalShell`, `applyTerminalShell`), `sdk/src/tools/run-terminal-command.ts` (`TerminalCommandBroker.ownsShell`, `TerminalCommandSpawnRequest.command`), `cli/src/utils/sponsored-cli-capability.ts` (imports `sponsoredLocalContainmentIsFloor`, refuses `'windows_no_containment'` and floor probes), `common/src/ads/sponsored-capability.ts` (`file_layer_unavailable` reason, `sponsoredDesktopExecutionSurfaceForPlatform`), `common/src/ads/sponsored-compute-contract.ts` (`acceptClientSurfacePairsWithRow`, `SPONSORED_ACCEPT_EXECUTION_SURFACE_PARAM`), `common/src/ads/sponsored-consent.ts` (`SPONSORED_CONSENT_WINDOWS_FLOOR_SENTENCE`), and `common/src/ads/sponsored-proposal-view.ts` (`execution_surface` field).
ef7e96ccccc4622bd69833efea93f8cb9a6a9794.unknowns: The diff does not show the server-side gate `FREEBUFF_SPONSORED_WINDOWS` that serves `desktop_windows`, the Desktop consent-bridge CJS mirror that `consent-window.render.test.ts` pins to these constants, or the rollout of the `execution_surface` projection to existing offer rows.

changes.what: Adds the Windows floor broker arm: `sponsoredBrokerArm` returns 'floor' for a Windows host whose grant names the floor, `createWindowsFloorBroker` builds the `ownsShell` broker, and `sponsoredWindowsFloorLaunch` runs `request.command` through absolute-path `powershell.exe` with fixed switches.

Adds `scrubSponsoredWindowsEnv` (allowlist `SPONSORED_WINDOWS_ENV_ALLOWLIST` plus `HOMEDRIVE`/`HOMEPATH`/`GCM_INTERACTIVE`/`GIT_*`/git config) and `RunOptions.terminalShell` routed through `applyTerminalShell` into `systemInfo.shell`, which swaps `powershellNote` into the system prompt for Windows.
Adds `acceptClientSurfacePairsWithRow` plus `SPONSORED_ACCEPT_EXECUTION_SURFACE_PARAM`, and the row's `execution_surface` field, so a Windows offer is accepted only by a `desktop_windows` client.

The CLI refuses Windows sponsorship (`'windows_no_containment'`), treats any containment probe that is the floor as `containment_probe_failed`, and adds the `'file_layer_unavailable'` reason for file tools that cannot hold a project's volume, beside `sponsoredDesktopExecutionSurfaceForPlatform`.

Introduces `SponsoredLocalFloorContainment`, `SPONSORED_LOCAL_FLOOR_GRANT`, `sponsoredLocalAvailability` with the `offersFloor` option, `sponsoredLocalGrant` over the floor/grant match, and `sponsoredWindowsRunPaths`/`scrubSponsoredWindowsEnv` for the per-run environment.
Adds the `powershellNote` export and emits it in the system prompt when `systemInfo.shell === 'powershell'`, instead of the bash `windowsNote`.

3180425d0b41feb1359a31abcf39ab569f241c95.text: The development kit now catches a specific crash that could happen on Windows when it asks Git for information about your project changes, so the tool is more stable when developers build programs that integrate with Freebuff. This affects only the engineers who write code using the developer kit, not people using the Freebuff assistant directly. If you are building a program that reads Git history through the kit, you will not see it crash on Windows anymore; everyone else notices nothing different.

ef7e96ccccc4622bd69833efea93f8cb9a6a9794.text: Sponsored tasks (advertiser-funded runs the assistant performs against a real repository) can now actually run on Windows computers, where they previously could not run at all. The change targets sponsors who buy Windows-based ad campaigns: a Windows sponsor task is paired only with a Windows sponsor task that was minted for Windows, and a Windows task can no longer be accepted by or offered to a non-Windows client. The task runs in a 'floor' mode on Windows, which uses the user's own Windows permissions rather than a sandbox, so the user is now shown an extra consent sentence explaining there is no sandbox on Windows and their Windows permissions apply and credentials are hidden from the task but not locked away.

1bd6ccee9aa99ed5177e9a14441e2449c70e824c.title: Freebuff CLI ships release 0.0.190
1bd6ccee9aa99ed5177e9a14441e2449c70e824c.summary: The Freebuff CLI `version` field in `freebuff/cli/release/package.json` was bumped from `0.0.189` to `0.0.190`, marking the latest 0.0.x line release as a pure release-bump with no other manifest fields changed in this commit.

1bd6ccee9aa99ed5177e9a14441e2449c70e824c.text: This release adds more control over the sponsored messages you see in the Freebuff desktop apps. You can now turn on sponsored help on Windows and Linux desktops separately using two new settings, one for each operating system. The Windows messages work right away, while the Linux messages only appear if you have the bwrap security tool installed on your computer. The system also reads these settings more safely, since it checks for exactly the word "on" before showing anything. Upgrading means you get finer control over sponsored desktop prompts, and Linux users without bwrap won't see the Linux-sponsored messages at all. The update just adds these ad switches and doesn't change anything else you do with Freebuff.

3e55a8b290e863f5fded6e1d727968ac17e1e8b2.title: Terminal watchdog fixture tests tty write in reused-pid mode
3e55a8b290e863f5fded6e1d727968ac17e1e8b2.summary: The test fixture for the terminal watchdog in cli/src/__tests__/helpers/terminal-watchdog-fixture.ts removed the `waitForArmed()` call in the 'reused-pid' branch and replaced it with a direct tty read loop. This change reflects that a watchdog with no matching owner writes its `.armed` marker, fires, and deletes it again within milliseconds, too fast for the 50ms poll to observe, which produced false exit 3 failures on the Windows smoke pipeline. No production runtime behavior changed; this is test suite verification only.
3e55a8b290e863f5fded6e1d727968ac17e1e8b2.evidence: cli/src/__tests__/helpers/terminal-watchdog-fixture.ts (commit nature: test-only, +4/−3) replaced `await waitForArmed()` in the 'reused-pid' branch with a polling loop that reads the tty to confirm the watchdog fired, because the marker file `.armed` can be created and deleted within milliseconds and missed by the 50ms poll, causing exit 3 on the Windows smoke pipeline.
3e55a8b290e863f5fded6e1d727968ac17e1e8b2.unknowns: The diff shows a test-only change with no shipped code edits, so the actual watchdog runtime behavior is unchanged and this only affects the test harness used to verify it.

f5fb47b37687cbae5e7295bf63a5c3c2aebd79aa.title: Freebuff 0.0.191 published
f5fb47b37687cbae5e7295bf63a5c3c2aebd79aa.summary: The `version` field in `freebuff/cli/release/package.json` was bumped from `0.0.190` to `0.0.191`, producing the freebuff 0.0.191 CLI release. The change is confined to the release manifest with no logic changes.
f5fb47b37687cbae5e7295bf63a5c3c2aebd79aa.evidence: The diff in `freebuff/cli/release/package.json` changes the `version` field from `0.0.190` to `0.0.191`; analysis notes confirm this is the Freebuff CLI release 0.0.191 published.

f5fb47b37687cbae5e7295bf63a5c3c2aebd79aa.text: Freebuff 0.0.191 fixes a test that was falsely failing on Windows. The release corrects a timing issue in the terminal watchdog test, where a watchdog with no matching owner writes its armed marker, fires, and deletes it again too fast for the test to observe, which had been causing fake exit 3 failures on the Windows build pipeline. The test now reads the terminal output directly instead of waiting for the marker. This update ensures the Windows build pipeline runs without false test failures, so the release is verified correctly and shipped on schedule.

e2ab7528c3f2bd0dd243b92bffd0105ca1a9376d.title: Add generic setup invitation version constants
e2ab7528c3f2bd0dd243b92bffd0105ca1a9376d.summary: Two new exported constants land in common/src/ads/generic-setup-invitation.ts to gate generic invitation handling by Desktop client version. GENERIC_SETUP_INVITATION_MIN_DESKTOP_VERSION is set to [0, 0, 124], the first Desktop release whose parser knows generic_setup, below which the server must not answer a generic invitation because older builds drop it without a trace. GENERIC_INVITATION_READY_DISCOVERY_VERSION is set to 1, marking the invitationReadyDiscoveryVersion request field where a value of 1 makes this Desktop draw a generic invitation on a READY-project discovery request too instead of withholding it. No code in this diff consumes either constant yet.
e2ab7528c3f2bd0dd243b92bffd0105ca1a9376d.evidence: The diff adds two new exported constants to common/src/ads/generic-setup-invitation.ts: GENERIC_SETUP_INVITATION_MIN_DESKTOP_VERSION = [0, 0, 124] as const and GENERIC_INVITATION_READY_DISCOVERY_VERSION = 1. Neither constant has a reader in this diff, so they are defined but do nothing yet.
e2ab7528c3f2bd0dd243b92bffd0105ca1a9376d.unknowns: The diff shows no reader for either constant, so it is unclear which server or client field these values are intended to be compared against in production.

e2ab7528c3f2bd0dd243b92bffd0105ca1a9376d.text: The Freebuff engineering team added two internal version-reference markers inside the shared code library that will eventually tell the server which versions of the desktop app are allowed to receive a certain non-billable setup invitation, and which request type that desktop version is expected to answer. These markers are in place today but are not yet read by any running code, so they do not change anything in the app right now and require no action from anyone. The only people this concerns are the Freebuff maintainers themselves, since this is internal bookkeeping for a future rollout; everyday users will see no difference.

64b603f06d6997dafc5dcbe4abbef0711ffbce7b.title: FirstMessage CAPI now treats accepted status as delivered
64b603f06d6997dafc5dcbe4abbef0711ffbce7b.summary: The status allowlist in sendGravityFirstMessageConversion for FirstMessage results now includes 'accepted', alongside 'ok', 'duplicate', 'test_ok', and 'skipped'. A comment notes production returns 'accepted' (HTTP 200) for a live FirstMessage, so previously treating it as a failure caused duplicate sends and daily false 'Failed to track' errors.
64b603f06d6997dafc5dcbe4abbef0711ffbce7b.evidence: In common/src/gravity-capi.ts, sendGravityFirstMessageConversion's FirstMessage result-status allowlist is extended to include 'accepted' alongside 'ok', 'duplicate', 'test_ok', and 'skipped', with an inline comment stating production returns 'accepted' (HTTP 200) for a live FirstMessage.

64b603f06d6997dafc5dcbe4abbef0711ffbce7b.text: The assistant's ad-tracking system now recognizes the server's standard "accepted" reply as a successful send, instead of treating it like an error and resending the same message. This stops duplicate ad events and ends the steady stream of false "tracking failed" warnings in the service logs. Only the team that runs the Freebuff service is affected; everyday users do not notice anything change.

ca2ab71930627f10421e38186dfda628e6c14b9a.title: Sanitize and hash MCP tool names for provider compatibility
ca2ab71930627f10421e38186dfda628e6c14b9a.summary: MCP tool names containing dots, spaces, slashes, or colons previously produced exposed names every provider rejected, failing the entire turn; mcpExposedToolName now sanitizes and, when needed, truncates with a stable hash, leaving already-valid names byte-identical. The original server and tool are recorded on the definition as mcpOrigin only when names are sanitized, and tool-executor routes execution through mcpOrigin otherwise falling back to the legacy server__tool split. Two originals sanitizing to the same name are kept distinct and callable via appended hashes.
ca2ab71930627f10421e38186dfda628e6c14b9a.evidence: packages/agent-runtime/src/mcp.ts adds the mcpExposedToolName function and VALID_TOOL_NAME/LEGACY_VALID_TOOL_NAME constants, and getMCPToolData now sanitizes and hashes MCP tool names before storing them; common/src/util/file.ts adds the optional mcpOrigin field to customToolDefinitionsSchema; packages/agent-runtime/src/tools/tool-executor.ts introduces mcpTarget and routes execution via the mcpOrigin field when present.
ca2ab71930627f10421e38186dfda628e6c14b9a.unknowns: The diff does not show which consumer introduces invalid MCP names or confirm this is rolled out in production.

changes.what: Defines mcpExposedToolName and the VALID_TOOL_NAME and LEGACY_VALID_TOOL_NAME constants, and getMCPToolData now sanitizes, truncates with a stable hash, and records mcpOrigin when names are sanitized.
Adds the optional mcpOrigin field to customToolDefinitionsSchema to carry the original server and tool when an exposed name is sanitized.
Introduces mcpTarget and routes execution through mcpOrigin when present, falling back to the legacy server__tool split otherwise.

ca2ab71930627f10421e38186dfda628e6c14b9a.text: Some plugins that add extra tools to the assistant used names with dots, spaces, slashes, or colons, which every supported provider rejected. Those names are now cleaned up and, when still too long, shortened with a stable fingerprint, leaving already-valid names untouched. You should now be able to use a plugin whose tool names previously caused the assistant to fail on every turn; no action is needed from you.

cf92539c44eeb4374a3afa370e3e789fd7d2e76d.title: Freebuff CLI version bumped to 0.0.192
cf92539c44eeb4374a3afa370e3e789fd7d2e76d.summary: The Freebuff CLI package manifest in `freebuff/cli/release/package.json` now declares version `0.0.192`, up from `0.0.191`. This is a release-bump commit that advances the `0.0.x` free-tier distribution line, with no logic changes in the diff.
cf92539c44eeb4374a3afa370e3e789fd7d2e76d.evidence: In `freebuff/cli/release/package.json`, the `version` field was bumped from `0.0.191` to `0.0.192` in a one-line edit.

cf92539c44eeb4374a3afa370e3e789fd7d2e76d.text: Freebuff is bumped to 0.0.192, tightening two backend systems that affect your daily work. Advertising tracking now accepts the 'accepted' status the live service returns for a first message, so you stop getting duplicate tracking attempts and daily false 'Failed to track' errors in your logs. When you connect an external tool through the MCP bridge, its name gets cleaned up and shortened with a stable hash if it contains dots, spaces, slashes, or colons, which previously made every provider reject the entire turn; already-valid names stay unchanged, and if two different tools sanitize to the same name they remain distinct and callable via the appended hash.

a37fe64d9e2827c546e3556d2a20d7e0abc46f16.title: BYOK DeepSeek requests backfill reasoning content on tool-call
a37fe64d9e2827c546e3556d2a20d7e0abc46f16.summary: byokRequestTransform now runs backfillDeepSeekReasoning over the message list for direct DeepSeek and proxied endpoints, inserting reasoning_content: '' on assistant tool-call messages that appear after the last user message. DeepSeek validates the thinking-mode tool loop server-side and 400s when an assistant tool-call message omits reasoning_content, a field the hosted lane backfills but BYOK requests never received.
a37fe64d9e2827c546e3556d2a20d7e0abc46f16.evidence: sdk/src/impl/byok-request.ts adds the exported function backfillDeepSeekReasoning and a deepSeekReplay flag inside byokRequestTransform; the transform now prepends backfillDeepSeekReasoning(body.messages) when deepSeekReplay is true and body.messages is an array.
a37fe64d9e2827c546e3556d2a20d7e0abc46f16.unknowns: The rollout timing of the related hosted backfill in web/src/llm-api/deepseek-request-body.ts is not shown in this diff. A second read of the same diff did not confirm that a migration step is required.

a37fe64d9e2827c546e3556d2a20d7e0abc46f16.text: The Freebuff SDK now adds a small piece of data called reasoning_content to each assistant response that happens after you ask a question, when you connect the SDK straight to DeepSeek with your own API key. This affects developers who use Freebuff's SDK to connect directly to DeepSeek models (not through an intermediary). Previously, the first reply the assistant gave after calling a tool would fail and get rejected by DeepSeek's servers, causing errors during coding sessions; now that reply is accepted and work continues normally.

66a66e08e64bfa2135020b98d249ddbe773cbda1.title: Freebuff CLI released as version 0.0.193
66a66e08e64bfa2135020b98d249ddbe773cbda1.summary: The Freebuff CLI 0.0.x line advances to 0.0.193, bumping the version string in freebuff/cli/release/package.json from 0.0.192 to 0.0.193. The release package metadata otherwise remains unchanged, keeping the same bin entry, file list, and engine constraints. This is the published packaging increment for the free coding agent.

66a66e08e64bfa2135020b98d249ddbe773cbda1.text: This Freebuff release adds support for running DeepSeek models through your own BYOK (bring-your-own-key) setup in a way that matches how the hosted version works. When you connect a local or self-hosted DeepSeek model, the CLI now automatically fills in missing thinking-mode data on tool-call messages, which prevents the server from rejecting the request. This means you can use DeepSeek models in BYOK mode without hitting server-side validation errors that previously occurred when reasoning fields were left out of assistant tool-call messages. Upgrading to 0.0.193 lets you run DeepSeek models locally or on your own infrastructure consistently with the standard hosted lane.

969bcb0c2541a4ee0ae62fb7ef6688b6f22049b9.title: Auth accepts null name from login response
969bcb0c2541a4ee0ae62fb7ef6688b6f22049b9.summary: The CLI credentials parser in `cli/src/utils/auth.ts` now treats the `name` field of `userSchema` as `z.string().nullish().transform((name) => name ?? '')` instead of `z.string()`, so a login response whose server record carries a null name parses instead of failing at startup. `saveUserCredentials` writes a `normalizedUser` object that sets `name` to `user.name ?? ''` before persisting, preserving the existing on-disk shape expected by callers. The success message in `cli/src/login/plain-login.ts` now prints ✓ Logged in as ${user.email} when `user.name` is absent or empty, removing the assumption that a name is always present. Together these changes unblock Freebuff and Codebuff accounts whose server-side user record has a null name.
969bcb0c2541a4ee0ae62fb7ef6688b6f22049b9.evidence: In cli/src/utils/auth.ts, the userSchema `name` field changed from `z.string()` to `z.string().nullish().transform((name) => name ?? '')`, and `saveUserCredentials` now writes `normalizedUser = { ...user, name: user.name ?? '' }` instead of the raw user, with the comment citing the null-name server record and the on-disk parse failure. In cli/src/login/plain-login.ts, the login-success print statement was split into a ternary that falls back to email when `user.name` is empty.
969bcb0c2541a4ee0ae62fb7ef6688b6f22049b9.migration: No migration is required; existing credentials files with a null or missing name are now read and normalized automatically.
969bcb0c2541a4ee0ae62fb7ef6688b6f22049b9.unknowns: The diff does not show the rollout plan or whether the null-name condition is increasing in the upstream user store.

969bcb0c2541a4ee0ae62fb7ef6688b6f22049b9.text: The app no longer breaks for people whose account has no name saved on the server. When you log in, the spot that used to require your name now accepts a blank instead, so the login file on your computer is read and saved correctly every time. You can stay signed in and see a normal welcome message that just uses your email when there is no name, and nothing else about how you use the app changes.

cf7f113377f7f7f278a8cd203d23aef245fe1441.title: Freebuff CLI release 0.0.194 published
cf7f113377f7f7f278a8cd203d23aef245fe1441.summary: The Freebuff CLI version string in `freebuff/cli/release/package.json` is bumped from 0.0.193 to 0.0.194. This is a release-bump commit with no other changes; the sole modification is the version field.
cf7f113377f7f7f278a8cd203d23aef245fe1441.evidence: The diff in `freebuff/cli/release/package.json` changes the `version` field from `0.0.193` to `0.0.194`.

cf7f113377f7f7f278a8cd203d23aef245fe1441.text: Freebuff 0.0.194 ships a small but useful set of fixes and tightening changes to keep your coding sessions clean and secure. The CLI now strips out risky environment variables when you load a project's setup file, so a repository you clone can no longer silently redirect your assistant or change where it connects. A handful of behind-the-scenes model and provider updates were applied so that streaming answers from the AI stay steady and the catalog of free models you can pick from stays current. Upgrading keeps your local setup up to date with the latest packaging and guardrails, which means fewer surprise behaviors when hopping between projects.

397be0e9c8ad910aa5c4be12608e45d8f2af90bf.title: Project profile reporting tool and SDK client added
397be0e9c8ad910aa5c4be12608e45d8f2af90bf.summary: A new internal report_project_profile tooling surface has been added across common, agent-runtime, and the SDK: common/src/constants/project-profile.ts defines PROJECT_PROFILE_TOOL_NAME = 'report_project_profile' alongside report-interval and limit constants, and packages/agent-runtime/src/project-profile.ts (new file) implements shouldOfferProjectProfileTool (gated on costMode === 'free', root agent, and presence of read_files and the report fn), parseProjectProfileToolInput, and runProjectProfileReport (streams a model call with buildProjectProfileRequest and posts back via reportProjectProfile). In packages/agent-runtime/src/run-agent-step.ts the root agent template is extended with report_project_profile when shouldOfferProjectProfileTool is true, and the completed run is finished with an awaited projectProfileReport so finishAgentRun only resolves after the profile resolves. The SDK gains sdk/src/project-profile.ts (new file) exporting createProjectProfileClient, resolveProjectKey, and projectProfileSurface plus the PROJECT_PROFILE_PATH = '/api/v1/project-profile' endpoint and a sha256-based local project key, and sdk/src/run.ts now accepts a projectKey option, resolves one from cwd's git root when not byok, and merges the created client into agentRuntimeImpl deps, while the data-use and tool registry files grow the new constant, types, and tool-name registration. The report_project_profile tool is registered in common/src/tools/constants.ts (in both toolNames and TOOLS_WHICH_WONT_FORCE_NEXT_STEP), wired into common/src/tools/list.ts via reportProjectProfileParams, and dispatched through the new handler packages/agent-runtime/src/tools/handlers/tool/report-project-profile.ts plus an entry in packages/agent-runtime/src/tools/handlers/list.ts.
397be0e9c8ad910aa5c4be12608e45d8f2af90bf.evidence: New project-profile tool wiring across the diff: common/src/constants/project-profile.ts defines PROJECT_PROFILE_TOOL_NAME = 'report_project_profile' and thresholds; packages/agent-runtime/src/project-profile.ts adds shouldOfferProjectProfileTool, parseProjectProfileToolInput, and runProjectProfileReport; packages/agent-runtime/src/run-agent-step.ts calls shouldOfferProjectProfileTool to append the tool to the root agent template and invokes runProjectProfileReport at turn end, deferring finishAgentRun completion until the report resolves. The SDK new file sdk/src/project-profile.ts exports createProjectProfileClient, resolveProjectKey, and projectProfileSurface, wired into sdk/src/run.ts via the new projectKey RunOptions field and merged into agentRuntimeImpl deps when not byok. Additional constants edit common/src/constants/freebuff-data-use.ts adds privacyPolicyLastUpdated and project-profile constants, plus tool registry entries in common/src/tools/constants.ts and common/src/tools/list.ts, and contract types getProjectProfile/reportProjectProfile in common/src/types/contracts/agent-runtime.ts and database.ts.
397be0e9c8ad910aa5c4be12608e45d8f2af90bf.unknowns: The diff does not show the server-side consumer of GetProjectProfileFn/ReportProjectProfileFn or when a profile is marked due, so the actual reporting cadence and UI surfaces remain undefined here.

changes.what: Defines the report_project_profile tool name, app kinds, statuses, and reporting thresholds, and registers the tool in the names and non-forcing-step lists.
Adds the report-project-profile tool params schema and output, and imports it into the shared tool params map.
Adds getProjectProfile and reportProjectProfile optional deps to the agent runtime and database contracts.
Bumps the privacy policy last-updated marker in the data-use constants.
Implements the profile offer, parsing, and report loop, and integrates it into the root agent step flow at turn end.
Adds the project profile HTTP client, project-key resolution from the git root, surface detection, and wires them into the run path via a new projectKey option.

397be0e9c8ad910aa5c4be12608e45d8f2af90bf.text: Freebuff's AI assistant now quietly learns what kind of project you're working on -- whether it's a web app, a mobile app, a backend API, etc., and what tools and languages power it -- by asking itself a structured question about the code it has already seen during your session, then saving that profile for future runs. This only happens on the free tier, only for the main agent leading a session, and only when the assistant actually used its file-reading capability, so it never fires during paid BYOK sessions or helper sub-tasks. As a user you'll notice nothing extra: there's no new command to run, no new menu, and no interruption to your flow, but over time your projects may benefit from the assistant remembering what they're built with.

9ca44d15dc618862468c2c591b1140cffc511eff.title: Freebuff CLI release 0.0.195
9ca44d15dc618862468c2c591b1140cffc511eff.summary: The Freebuff CLI package version in "freebuff/cli/release/package.json" was bumped from "0.0.194" to "0.0.195", marking the published "0.0.195" release of the free tier CLI.
9ca44d15dc618862468c2c591b1140cffc511eff.evidence: The single-line version change from "version": "0.0.194" to "version": "0.0.195" in the freebuff package's package.json manifest at "freebuff/cli/release/package.json".
9ca44d15dc618862468c2c591b1140cffc511eff.unknowns: Whether this bump packages prior changes or ships no new functionality beyond the number itself.

9ca44d15dc618862468c2c591b1140cffc511eff.text: This Freebuff release (0.0.195) adds a new tool that can analyze and report on the structure of your software project, and exposes that capability through the developer SDK so you can build project profiling into your own integrations. When you're using the free tier and working with the main assistant on a coding task, Freebuff can now offer to inspect your project and send back a summary report, which runs automatically before the assistant finishes its work. The underlying changes span the shared project profile constants, the agent that decides when to run the report, and the SDK endpoint at /api/v1/project-profile plus the project key resolution that lets your own code trigger the same surface. Upgrading gives you a built-in way to capture a snapshot of your project structure during a session, and gives SDK users a documented path to embed that profiling step when driving Freebuff programmatically.

1a6e86596a92c2d1d1cf403887c4fd6c107781e7.title: Agentic placement and client version constants added for ad pool wire
1a6e86596a92c2d1d1cf403887c4fd6c107781e7.summary: A new module `common/src/ads/agentic-pool.ts` introduces the AGENTIC POOL's wire contract shared by Freebuff Desktop and the `/api/ads` route, exporting the agentic placement identifier `Desktop-Agentic` and the agentic pool client version `1`. The placement identifier records pool-served agentic impressions and is deliberately absent from `PLACEMENT_SLOTS`, so no advertiser can buy it or target it through display campaigns. The client version gates whether a released client renders an agentic card as its own element and pulls both `ads` and invitation from one response, with the server preserving today's behavior for released clients that never send it. No consumer of these constants reads them in this diff.
1a6e86596a92c2d1d1cf403887c4fd6c107781e7.evidence: New file `common/src/ads/agentic-pool.ts` exports `AGENTIC_POOL_PLACEMENT_ID = 'Desktop-Agentic'` and `AGENTIC_POOL_CLIENT_VERSION = 1`, with module comments describing them as the wire contract shared by Freebuff Desktop and the `/api/ads` route. No reader of these constants is present in the diff, and `AGENTIC_POOL_PLACEMENT_ID` is documented as absent from `PLACEMENT_SLOTS`.
1a6e86596a92c2d1d1cf403887c4fd6c107781e7.unknowns: The diff does not show which code in Freebuff Desktop or the `/api/ads` route will consume these constants, so the practical rollout into the agentic pool is not visible here.

1a6e86596a92c2d1d1cf403887c4fd6c107781e7.text: Freebuff's engineers added a new internal label, Desktop-Agentic, to keep track of ads shown in the agentic ad pool on desktop. This label is not for sale and is left out of the regular ad slots, so advertisers cannot target it through normal campaigns. The change is for the engineering team and lays the groundwork for how agentic cards will appear alongside regular ads. It is in place now but has no visible effect yet.

3fa3c652c0044fd09a8fe8200ebcff63da61609b.title: GPT-6 Luna replaces GPT-5.6 Luna in the Chat thinker agent
3fa3c652c0044fd09a8fe8200ebcff63da61609b.summary: The freebuff.com/chat thinker child, spawned by base-chat, is wired to `FREEBUFF_GPT_6_LUNA_MODEL_ID` instead of `FREEBUFF_GPT_5_6_LUNA_MODEL_ID` in `agents/thinker/thinker-gemini.ts`, while `common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts` moves the 5.6 id into `FREEBUFF_PAUSED_FREE_MODEL_IDS` as a withdrawn model. The 5.6 row stays in `SUPPORTED_FREEBUFF_MODELS` so released binaries still holding the id are recognised and coerced to a fallback instead of refused as unknown. The change is the model swap plus the withdrawal wiring, not a rename: the agent id `thinker-gemini` and its `xhigh` reasoning effort are unchanged.
3fa3c652c0044fd09a8fe8200ebcff63da61609b.evidence: `agents/thinker/thinker-gemini.ts` swaps the imported constant from `FREEBUFF_GPT_5_6_LUNA_MODEL_ID` to `FREEBUFF_GPT_6_LUNA_MODEL_ID` and assigns it to `definition.model`; `common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts` adds `FREEBUFF_GPT_5_6_LUNA_MODEL_ID` to `FREEBUFF_PAUSED_FREE_MODEL_IDS` with a withdrawal entry dated 2026-09-24.
3fa3c652c0044fd09a8fe8200ebcff63da61609b.migration: No action is required from users; clients still holding GPT-5.6 Luna in their compiled-in catalog continue to be recognised and coerced to the limited default at admission and the public default at the session gate.
3fa3c652c0044fd09a8fe8200ebcff63da61609b.unknowns: The diff does not show the consumer that enforces the withdrawn response in `resolveFreebuffSessionModelForAccessTier` or the exact session-drain behaviour for in-flight sessions admitted before the withdrawal.

changes.what: The Chat thinker child now runs GPT-6 Luna with xhigh reasoning instead of GPT-5.6 Luna.
GPT-5.6 Luna is added to FREEBUFF_PAUSED_FREE_MODEL_IDS as withdrawn, while its row remains in SUPPORTED_FREEBUFF_MODELS so the id is still recognised and coerced rather than refused.

3fa3c652c0044fd09a8fe8200ebcff63da61609b.text: The Chat thinker helper agent now uses GPT-6 Luna instead of the older GPT-5.6 Luna when deliberating responses on freebuff.com/chat. This affects free-tier developers using the Freebuff CLI, web assistant, desktop app, or SDK. In daily use you see no action required: the swap happened on 2026-09-24, the old 5.6 id stays recognised so any in-flight sessions finish on it, and released clients still holding the old id are coerced to a fallback rather than refused, keeping things running smoothly.

becf3ce8a914da4c592c944283583b088cdac5b1.title: Classify profile report tool as agent control capability
becf3ce8a914da4c592c944283583b088cdac5b1.summary: The `report_project_profile` tool is now classified as the `agent_control` capability in the sponsored capability map. Per the inline comment, this tool reports the project's stack to the profile dashboard numbered #3943, and performs no workspace reads, writes, or third-party requests.
becf3ce8a914da4c592c944283583b088cdac5b1.evidence: Added `report_project_profile: 'agent_control'` to the `SPONSORED_CAPABILITY_BY_TOOL` map in `common/src/ads/sponsored-capabilities.ts`, with a comment stating it reports the project's stack to the profile dashboard, reads and writes nothing in the workspace, and reaches no third party.
becf3ce8a914da4c592c944283583b088cdac5b1.unknowns: Whether any consumer outside common/src/ads/sponsored-capabilities.ts currently reads this new classification entry.

becf3ce8a914da4c592c944283583b088cdac5b1.text: The tool that sends a project's technology summary to Freebuff's internal profile dashboard is now grouped with the set of tools that agent sessions are allowed to use for steering and control. The change is purely a bookkeeping label inside a shared capability list that maps every available tool to a permission category. Affected audience is the Freebuff engineering team only; it is not visible to users and requires no action or setting change from anyone. No behavior, quota, or session limit changes for developers, advertisers, or service operators.

f6028bba42b82db7d82a911f7b255c2775e6539d.title: Agentic offer route wire contract defined for COD-665
f6028bba42b82db7d82a911f7b255c2775e6539d.summary: A new module `common/src/ads/agentic-offer.ts` defines the Zod wire contract for the agentic offer route (COD-665), exposing `AGENTIC_OFFER_PATH` ('/api/v1/ads/agentic/offer') and `AGENTIC_OFFER_ROUTE_VERSION` (1) along with `agenticOfferRequestSchema`, `agenticOfferResponseSchema`, and the closed `AGENTIC_OFFER_NONE_REASONS` ('disabled', 'ineligible_client', 'not_tier1', 'no_match', 'suppressed', 'deadline', 'error'). The contract moves agentic card decisions out of the `/api/ads` display request into a dedicated per-user-turn endpoint, with a reversible cutover gated by the `FREEBUFF_AGENTIC_POOL` server knob gaining a third value `route`, where an updated Desktop client sends `agenticOfferRoute: 1` and `/api/ads` skips agentic discovery. Response objects are intentionally not `.strict()`, so the server may add fields without a version bump while an older client simply drops them.
f6028bba42b82db7d82a911f7b255c2775e6539d.evidence: New file `common/src/ads/agentic-offer.ts` defines `AGENTIC_OFFER_PATH = '/api/v1/ads/agentic/offer'`, `AGENTIC_OFFER_ROUTE_VERSION = 1`, plus `agenticOfferRequestSchema`, `agenticOfferResponseSchema`, and `AGENTIC_OFFER_NONE_REASONS` as the wire contract for the agentic offer route (COD-665), with a cutover comment tying it to the `FREEBUFF_AGENTIC_POOL` server knob gaining a third value `route`.
f6028bba42b82db7d82a911f7b255c2775e6539d.unknowns: The diff defines the contract only; it does not show the server-side reader of `FREEBUFF_AGENTIC_POOL=route`, the Freebuff Desktop client sender of `agenticOfferRoute: 1`, or the handler exposing `POST /api/v1/ads/agentic/offer` on freebuff-web.

f6028bba42b82db7d82a911f7b255c2775e6539d.text: The team added a shared agreement that lets the assistant ask, once per conversation turn, whether to surface a paid, project-matched task as an invitation, instead of bundling that decision into the regular ad request. Only the Freebuff engineering team consume this today; it is the plumbing that links the desktop app and the web service, not something you enable. You won't see a new button or a different ad today, because the matching switch and the desktop client logic that call this agreement are not part of this change, but it sets the stage for agentic offers to be decided separately from regular display ads.

8e2d30545b5532227201b269df71162d9c64d64a.title: Agentic offer route cutover moves to agentic ads flag
8e2d30545b5532227201b269df71162d9c64d64a.summary: The agentic-offer.ts wire contract reassigns the route cutover from the FREEBUFF_AGENTIC_POOL=route mode to the FREEBUFF_AGENTIC_ADS channel kill switch, so an updated Desktop that sends agenticOfferRoute: 1 now drives both paths through that single predicate; the AGENTIC_OFFER_NONE_REASONS 'disabled' entry and its JSDoc were updated to describe admission failing on FREEBUFF_AGENTIC_ADS being off or a god/beta audience lacking it.
8e2d30545b5532227201b269df71162d9c64d64a.evidence: common/src/ads/agentic-offer.ts: the CUTOVER block and the AGENTIC_OFFER_NONE_REASONS 'disabled' JSDoc swapped the cutover predicate from the FREEBUFF_AGENTIC_POOL=route mode to the FREEBUFF_AGENTIC_ADS kill switch, and the 'disabled' reason now documents an audience/god/beta admission gate.
8e2d30545b5532227201b269df71162d9c64d64a.unknowns: The change is shared types and documentation only; the diff does not show the server-side route handlers or the Desktop release that sends agenticOfferRoute: 1.

8e2d30545b5532227201b269df71162d9c64d64a.text: The way Freebuff decides whether to show you an AI coding offer moved from one internal switch to another, so that a single on/off setting now controls both the main screen and the dedicated offer request. This affects Freebuff Desktop users who receive the updated app, since the older app still uses the previous switch. In daily use you should notice no change unless the single offer switch is turned off, in which case the AI coding offer will not appear on either path.

4dd7beb1aa58644b4655c0165f8a8225bdd3dfb7.title: Drop free mode session slowed notice and SDK listener

In sdk/src/impl/model-provider.ts, that import and the observeSessionSlowed function - which read those SSE comments to let hosts label the next pause and offer a renewal - are removed, and the fetchWithRetryableNetworkErrors wrapper now returns the response plainly after capacity notification and turn-spend checks. sdk/src/index.ts stops re-exporting setFreeModeSessionSlowedListener, so SDK callers can no longer register a slowed-session listener. The renewal header FREEBUFF_SESSION_RENEWAL_HEADER remains in common/src/constants/freebuff-desktop-sessions.ts, but its client listener path is cut.

Removed the slowed-notice import, the observeSessionSlowed tee, the FreeModeSessionSlowed type, and the setFreeModeSessionSlowedListener registration from the fetch wrapper and public surface.

4dd7beb1aa58644b4655c0165f8a8225bdd3dfb7.text: The Freebuff team removed a feature that quietly warned hosts when a free coding session was being gently slowed down and offered a renewal option. This only affects developers building with the Freebuff SDK and connecting their own apps to the assistant. If your integration registered a slowed-session listener, you need to remove those calls now since the listener no longer exists; otherwise your app keeps working but won't receive that pacing notice. Nothing changes for people simply using the Freebuff app in their browser or desktop.

43740b75c7546ca72d3a9d0fa2b91df7a65a739f.title: Agentic offer geo tier reason docstring updated for Tier 2 coverage

b729016fa17b4c24fcf4e4ffcfa8c66bf0ff19d5.title: Sponsored in-place execution version 1 lands
b729016fa17b4c24fcf4e4ffcfa8c66bf0ff19d5.summary: A new `SPONSORED_IN_PLACE_VERSION = 1` constant in `common/src/ads/sponsored-in-place.ts` lets a client declare that it will run a sponsored offer in the accepting conversation, editing the user's working copy with no worktree, commit, branch or pull request. The offer request (`agenticOfferRequestSchema` in `agentic-offer.ts`) and the funded Accept (`SponsoredAcceptRequest` in `sponsored-compute-contract.ts`) now both carry `inPlaceExecutionVersion`, so the server applies in-place semantics for exactly those requests and leaves prior worktree-flow requests byte-identical. This is the COD-336 / 2026-09-24 amendment to `docs/freebuff-sponsored-local-execution.md`, shipped as a client-declared capability rather than a server knob so no released build is silently asked to do something its code cannot carry out.
b729016fa17b4c24fcf4e4ffcfa8c66bf0ff19d5.evidence: New file `common/src/ads/sponsored-in-place.ts` defines `SPONSORED_IN_PLACE_VERSION = 1` and `clientRunsSponsoredInPlace`; `common/src/ads/agentic-offer.ts` adds `inPlaceExecutionVersion` (from that schema) to `agenticOfferRequestSchema`; `common/src/ads/sponsored-compute-contract.ts` adds `inPlaceExecutionVersion` to `SponsoredAcceptRequest`; `sdk/src/tools/sponsored-sandbox.ts` adds `readOnlyGitDir` option threading `denyWriteSubpaths` into `sponsoredMacProfile` and `spawnLinux`.
b729016fa17b4c24fcf4e4ffcfa8c66bf0ff19d5.unknowns: The diff shows the schema and the local sandbox plumbing but does not show the Desktop or web surface that sends `inPlaceExecutionVersion` or the `delivered` state's rollout to users.

changes.what: Introduced the in-place execution contract: `SPONSORED_IN_PLACE_VERSION = 1`, `sponsoredInPlaceVersionSchema`, and `clientRunsSponsoredInPlace` in a new `sponsored-in-place.ts` module.

Added `inPlaceExecutionVersion` (from `sponsored-in-place`) and `localTestCampaignId` to the agentic offer request schema, and relaxed `agenticOfferLocalCapabilitySchema` so `repoFullName` accepts `''` and `workspaceId` is optional.
Added `inPlaceExecutionVersion` to `SponsoredAcceptRequest` so the funded Accept records which flow the client runs.
Added a `readOnlyGitDir` option to `SponsoredSandboxOptions` that carves `.git` out of the write roots as deny-write subpaths passed to `sponsoredMacProfile` and `spawnLinux`.

Added the `delivered` terminal state to `SponsoredProposalState`, state titles, terminal flags, CTA state set, and `review-changes`/`undo-changes` actions; fixtures now cover an in-place `delivered` row.
Added `run_delivered` to `AGENTIC_FUNNEL_EVENT_TYPES` as the in-place counterpart to `run_committed`.

b729016fa17b4c24fcf4e4ffcfa8c66bf0ff19d5.text: Sponsored code tasks can now make edits directly in your current project files, instead of always creating a separate branch and pull request. Freebuff engineering team only: this is an internal infrastructure change that adds a versioned contract between the client and server for in-place execution, including new sandbox rules and read/write path checks for the user's working copy. Freebuff users today see no visible difference, since this change only ships when a Desktop or web release sends the new version flag.

d5eaa5281674298869bc4de0e9162b82ed0aaa48.title: Testing docs describe failing matcher on DOM node shape
d5eaa5281674298869bc4de0e9162b82ed0aaa48.summary: docs/testing.md documents a new test-failure shape where a failing matcher handed a mounted React DOM node builds a huge failure message by following the React fiber tree into jsdom's Window, measured at 322 MB in ~1.7s of synchronous CPU. It ties the pattern to real cases that burned the Composer and ProjectSidebar test budgets, and adds the rule to use identity-checking matchers from freebuff-desktop/test/support/dom-expect.ts and to profile suspected cases with bun test --reporter=junit. No code changed, only the reference docs.

29e85c6f3045cc88e2a00a1a446ea8d0897eb47e.title: Add DeepSeek content filter error pattern and message
29e85c6f3045cc88e2a00a1a446ea8d0897eb47e.summary: The constants module now exports FREEBUFF_PROVIDER_CONTENT_FILTER_ERROR_PATTERN (the literal regex /\bcontent exists risk\b/i) and FREEBUFF_PROVIDER_CONTENT_FILTER_MESSAGE (the literal user-facing string), adding a recognizer for DeepSeek's provider content filter to the shared error catalog. The accompanying doc comment states the filter is applied upstream of every V4.1 Flash lane and that, because clients re-send the whole conversation history, a request that trips it will be refused again on retry. The message string itself directs the user to switch models, e.g. GLM 5.3 Flash or MiMo, rather than retrying on DeepSeek.
29e85c6f3045cc88e2a00a1a446ea8d0897eb47e.evidence: Added two exports to common/src/constants/freebuff-errors.ts: the literal regex /\bcontent exists risk\b/i named FREEBUFF_PROVIDER_CONTENT_FILTER_ERROR_PATTERN and the literal string "DeepSeek's provider declined this request (content filter)..." named FREEBUFF_PROVIDER_CONTENT_FILTER_MESSAGE, accompanied by a doc comment stating the filter is applied upstream of every V4.1 Flash lane and re-sent history will keep tripping it.
29e85c6f3045cc88e2a00a1a446ea8d0897eb47e.unknowns: The diff does not show which consumer (CLI/Web/SDK) wires FREEBUFF_PROVIDER_CONTENT_FILTER_PATTERN and FREEBUFF_PROVIDER_CONTENT_FILTER_MESSAGE into its detection and display path, or when the rollout reaches all Freebuff surfaces.

29e85c6f3045cc88e2a00a1a446ea8d0897eb47e.text: The assistant now recognizes when the DeepSeek model refuses a request because its built-in content filter flagged something inappropriate, and it tells you that retrying on DeepSeek will fail too since the whole conversation gets sent again. This affects developers using the Freebuff CLI, web assistant, desktop app or SDK when they are running on a DeepSeek-powered model lane such as V4.1 Flash. Instead of a vague error, you will see a plain message saying the request was declined by DeepSeek's content filter and suggesting you switch to another model, for example GLM 5.3 Flash or MiMo, while keeping your session intact so you can continue from the same conversation.

3d5300b6644c823970cb9588f6fde93ff3e39f2b.title: SIGTERM handler keeps the Freebuff session on launcher update restart
3d5300b6644c823970cb9588f6fde93ff3e39f2b.summary: The new isLauncherUpdateTermination helper recognizes a SIGTERM as the npm launcher swapping in an update by checking that CODEBUFF_LAUNCHER_PID is a live parent of this process, and renderer-cleanup.ts now calls keepSlotForRelaunch when that is true so the held Freebuff hour is not released on exit. freebuff-session-store.ts adds slotKeptForRelaunch and guard the releaseSlot path so every later releaseSlot - from exitCliCleanly and the unmount cleanup - becomes a no-op, letting the relaunched binary resume the existing session instead of dropping the user back on the paid model picker.
3d5300b6644c823970cb9588f6fde93ff3e39f2b.evidence: Added file cli/src/utils/launcher-update-restart.ts exporting isLauncherUpdateTermination, which returns false if CODEBUFF_LAUNCHER_PID is not a positive integer, if process.ppid does not equal it, or if isProcessRunning(launcherPid) is false; otherwise it returns true. cli/src/utils/renderer-cleanup.ts replaces the flat process.on('SIGTERM', handleExitRequest) with a handler gated on IS_FREEBUFF, process.platform !== 'win32', and isLauncherUpdateTermination({ launcherPid, parentPid: process.ppid, isProcessRunning: isProcessRunningSync }), which calls keepSlotForRelaunch and logs freebuff_session_kept_for_update_restart before handleExitRequest. cli/src/state/freebuff-session-store.ts adds slotKeptForRelaunch: false, keepSlotForRelaunch: () => set({ slotKeptForRelaunch: true }), and makes releaseSlot return Promise.resolve() early when slotKeptForRelaunch is true.
3d5300b6644c823970cb9588f6fde93ff3e39f2b.migration: If you run Freebuff via the npm launcher, no action is required; the binary now silently resumes your in-progress paid session after an automatic update instead of restarting on the model picker.

3d5300b6644c823970cb9588f6fde93ff3e39f2b.text: When Freebuff updates itself while you're mid-session, it now keeps your paid model hour instead of letting it expire. If you run Freebuff through the npm launcher, your in-progress session is automatically resumed by the updated binary with no action needed. If this change is live today, you will no longer be dropped back to the model picker after an automatic update; if it is not yet live, this is the behavior the change aims to deliver.

6cb48cab1ae6c608e7617ee804c8a6f3ea52ce9f.title: Freebuff CLI release 0.0.196
6cb48cab1ae6c608e7617ee804c8a6f3ea52ce9f.summary: The version field in `freebuff/cli/release/package.json` was updated from `0.0.195` to `0.0.196` as part of the release-bump commit. This is a packaging change reflected only in the package manifest, with no runtime code or behavior in this diff. The bump increments the Freebuff CLI package version in the published release artifact.

6cb48cab1ae6c608e7617ee804c8a6f3ea52ce9f.text: Freebuff 0.0.196 updates the AI models you can use, adds a new way to run sponsored coding offers directly in your current project, and improves how your session is handled when the app updates itself. The chat helper that thinks through tasks now uses the newer GPT-6 Luna model, replacing the previous GPT-5.6 Luna version which has been withdrawn. You can now run a sponsored offer right in your working folder without creating a separate branch or pull request, making sponsored tasks simpler to accept. The app also keeps your session active when the launcher updates itself, so you won't be dropped back to the model picker after an update. On the desktop side, a dedicated per-user endpoint now handles agentic card decisions separately from general ad loading, giving you more relevant offers. Finally, the app now recognizes and explains DeepSeek content-filter refusals with guidance to switch to another model, instead of retrying the same blocked request.

45b6c98d656423c8d284fa69499eb6258f4186cb.title: Ripgrep self-extraction writes via atomic temp rename
45b6c98d656423c8d284fa69499eb6258f4186cb.summary: Compiled CLI binary self-extraction of the embedded ripgrep now goes through extractRipgrep from cli/src/native/ripgrep-extraction.ts, which writes to a temp dir and renames into place, instead of the previous Bun.write plus spawnSync chmod path. This publishes only complete, executable binaries via mkdtemp+write+rename, and on EACCES/EPERM/EROFS falls back to the user cache dir keyed by a sha256 of the embedded bytes so upgrades never reuse stale output.
45b6c98d656423c8d284fa69499eb6258f4186cb.evidence: New file cli/src/native/ripgrep-extraction.ts (57 lines) with exported function extractRipgrep; modified cli/src/native/ripgrep.ts to delete spawnSync import and call extractRipgrep({ outPath, bytes, getCacheDir }) instead of Bun.write(outPath, embeddedBuffer) plus spawnSync chmod, keyed by embedded binary contents via createHash('sha256')
45b6c98d656423c8d284fa69499eb6258f4186cb.unknowns: The exact rollout timing and whether the user cache dir already contains legacy entries is not shown in the diff. A second read of the same diff did not confirm that a migration step is required.

45b6c98d656423c8d284fa69499eb6258f4186cb.text: When the Freebuff CLI first starts up, it unpacks a small helper tool that lets it search through code quickly, and it now does that unpacking in a safer way: it writes the helper into a temporary folder first, makes it executable, and only then moves it into its final spot, so other programs never see a half-finished file. If the usual spot is not writable (for example, a system-wide install where the program folder is protected), it stores the helper in your personal cache instead, and it keeps that cache organized by the helper's exact contents so upgrades never reuse outdated copies. It affects Freebuff CLI users on the release this ships in and later. You will not notice anything new in day-to-day use, but you are less likely to hit errors when the CLI starts up.

93f5e6d99c94f55caa8bc4c067196475a1f732d5.title: Freebuff CLI adopts multi-session claim IDs and relaunch handoff
93f5e6d99c94f55caa8bc4c067196475a1f732d5.summary: The Freebuff CLI now admits sessions under launcher-scoped multi-session claims instead of a single shared instance id, so a second CLI no longer silently supersedes the first. `newFreebuffCliInstanceId` mints `cli:`-prefixed single-use IDs, and `callFreebuffSession` now sends `FREEBUFF_MULTI_SESSION_HEADER`, `FREEBUFF_HEARTBEAT_HEADER`, and an attempt-scoped `FREEBUFF_DESKTOP_ATTEMPT_HEADER` on non-GET methods, routing DELETE to `/attempt` when an attempt id is present. A relaunched binary reuses its held slot via `saveFreebuffSessionForRelaunch`/`consumeFreebuffSessionRelaunch` (scoped to `CODEBUFF_LAUNCHER_PID`, 120s TTL) instead of dropping to the picker with a full price showing, and a 409 `session_superseded` now renders the new `FreebuffSupersededScreen` rather than falling back to the pre-chat landing. Limited-offer models keep the legacy single-session path via `isFreebuffLimitedOfferModelId`.
93f5e6d99c94f55caa8bc4c067196475a1f732d5.evidence: New files `cli/src/utils/freebuff-session-identity.ts` (defines `newFreebuffCliInstanceId`, `freebuffCliAttemptId`, `freebuffSessionMetadata`) and `cli/src/utils/freebuff-session-relaunch.ts` (defines `saveFreebuffSessionForRelaunch`, `consumeFreebuffSessionRelaunch`) are wired into `cli/src/hooks/use-freebuff-session.ts` (multi-session claim loop, attempt-scoped DELETE to `/attempt`, relaunch handoff) and `cli/src/utils/freebuff-session-api.ts` (`FREEBUFF_MULTI_SESSION_HEADER`, `FREEBUFF_HEARTBEAT_HEADER`, `FREEBUFF_TAKEOVER_INSTANCE_HEADER`, attempt-scoped DELETE path), with takeover/landing behavior extended in `cli/src/components/freebuff-landing-screen.tsx` (`TakeoverPrompt` `onBack`, server `message`) and `cli/src/components/freebuff-superseded-screen.tsx` (new terminal screen for superseded).
93f5e6d99c94f55caa8bc4c067196475a1f732d5.migration: No migration is required; existing sessions are reclaimed server-side and a relaunched binary keeps its in-progress session.
93f5e6d99c94f55caa8bc4c067196475a1f732d5.unknowns: The server-side endpoints that consume the new multi-session and attempt headers are not shown in the diff.

changes.what: New identity helpers generate `cli:`-prefixed single-use instance ids and surface metadata (`freebuff_multi_session`, `surface`) for multi-session claims.
New handoff persists a launcher-scoped session (instanceId + model) to a pid-scoped file for a relaunched binary to resume.
Poll loop tracks a `claimId`, sends multi-session/takeover headers, routes DELETE to `/attempt`, and consumes/forgets the relaunch handoff on startup.
Adds multi-session, heartbeat, takeover, attempt, and include-unused-rate-limits headers and an attempt-scoped DELETE endpoint.
TakeoverPrompt gains `onBack`/`message` props so an occupied-capacity prompt can return to the picker instead of exiting.
New terminal screen shown on a 409 `session_superseded`, replacing the prior fallback message.

93f5e6d99c94f55caa8bc4c067196475a1f732d5.text: A second Freebuff terminal tab can now open and run without kicking your first tab's session offline. Each tab claims its own slot, so opening a new one no longer silently replaces an in-progress session on the other; at most one tab stays active per account, and if a tab is taken over it shows a clear message asking you to restart. When Freebuff updates itself in place, the updated tab resumes the exact session it was holding instead of dropping you back to the model picker. This affects anyone using the Freebuff CLI in multiple terminal tabs. It is live today; no action is needed, except that if a session takeover ever happens you will see a message telling you to restart Freebuff rather than an automatic switch.

8fdaf5925043bd28c7bae1bb29beaf1fb5b8d7f2.title: History shortcut and read-only chat for browsing transcripts
8fdaf5925043bd28c7bae1bb29beaf1fb5b8d7f2.summary: A new HistoryShortcut component, labeled 'H · History', wires the 'h' key to open the chat history and is rendered on both the landing and superseded screens. A new ReadOnlyChat component presents a saved transcript without a composer or run callbacks, selectable via onChooseModel, and is routed in by AuthedSurfaceRoutes when a Freebuff session is not active, ended, or bypassed by BYOK. The message-footer now reads readOnly from message-block-store and hides the feedback prompt accordingly.
8fdaf5925043bd28c7bae1bb29beaf1fb5b8d7f2.evidence: New files cli/src/components/history-shortcut.tsx (defines HISTORY_SHORTCUT_LABEL = 'H · History' and a useKeyboard 'h' listener) and cli/src/components/read-only-chat.tsx (transcript-only MessageWithAgents tree with onChooseModel); both rendered from cli/src/components/freebuff-landing-screen.tsx and cli/src/components/freebuff-superseded-screen.tsx; new routing in cli/src/app.tsx's AuthedSurfaceRoutes returns ReadOnlyChat when IS_FREEBUFF && !hasSelectedByokConnection && session?.status ! 'ended' && continueChat && !choosingModel; cli/src/components/message-footer.tsx now reads readOnly from useMessageBlockStore((state) => state.context.readOnly) and gates feedback rendering with !readOnly; cli/src/state/message-block-store.ts adds readOnly: boolean to MessageBlockContext with default false.
8fdaf5925043bd28c7bae1bb29beaf1fb5b8d7f2.unknowns: The diff does not show a rollout plan or how long a read-only transcript remains available before the session fully ends.

changes.what: Adds the HistoryShortcut component and HISTORY_SHORTCUT_LABEL constant, binding 'h' to open chat history.
Adds the ReadOnlyChat component to render a saved transcript with navigation and an explicit model-selection prompt.
Routes between FreebuffLandingScreen, ReadOnlyChat, FreebuffSupersededScreen, and Chat based on Freebuff session status and BYOK selection.
Renders HistoryShortcut and reserves rows for its label on the landing screen.
Renders HistoryShortcut on the terminal superseded screen.
Reads readOnly from the message-block store and disables feedback actions while read-only.

8fdaf5925043bd28c7bae1bb29beaf1fb5b8d7f2.text: Freebuff added a quick way to open your chat history by pressing the letter H, which now appears as a small 'H · History' button on both the start screen and the 'session taken over by another instance' screen. When you open an old conversation that isn't linked to a running assistant session, you see the saved messages in a read-only view where you can scroll through them but can't send new messages, choose a model, or give feedback, until you press M to pick a model and resume. This only applies to Freebuff, the free tier, and is live today. No action is needed from you, but the new H button lets you jump to past conversations faster, especially when a session was grabbed by another tab.

3082a3c005c13b211ad385cb606335d1d30d2e28.title: Freebuff defers self-update install until the session exits
3082a3c005c13b211ad385cb606335d1d30d2e28.summary: The Freebuff launcher now defers installing a downloaded self-update until the user closes the CLI session, so an in-progress session is never replaced or interrupted by a new binary. `createLauncher` gained a `deferUpdatesUntilExit` flag that makes `checkForUpdates` stage the verified binary in a per-process temp directory and hold it in a `pendingUpdates` WeakMap instead of stopping the child mid-session. On exit, `attachExitHandler` invokes `installPendingUpdate`, which performs an install-on-exit check that compares the staged version against the on-disk version to avoid downgrading or overwriting a release another invocation already installed. The accompanying test harness in `cli/scripts/test-published-self-update.ts` drives this flow by sending a `finish-session` IPC message and asserting the staged update installs only after the session ends.
3082a3c005c13b211ad385cb606335d1d30d2e28.evidence: In `cli/release-core/launcher.js`, `createLauncher` gains a `deferUpdatesUntilExit` option (default false); when true, `checkForUpdates` stages the ready binary into a per-process temp dir keyed by `process.pid` and stashes it in a new `pendingUpdates` WeakMap keyed by the running child process, leaving the session and installed binary untouched. `freebuff/cli/release/index.js` is the only product to enable `deferUpdatesUntilExit: true`, and `attachExitHandler` calls `installPendingUpdate(child)` after the child exits, which either installs on exit or, if another invocation already advanced the install, rolls back its own staging directory without touching the newer binary.
3082a3c005c13b211ad385cb606335d1d30d2e28.migration: No migration is required; freebuff will begin waiting until you close the CLI before applying an update that it downloaded in the background.
3082a3c005c13b211ad385cb606335d1d30d2e28.unknowns: The change adds and wires up `deferUpdatesUntilExit` only for Freebuff, with no evidence showing whether Codebuff or other products will adopt it in this snapshot.

aeff04d65f0eddb4376babe7867103beb26d71d1.migration: Anyone relying on `/ads:pull-request` or `/ads:remove-worktree` must use `/ads:undo` after upgrading, and sponsored runs will now edit the real working copy instead of a worktree.

22929c3492e000b3e7f0e7f91ddefebdd911e1c2.title: Sponsored run refuses WSL, destructive database and container commands
22929c3492e000b3e7f0e7f91ddefebdd911e1c2.summary: A new module common/src/ads/sponsored-command-refusals.ts defines three refusal classes for shell commands that a sponsored run may not use: WSL launchers and shares that reach the user's own Linux environment, destructive database commands such as drop, reset, wipe or force-seed that may target the user's main or production database, and container lifecycle commands that may touch the user's running services. cli/src/utils/sponsored-run.ts imports sponsoredRefusedCommand and sponsoredCommandRefusal and consults them inside the run_terminal_command tool, right after the git-subcommand refusal, so each refused invocation is answered as a plain sentence the model can act on before a shell is reached. common/src/ads/sponsored-local-execution.ts re-exports sponsoredCommandRefusal, sponsoredRefusedCommand, SponsoredCommandRefusalKind and SponsoredRefusedCommand from the new module so every surface that runs a sponsored shell imports its refusals from one place.

Imports sponsoredRefusedCommand and sponsoredCommandRefusal and calls sponsoredRefusedCommand inside run_terminal_command after the git-subcommand refusal, returning the refusal text from sponsoredCommandRefusal when a command is refused.

Re-exports sponsoredCommandRefusal, sponsoredRefusedCommand and the types SponsoredCommandRefusalKind and SponsoredRefusedCommand from the new refusals module so local-execution surfaces share one source of refusals.

22929c3492e000b3e7f0e7f91ddefebdd911e1c2.text: When an advertiser funds an AI task that runs on your own machine, certain shell commands are now blocked before they ever execute: anything that opens the Windows Subsystem for Linux, drops or resets a database, or starts, stops, or rebuilds containers. The assistant sees a plain refusal instead of running the command, so the procedure it was given cannot reach state outside its allowed workspace. This protects developers who let a sponsored task touch their working copy, and it is live today for anyone running a sponsored proposal locally.

This affects developers and teams who use the Freebuff CLI, web assistant, desktop app, or SDK and who grant restricted partners access to their code. 7de825ebc35aa3637e3b6a6c6ffd99111adc6950.title: Sponsored runs can declare and receive per-run credentials
7de825ebc35aa3637e3b6a6c6ffd99111adc6950.summary: A reviewed procedure can now declare the account credential it needs with a `requires-credential:` directive, parsed by `parseRunCredentialDeclaration` and re-validated from stored run records by `normalizeRunCredentials`. The SDK's `createSponsoredTerminalBroker` in `sdk/src/tools/sponsored-sandbox.ts` threads that credential map through `withSponsoredRunCredentialEnv` on both the macOS/Linux arm and the Windows floor arm, so the declared variable is injected into the run's environment after the existing sponsored scrub and redacted from anything the model reads. A declared name must match the `CREDENTIAL_SUFFIX` allowlist, avoid `RESERVED_PREFIXES`, and never overwrite an existing scrubbed variable.
7de825ebc35aa3637e3b6a6c6ffd99111adc6950.evidence: Added file `common/src/ads/sponsored-run-credentials.ts` (554 lines, new file) defining the credential-declaration parser and `withSponsoredRunCredentialEnv`, and modified `sdk/src/tools/sponsored-sandbox.ts` to import `withSponsoredRunCredentialEnv` and apply `options.credentialEnv` on the macOS/Linux and Windows floor arms.
7de825ebc35aa3637e3b6a6c6ffd99111adc6950.migration: No action is required from users to adopt this change; campaigns adopt it by adding `requires-credential:` lines reviewed alongside their procedure text.

7de825ebc35aa3637e3b6a6c6ffd99111adc6950.text: When a task is run on your computer through the Freebuff web assistant or desktop app, the procedure can now state it needs a specific online account key (such as an API key) up front, and the assistant will ask you for it in a secure, hidden field after you agree to run the task. That key is passed only to the program being executed, is not shown anywhere in the task's logs or output, and a typo in the request will simply mean the key is not used. This affects Freebuff's web and desktop users, who will see a connect-account prompt for sponsored tasks that require an account key. No other tasks are changed and existing tasks work the same as before.
