06379878ff49e15244d63ec7360b85223d0e0f70.text: If you edit an older message in the middle of a conversation, the assistant can now forget everything after that point instead of either keeping stale history or wiping the whole chat clean. Freebuff Desktop used to erase the entire run state on any earlier edit, which made long threads restart from scratch; hosts that embed the assistant into their own app can now call the new SDK export to trim the stored transcript to the edited turn before resuming, so the next reply lines up with what the screen shows. The cut is based on how many user turns should survive, and if the stored history does not actually contain that many user messages yet, it safely returns nothing and lets the caller fall back to clearing state rather than guessing.

921b8dfb464d70e19cc035befb643702dbac931a.text: Freebuff's advertising-attribution system now hashes email addresses in one single, standardized way before sending them to Meta, TikTok, and X, instead of each platform using its own slightly different hashing logic. This is internal work that affects only Freebuff's engineers; it does not change any feature, quota, or experience you see when using the assistant. In daily use you will notice nothing different, and no action is required on your part.

fd93692e814f3a7a4a3e61773e10e58384120e64.text: This Freebuff release adds new AI models to choose from, makes it easier to manage long coding sessions, and sharpens how you're billed. MiMo 2.6 Flash replaces MiMo 2.5 in the free model picker, and a separate MiMo 2.6 Pro row is now available with its own 50-Freebucks entitlement, so the pricier model can't be run on the unmetered 10-Freebuck Flash session. You can now compact your conversation history on demand using the SDK compaction API, and the SDK can rewind a stored run state to the point of an edited user message, keeping your transcript aligned when you go back and change an earlier message. Billing clarity improves with prepaid annual subscription fields now modeled as a one-time annual checkout and a marked renewal date, and the off-peak price tooltip now states the discount is already included rather than implying an extra first-tab discount. On the safety side, the CLI now proves that dotenv files in a project cannot redirect your backend URL, so cloned repositories can't hijack where your assistant connects. If you hit a Freebucks wall, you can now start a /byok session directly without a live session, and the landing screen names the specific host it could not reach on network failures, pointing you to mobile data, another ISP, or the web interface instead of just blaming the client. Upgrading gets you these updated model options, clearer pay-once billing, safer repository loading, and more control over trimming and correcting long coding conversations.

d06f775277568095b3691deadd4f6458bcc0bde5.text: The team added three new AI models - two new versions of DeepSeek (V4.1 Flash and V4.1 Pro) and a new version of GLM 5.3 - plus two hidden test models, into the shared configuration that routes which AI model gets used for different tasks. These are provisioned-tier models, meaning they aren't publicly available in the free model picker and are reserved for specific accounts that have been granted access directly. Since this is a backend configuration update on the Core/shared layer and nothing visible to general users is wired up yet, there is no change to what you can see or do today; access remains as before unless your account already holds a grant.

d6c8cb0a140c8b3ece3730206176a37a74172b20.text: The assistant now automatically converts picture files it does not understand into a format it can read. When you paste or attach a BMP or TIFF image inside the app, the CLI silently converts it to a PNG behind the scenes. When the same happens through the SDK's read_files tool, the assistant instead refuses the unsupported file and tells you how to convert a copy yourself, such as running a magick command to make a PNG. Everyday users of the Freebuff CLI see no interruption, since it just works; SDK users see a clear, actionable error that still gets their image through after conversion. Live today: this is in the latest build.

0a94252116dc9319f6db81f5abb25f50a5a8f6c7.text: Freebuff now shows a clearer message when your account still carries reduced model access because it was recently used from a region where some models aren't available yet, and it tells you how long those limits stick around. It affects Freebuff users on the free tier who see the smaller model catalog after a recent connection from a restricted region. In daily use, instead of a generic 'some models aren't available' line, the notice explains the situation in plain words and points you to the country-verification page if you've actually moved, so you know whether this is temporary or worth fixing on your account.

4ba40c22c6481732936643698562bfcc1b874d51.text: When Freebuff now shows your daily-use streak on the landing screen, the reward text it displays is driven straight from what the server has decided to credit to your account this time. Freebuff users who are on the Freebucks pay-as-you-go meter see +N Freebucks every day as the recurring 7+ day streak perk, matching what the ledger credits; otherwise it falls back to the session reward copy. You don't need to do anything; when you open the landing screen and have earned the weekly streak, you now see an accurate perk line (Freebucks on the meter, sessions off it) rendered in the same shared way the CLI and desktop surfaces use.

502a0060842d7b99b090d8a19756e14230c60699.text: The assistant can now pass a private, one-time tracking code to a specific sponsored command without touching the rest of the work it does, so advertisers can measure whether their sponsored task led to a real result. This only affects the internal plumbing that runs sponsored tasks for advertisers, and it does not change anything free users or paid subscribers see in their daily coding sessions. There is nothing for you to do; if a sponsored procedure wants this tracking code, it gets it, and if the code is missing or invalid, that one step is simply skipped rather than faked. It is live today for the sponsored-task system.

10c51ede09cee9de5090c0aa49d4d200a6e9a065.text: The change adds two new internal rules that are now in the code but not wired into any feature yet, so nothing you use will behave differently today. One rule tells the desktop app when it is allowed to quietly check for a special sponsored task offer, and it stops checking the moment you switch away from that window or it is no longer the active app. The other rule defines the exact shape of a read-only check that a developer can ask for a guided setup walkthrough inside the desktop app, and it makes clear that this check never bills anyone or runs any paid work. This is internal scaffolding the engineering team added ahead of future work, and it does not change what you see or do right now.

6edaba95110f54cfee58529bbb0cfe1e19d95f5d.text: The assistant now quietly fixes two small problems that used to cause requests to certain AI services to fail or be mislabeled. When you (a Freebuff SDK user) send a request through your own API key instead of through your Freebuff account, the request is automatically rewritten to match what each service expects. For the Luna model, the rewrite changes a token limit field name, removes a field Luna rejects, and slows down its internal reasoning when you ask it to use plugins. For traffic going through OpenRouter to OpenAI-style models, the rewrite attaches a stable anonymous label derived from your API key, so your usage gets attributed correctly instead of being mixed together with other people's requests.

912a3f96607449b4b2915e6addd9b91db2333974.text: Freebuff added an internal diagnostics helper that collects facts a user's computer reports about itself, like its operating system and which product it is running, then packages those facts into a clean, standardized report. Only Freebuff's engineers can see or use the report today; it is not wired into any feature you can reach. You will notice nothing different, because the helper simply organizes information that already existed without sending you anything new.

59628850f6c070bfd42383e35717d22844834d2c.text: The Freebuff team published the list of countries that split the free tier into three groups, ranked by how well ads perform in each market, along with a helper that prints country codes the way the public landing page reads them. It affects free-tier users in or near those countries: the United States, Canada, Britain, Australia, New Zealand, and Ireland plus a second wave of European nations are placed in higher- and lower-value groups, while users elsewhere fall back to limited access. A few countries recently left full access and a couple stayed in the lower tier, so anyone checking eligibility from Singapore, Israel, or South Korea may now see restricted availability.

a659222a118d5923e8a49c83f036c3faeab55fd8.text: Freebuff trimmed a few outdated choices from the post-signup questionnaire (Reddit, GitHub, Designer-or-PM, Non-technical, and GitHub Copilot are gone) and now counts those old answers under their replacement options so the totals stay honest. The tally of responses now also rebuilds under a new version stamp and correctly swaps out a re-submitted answer instead of double-counting it. This only affects the internal survey analytics that the Freebuff service operator reads, so everyday users will not see or need to do anything differently.

30c6fe6b64f898b58aa0fe79858a70d373ecad13.text: {"eli5": "Freebuff now offers a one-time discount on your first session of the day, automatically applied to whichever model you pick, with the savings shared across the desktop app and the command-line tool so only one of them can use it at a time. When you open the assistant in your terminal or on the desktop for the first time today, the model list shows the already-reduced price and labels it as a 'First-tab discount' so you know the lower cost is built in. If a second window tries to start a session at the same time, that one pays the regular price until the first session ends, and the picker updates in real time to reflect which price you will actually be charged."].

990e923559d61a9fd04f94fc5f330ae24f0c8f97.text: The way your daily Freebucks refill time is displayed has been made smarter and more consistent across the app and the web tools developers use. Instead of always showing a reset based on Pacific Time, the system now sends your device's local timezone to the servers, so your Freebucks balance updates based on your own daily schedule. The CLI terminal tool now also shows 'Updating balance…' when your daily pool is due for a refill, instead of using a generic message. This means the reset time you see should now accurately reflect when your Freebucks will renew, based on your location and device settings, rather than a fixed timezone. These changes are live today for anyone using the Freebuff CLI.

2964be866c3e4b3da1f3d9208ed1e8ee6d476a12.text: Before a sponsored task (an advertiser-funded coding job) can run in the terminal, Freebuff now inspects the project to confirm it can be safely contained and identifies it to the server, writing a persistent anonymous project ID only for local repositories without a remote. When a capable project is detected, the ad request is sent to a v2 delivery endpoint carrying this capability evidence, and a sponsored proposal is first previewed and then accepted with the reviewed task bound to that exact project and run, so a task can be refused before it starts if the sandbox or project identity is not actionable.

8ae0c9c1da31404dd515238cb4e196c13c2872fc.text: When you ask Freebuff's agent to work on a task, it normally updates its internal to-do list as it goes, then uses tools to actually do each item. Sometimes a model gets stuck simply rewriting the exact same to-do list over and over instead of acting on it, silently burning through your session's step budget without making progress. Now the agent runtime detects three identical to-do rewrites in a row and injects a recovery reminder telling the model to use a tool or explain the blocker, then at six repeats it stops the turn explicitly and surfaces a clear error so you know the model looped instead of appearing to run forever.

4b2b9ba193f215d52fdda833622d4929ab3b2be8.text: The assistant's memory management just got smarter about keeping the right things in context. When things start to overflow the conversation window, it now carefully sets aside space for the system instructions, the tools it can use, and the current step's guidance before deciding what older parts of the conversation can be safely summarized. This means the latest tool results (like file contents it just read) and the most important recent steps are much less likely to be squeezed out, while still condensing the earlier back-and-forth into a compact summary. You are a Freebuff developer using the CLI or web app, and if you ever hit long, complex coding sessions where context starts to fill up, the assistant will stay on task without losing the crucial recent details.

72627b4a8b54f0f2fb08b872d0ad770891b87e24.text: The internal report that tracks how much it costs to serve paying subscribers now measures each recent hour the system has actually been running, instead of only counting whole, fully covered days. That same report gained new fields that separate those freshly measured hours (which can include a partial day) from the complete days used to build the 30-day cost outlook. Freebuff's cost-tracking system now reads these new fields, so the engineering team can tell whether the latest data is based on hours that are still being gathered or on the steady, full-day baseline behind the forecast.

dedd70d5414f7b9b98050623b74a4fa850669e1b.text: When you ask the assistant to read an image file, it now receives the actual picture instead of a block of unreadable text characters. This applies to anyone using the assistant through the Freebuff CLI, web app, desktop app, or SDK who asks it to look at an image. If you point the assistant at a photo or screenshot, you get back an accurate description of what is in the image rather than a garbled mess of bytes.

a7ea9ca1fdbf59aea2aedd91b557f4416f19695b.text: The Freebuff service now checks every incoming 'showcase ad presentation' report at the server before storing it, accepting only the narrow set of fields it needs and attaching your logged-in identity to the good rows while silently discarding anything that looks off. It affects only Freebuff engineering's internal logs and dashboards, not what you see in the assistant. You notice nothing today and need to take no action. The experiment code that assigns people to a 'treatment' or 'control' group is already written, but nothing in the app reads or uses it yet, so it sits in place doing nothing until it is wired up.

ebc17a50dc3d760f6d6eb023df4abc508e1dbd9f.text: The subscription system gained the building blocks for an optional yearly billing plan: a list of allowed billing cycles (monthly and yearly), a safety check to validate those cycles, and new fields on subscription offers and user subscriptions to carry a yearly price, the chosen billing cycle, and a renewal date. Only the Freebuff engineering team maintains this layer; no other component reads these fields yet, so it changes nothing for anyone at sign-in. Who it affects: this is internal to the Freebuff service - it's plumbing, not a published feature. Subscribers and free-tier users will not see a yearly option appear until a follow-up step wires up the missing pieces. Everyday impact: you notice nothing today.

2c8541e90dcc9e7641fe7d4ba7c03e1eea64bfa4.text: The label that describes what your monthly spending limit is measuring changed from 'tokens' to 'model spend', so the wording now matches the dollar amount shown next to it. Freebuff added an optional cost figure to the usage summary that shows how much your recent requests would cost at list price, but only when Freebuff has this feature configured for your account. You will notice clearer wording on the plans page if you see the cost card; if the card is absent, nothing changes for you.

217906d84aa2113d8c363debba204695a6e074db.text: When you run low on Freebucks (the paid credits that let you use pricier AI models in the CLI, web app, or desktop app) and hit a wall trying to keep working, the screen that stops you now shows a direct link to turn on auto top-up at freebuff.com/freebucks, alongside the existing advice to wait for your next allowance or pick a cheaper model. The existing monthly usage notice for Freebucks users is unchanged, and the new link only appears when the system detects you have too little balance left to continue with the model you selected. This is live today for developers on the Freebuff free tier who pay for compute beyond their allowance.

6bfe1fe6644c350a1d13259cd4141c316e57e1ac.text: Freebuff added a new yes/no flag and two ready-made messages to the part of its session system that decides whether you can start a freshly paid Desktop session. The flag is only meaningful on the Desktop multi-session path, and only takes effect once a server-side switch (FREEBUFF_DESKTOP_PURCHASE_ADMISSION) is turned on, which the diff does not itself set. Because nothing in the shipped code reads the new flag yet, it is in place but does nothing today. The practical effect will be that, when Freebuff turns that switch on, someone trying to start a new paid Desktop session is told plainly that paid Desktop sessions are paused right now, the model itself is fine, and they should try again shortly, instead of the session being started and then refused or charged.

4aa36c7b25c32bdc0605e5abfc8529e306dc4dd7.text: Freebuff added a set of native ad slots specifically for the iOS app to its official ad catalogue, so iOS ads are now tracked separately with their own attribution instead of being merged into web or desktop ad reporting. This change is aimed at advertisers buying placement inventory, not at how you use the assistant. For daily use, there is no visible effect or action needed yet on your device, since the update only registers the new iOS ad slots in the shared definition that advertisers and the ad console use.

c7445e24582aabfa1c2f45c2108982511769385a.title: HY3 models fully withdrawn from Freebuff free mode and pickers
c7445e24582aabfa1c2f45c2108982511769385a.summary: All HY3 wire ids and bundled roots are removed from Freebuff's free-mode allowlists, root agent lists, and model option catalogs in common/src/constants/free-agents.ts and common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts. The constants themselves survive so web/src/llm-api/hy3-fallback.ts can still route them for paid/BYOK callers, exactly as paid/BYOK Kimi outlived its Freebuff removal. FREEBUFF_WEB_RETIRED_PICKER_MODEL_IDS is now empty as const and nothing references it except isFreebuffWebSelectableModelId, making every previously-retired route a hard deletion rather than a picker-only retirement.
c7445e24582aabfa1c2f45c2108982511769385a.evidence: The diff removes HY3-related constants (`FREEBUFF_HY3_MODEL_ID`, `FREEBUFF_HY3_OPENROUTER_PAID_MODEL_ID`) from imports and deletes `base2-free-hy3`, `base2-free-hy3-atlas` entries from `FREEBUFF_ROOT_AGENT_IDS` and `FREE_MODE_AGENT_MODELS` in common/src/constants/free-agents.ts. In common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts, it deletes `HY3_MODEL` and `HY3_OPENROUTER_PAID_MODEL` model option objects, removes HY3 from `FREEBUFF_WEB_MODELS`, `FREEBUFF_WEB_GOD_ONLY_MODELS`, `FREEBUFF_WEB_GOD_ONLY_MODEL_IDS`, and `FREEBUFF_WEB_PREMIUM_MODEL_IDS`, and clears `FREEBUFF_WEB_RETIRED_PICKER_MODEL_IDS` to an empty array.
c7445e24582aabfa1c2f45c2108982511769385a.migration: Freebuff users who had an active session running on HY3 or HY3 (OpenRouter) will be disconnected on the next session admission check; new free sessions can no longer be started on HY3.
c7445e24582aabfa1c2f45c2108982511769385a.unknowns: The diff does not show whether any Freebuff Web UI components still reference HY3 model slugs in templates or whether the paid/BYOK routing path in web/src/llm-api/hy3-fallback.ts was updated independently.

a3dbf723659094910c2cf7d85ec5535dadc3bd98.title: Freebuff hard-blocks VPN, proxy, and Tor traffic in free mode
a3dbf723659094910c2cf7d85ec5535dadc3bd98.summary: Freebuff introduces a hard-block tier for free mode that rejects VPN, proxy, Tor, and residential-proxy traffic outright instead of downgrading it to limited mode. The new common/src/util/freebuff-privacy.ts exports FREEBUFF_HARD_BLOCKED_PRIVACY_SIGNALS and isFreebuffHardBlockedPrivacySignal, and shouldHardBlockFreeModeAccess in web/src/server/free-mode-country.ts treats Cloudflare Tor country 'T1' and anonymous_network signals as hard blocks. The session handlers in web/src/app/api/v1/freebuff/session/_handlers.ts and the chat completions route in web/src/app/api/v1/chat/completions/_post.ts now return a 403 country_blocked response and terminate the session for hard-blocked requests. Hosting, relay, anonymous, and service signals remain limited rather than hard-blocked, and the CLI surfaces the country_blocked reason in the waiting room screen with a VPN/proxy/Tor-specific message.
a3dbf723659094910c2cf7d85ec5535dadc3bd98.evidence: Commit a3dbf723 adds common/src/util/freebuff-privacy.ts exporting FREEBUFF_HARD_BLOCKED_PRIVACY_SIGNALS (vpn, proxy, tor, res_proxy) and isFreebuffHardBlockedPrivacySignal, plus shouldHardBlockFreeModeAccess in web/src/server/free-mode-country.ts (hard-blocks Cloudflare Tor country 'T1' and anonymous_network with a hard-blocked signal); _handlers.ts and _post.ts call shouldHardBlockFreeModeAccess to return country_blocked 403 responses, and tests assert 'blocks VPN/proxy privacy signals before joining the queue', 'blocks Cloudflare Tor before joining the queue', 'returns country_blocked on GET for VPN/proxy privacy signals', 'returns country_blocked on GET for Cloudflare Tor', and 'hard-blocks Cloudflare Tor without falling back to IP geo'.
a3dbf723659094910c2cf7d85ec5535dadc3bd98.migration: Freebuff users on VPN, proxy, or Tor must disable that traffic and restart Freebuff to use free mode; hosting-only and relay signals continue to work in limited mode without changes.
a3dbf723659094910c2cf7d85ec5535dadc3bd98.unknowns: The diff does not show which ipinfo privacy-signal source populates the vpn/proxy/tor/res_proxy signals for non-Cloudflare requests, nor whether the hard-block list is configurable beyond code.

changes.what: New module defining FREEBUFF_HARD_BLOCKED_PRIVACY_SIGNALS and isFreebuffHardBlockedPrivacySignal for classifying vpn, proxy, tor, and res_proxy signals.
Adds shouldHardBlockFreeModeAccess that hard-blocks Cloudflare Tor country 'T1' and anonymous_network with a hard-blocked signal, while hosting and relay remain limited.
Session POST and GET handlers now check shouldHardBlockFreeModeAccess and return a 403 country_blocked response, ending any existing session.
Chat completions route checks shouldHardBlockFreeModeAccess and rejects hard-blocked free-mode requests with a 403 country_blocked response.
Waiting room screen renders the country_blocked reason with a VPN/proxy/Tor-specific message sourced from formatFreebuffHardBlockedPrivacySignals.
Send-message error handler uses getFreeModeUnavailableErrorMessage for free mode errors instead of the generic FREE_MODE_UNAVAILABLE_MESSAGE.

eb3a241ab9e1d873a2d3256baa5228323dcccf3d.title: TikTok CAPI reports activation events on native surface pages
eb3a241ab9e1d873a2d3256baa5228323dcccf3d.summary: TikTok Conversions API support in `common/src/paid-social-capi.ts` now accepts a `surface` field on `SendPaidSocialConversionParams` and uses `tikTokEventPage` to map non-registration events to `https://freebuff.com/desktop` or `https://freebuff.com/cli` instead of rejecting them. Previously only `CompleteRegistration` was sent for TikTok, with `event` hardcoded to `CompleteRegistration` and `page.url` pinned to the public OAuth signup path; the body now emits `params.eventName` and the resolved page URL per surface. Native coding activations are reported as a custom web event on the surface's public product page so TikTok sees a stable public URL rather than a private or token-bearing context.
eb3a241ab9e1d873a2d3256baa5228323dcccf3d.evidence: The diff adds surface?: 'web' | 'desktop' | 'cli' to `SendPaidSocialConversionParams` in `common/src/paid-social-capi.ts`, introduces the `tikTokEventPage` function, and replaces the prior `event: 'CompleteRegistration'` and page: { url: ... } literals with `event: params.eventName` and page: { url: page } driven by that new function.
eb3a241ab9e1d873a2d3256baa5228323dcccf3d.migration: Advertisers sending TikTok activation events must now supply the `surface` property on the conversion payload because native-surface activations are no longer rejected.
eb3a241ab9e1d873a2d3256baa5228323dcccf3d.unknowns: The diff does not show who calls `sendPaidSocialConversion` or passes the new `surface` value at runtime.

4cb83e770ab4290df3813b4526fcd55978f5a323.title: Sponsored Linux worktree git sandbox rebased on tmpfs
4cb83e770ab4290df3813b4526fcd55978f5a323.summary: The CLI's sponsored-run containment for linked git worktrees now mounts the user's real `.git` common dir as a tmpfs with its entries rebound read-only, instead of binding it read-only and covering dangerous paths. `prepareLinkedWorktreeForLinux` makes the run's own branch loose from `packed-refs` and creates the namespace directories the writable binds need, and `HIDDEN_COMMON_DIR_ENTRIES` keeps `packed-refs` and `packed-refs.lock` out of the bounce so git can take its lock while a packed-ref table rewrite is never reachable on the host. This is the Linux arm of `sdk/src/tools/sponsored-sandbox.ts`, which is shared by the CLI via `cli/src/utils/sponsored-run.ts`.
4cb83e770ab4290df3813b4526fcd55978f5a323.evidence: In `sdk/src/tools/sponsored-sandbox.ts`, `linkedWorktreeBindArgs` (read-only common dir with read-only overlays) is replaced by `prepareLinkedWorktreeForLinux`, which mounts an empty `--tmpfs` at the common dir, rebinds every existing entry read-only via `linuxCommonDirMounts`, and deliberately omits `packed-refs` and `packed-refs.lock` via `HIDDEN_COMMON_DIR_ENTRIES`; `spawnLinux` now calls `prepareLinkedWorktreeForLinux` and binds the granted write subpaths writable on top.
4cb83e770ab4290df3813b4526fcd55978f5a323.unknowns: The new test gate's integration into the CLI/Desktop suites and the ci.yml test-sponsored-containment job are not shown in this diff, and the consumer of the Auth pair's campaign ids in the serving path is not visible here.

changes.what: Rebased the Linux linked-worktree git sandbox on a tmpfs of the common dir with entries rebound read-only, replacing the previous read-only bind and per-path overlays; added prepareLinkedWorktreeForLinux, linuxCommonDirMounts, HIDDEN_COMMON_DIR_ENTRIES, and the --tmpfs flag.

Reworked upstream refusal handling in acceptSponsoredProposal: enumerated PROPOSAL_ERROR_SENTENCES (funded_accept_required, invalid_state, cloud_keyed), added looksLikeMachineCode, and rewrote upstreamMessage so known codes map to human sentences while unknown prose still surfaces; read_files.

Wired the typed OverrideToolHandlers into the sponsored turn: sponsoredOverrideTools now returns SponsoredOverrideTools (the seven admitted tools, all required) and runSponsoredTurn passes it without a `never` cast.

Added the Supabase format-pair registry: SUPABASE_FORMAT_DATABASE_PAIR (supabase-database-persist-one-feature@1.1.0) and SUPABASE_FORMAT_AUTH_PROCEDURE, plus supabaseFormatPairs/parseSupabaseAuthFormatCampaignIds reading FREEBUFF_SUPABASE_AUTH_FORMAT_CAMPAIGN_IDS and the pair lookup helpers.
Exported OverrideToolHandlers as a public SDK type alongside the existing run/run-state exports.

Added the shared containment test gate (sponsoredContainmentUsable, sponsoredContainmentTestGate) that skips when no sandbox host is present and fails the build under SPONSORED_CONTAINMENT_REQUIRED=1.

0d8894ca77aef154b2d414afb75c21846988c335.title: Self-serve plan changes with Stripe preview and overage tier split
0d8894ca77aef154b2d414afb75c21846988c335.summary: Replaced the single checkout-session flow with a self-serve plan change experience: `/api/stripe/subscription` returns the current plan, `/api/stripe/subscription/change` previews prorations via `stripeServer.invoices.retrieveUpcoming` and applies upgrades/downgrades with `stripeServer.subscriptions.update`. Plans were renamed from `PAID`/`PRO_PLUS` to `PRO`/`MOAR_PRO` in `common/src/constants.ts` (`PLAN_CONFIGS`), with overage rates split into `OVERAGE_RATE_PRO` (0.99) and `OVERAGE_RATE_MOAR_PRO` (0.9) and `OVERAGE_RATE_PRO_PLUS` removed. New Stripe env vars `STRIPE_PRO_PRICE_ID`/`STRIPE_PRO_OVERAGE_PRICE_ID`/`STRIPE_MOAR_PRO_PRICE_ID`/`STRIPE_MOAR_PRO_OVERAGE_PRICE_ID` replace the single `STRIPE_SUBSCRIPTION_PRICE_ID`, and the pricing cards now route to `/subscription/confirm?plan=...`. Retry logic was extracted from `backend/src/claude.ts` into `withRetry` in `common/src/util/promise.ts`, and helper types `InvoiceLineItem`/`SubscriptionPreviewResponse` were added in `common/src/types/plan.ts`.
0d8894ca77aef154b2d414afb75c21846988c335.evidence: web/src/app/api/stripe/subscription/change/route.ts (new file implementing GET preview + POST change with `stripeServer.subscriptions.update`, `stripeServer.invoices.retrieveUpcoming`, and `stripeServer.billing.meterEvents.create`), web/src/app/subscription/confirm/page.tsx (new confirm UI consuming the preview), web/src/app/api/stripe/subscription/route.ts (new GET returning `currentPlan`), web/src/lib/stripe-utils.ts (new helpers `getPlanPriceIds`, `getPlanFromPriceId`, `getSubscriptionItemByType`, `validatePlanChange`, `checkForUnpaidInvoices`, `getTotalReferralCreditsForCustomer`), web/src/components/pricing/paid-plan-footer.tsx + web/src/components/pricing/free-plan-button.tsx (pricing cards now route to /subscription/confirm?plan=...), common/src/constants.ts (plan enum renamed PAID/PRO_PLUS to PRO/MOAR_PRO via PLAN_CONFIGS, OVERAGE_RATE_PRO_PLUS replaced by OVERAGE_RATE_MOAR_PRO, STRIPE_SUBSCRIPTION_PRICE_ID removed from backend/src/env.mjs and web/src/env.mjs replaced by STRIPE_PRO_PRICE_ID/STRIPE_PRO_OVERAGE_PRICE_ID/STRIPE_MOAR_PRO_PRICE_ID/STRIPE_MOAR_PRO_OVERAGE_PRICE_ID), scripts/migrate-stripe-customers.ts deleted, web/src/app/api/stripe/checkout-session/route.ts deleted, web/src/lib/stripe.ts deleted, common/src/util/promise.ts + backend/src/claude.ts (withRetry extracted and promptClaudeStream delegates to it), common/src/types/plan.ts (new InvoiceLineItem/SubscriptionPreviewResponse), common/src/util/string.ts (capitalize added), web/src/components/ui/* (new.
0d8894ca77aef154b2d414afb75c21846988c335.migration: Operators must set STRIPE_PRO_PRICE_ID, STRIPE_PRO_OVERAGE_PRICE_ID, STRIPE_MOAR_PRO_PRICE_ID, and STRIPE_MOAR_PRO_OVERAGE_PRICE_ID in place of the removed STRIPE_SUBSCRIPTION_PRICE_ID and STRIPE_OVERAGE_PRICE_ID.

b816aed976efe357204d4878122710062c89ec89.title: Desktop purchase claim states added to session admission
b816aed976efe357204d4878122710062c89ec89.summary: Three new admission statuses cover Desktop purchase lifecycle: `purchase_claim_released` retires a single-use claim so a fresh id is persisted before retry, while `purchase_in_use` and `purchase_capacity` surface an occupied tab and remaining capacity for a requested Desktop model. The hook's `nextDelayMs` now returns null for those statuses, so the poll loop stops spinning instead of retrying atomically checked capacity. Admission and superseded responses carry `desktopPurchases` and `desktopRefunds` arrays; the refund shape records `poolDate` so it points at the daily spend pool restored by the reversal ledger entry, and `claimInstanceIds` ties each refund to its execution claims.

It also adds `desktopPurchases` and `desktopRefunds` arrays to admission and superseded responses, plus new interfaces `FreebuffDesktopRefundInfo` and `FreebuffDesktopPurchaseInfo`, and a `FREEBUFF_PURCHASE_CONTINUITY_HEADER` constant in common/src/constants/freebuff-desktop-sessions.ts.
b816aed976efe357204d4878122710062c89ec89.migration: No action required to keep using the CLI; the new statuses and purchase/refund payloads are consumed by the Desktop client and the admission gate, which handle them without changing existing session join behavior.

fb0ab0941b7c17b23b57e0d950f836d852c4d912.summary: The CLI now renders Freebucks as a currency label, wallet, and monthly usage line across the header, picker notice, rate-limited walls, and a monthly-limit refusal branch, while hiding the legacy session counter for metered accounts. The referral banner takes a new `metered` prop that swaps the dashboard label to `METERED_DASHBOARD_LABEL` ('Open Earn ↵') and switches locked-state copy to a Freebucks-only pitch, and the landing screen derives `metered` from `freebucksOf(session)`. settings.ts adds an allowlisted `freebucksIntroSeenAt` so the once-only Freebucks intro survives a round trip through settings.json, matching the test titled "survives a round trip through the settings file" and the one-time introduction mark.
fb0ab0941b7c17b23b57e0d950f836d852c4d912.evidence: In cli/src/utils/freebucks.ts, freebucksHeaderLine now joins parts as `${formatFreebucks(daily.remaining)}/${formatFreebucks(daily.limit)} ${FREEBUCKS_LABEL} daily`, `… in wallet`, and `… monthly usage left`; a new FREEBUCKS_PICKER_NOTICE is added and imported into cli/src/components/freebuff-landing-screen.tsx; the landing screen substitutes metered rate_limited/refusal copy and gates showSessionCounter with !metered; the referral banner gains a metered prop driving METERED_DASHBOARD_LABEL ('Open Earn ↵') and a Freebucks-only pitch branch; and settings.ts allowlists freebucksIntroSeenAt, with hasSeenFreebucksIntro/markFreebucksIntroSeen present but not invoked here.
fb0ab0941b7c17b23b57e0d950f836d852c4d912.migration: No migration required; existing settings.json files keep their prior keys and only gain freebucksIntroSeenAt on the next Freebucks intro render.
fb0ab0941b7c17b23b57e0d950f836d852c4d912.unknowns: The diff does not show where markFreebucksIntroSeen is invoked to set the one-time introduction mark, so the trigger path for that setting is not visible here.

9501bb0a55ec3bbbd225e477130c427534dc3f11.text: Freebuff added a new AI model called Solar Pro 4 to its free model selector, so you can now pick it from the list of models included with the service. It is available to anyone using the free tier of Freebuff, including the CLI, web app, and desktop app, as a limited-time trial with a large 524K context window for text-only tasks. Nothing else in your experience changes unless you choose Solar Pro 4 from the model picker instead of your usual default.

78d1eebe0a27ffa9f8d4d3b6d38261f19d5acd11.text: This release re-centers Freebuff on GLM 5.3 Flash as the default free model and brings a proper Freebucks pay-as-you-go credit system to the CLI, so you now see a clear dollar balance and monthly usage instead of just a session counter. A new /export command lets you save any conversation to a markdown or JSON file in your project folder, and slash commands like /skill now enter a dedicated input mode so you can add instructions before running them. Ad safety improves with stricter click-id tracking, household-leg eligibility checks, and a one-sentence consent screen for sponsored proposals that opens a local consent panel before any code runs. The CLI landing screen now spells out long wait times in days instead of hours, carries your Freebucks balance onto rate-limited and spend-limited screens, and shows an intro card for first-time metered users. Upgrading gives you a more transparent model picker, safer sponsored-code handling, and clearer billing signals when you are near a limit.

fd93692e814f3a7a4a3e61773e10e58384120e64.text: Freebuff 0.0.181 adds the newer MiMo 2.6 Flash and MiMo 2.6 Pro AI models to the free model picker (replacing the older MiMo 2.5), introduces a way to start a BYOK session directly from the paywall screen so you can keep coding when your free credits run out, and lets developers compact a stored conversation history on demand to free up space. The release also makes the landing screen name the specific server host that could not be reached when a session times out (instead of showing a raw technical error), drops the refund-display wording from the landing screen and end-session command, holds the GLM 5.3 Flash price ceiling at the same level after rejecting a raise, and fixes the daily Freebucks streak copy to match the Pacific-clock reset. Upgrading gives you access to the latest MiMo models, a smoother path past credit walls via BYOK, clearer network-failure messages naming the host involved, and on-demand history compaction that returns token savings alongside telemetry. These changes affect what models you can pick, how you recover from payment or network limits, and how much of a conversation the tool keeps when it trims history.

358336a18e557894e7bbdd623c43e34f1bc54f6f.text: This release adds a daily countdown to your free usage so you can see exactly when your pool resets, shows a peak pricing badge on model rows when demand is high, and lets you open the plans page directly from a model you can't yet afford. It fixes a keyboard bug where pressing any key on the Freebucks intro screen would accidentally start a session on the cheapest model instead of just dismissing the notice. The model picker now recommends the cheaper GLM 5.3 Flash as the hero for the limited tier while keeping DeepSeek V4 Flash as the safe fallback, and Muse Spark 1.2 replaces the withdrawn 1.3 in the free picker. The session lifecycle now tracks refunds explicitly and coalesces exit and end-session calls to prevent race conditions, while on-meter spend ceilings and trust level budgets are skipped to stop false exhaustion reports for accounts with remaining Freebucks. Daily spend caps have been replaced with soft session pacing that adds pauses rather than blocking prompts, and the CLI no longer shows monthly usage left in the header. Ad operations gain country exclusion codes, response body detail in error logs, and a new sponsor break creative module that renders a single accented word in break cards without counting the markup against the 28-character title limit.

eb3a241ab9e1d873a2d3256baa5228323dcccf3d.text: Freebuff now reports when someone signs up through its desktop app or command-line tool to TikTok ads, in addition to website signups. This only affects advertisers who buy ad placements and run TikTok ad campaigns. You do not need to do anything differently; your signups are just tracked more completely for those ad campaigns.

77a74b9437db605159cf13c57b72d52293a6f17b.text: This release makes GLM 5.3 Flash the default free AI model across the CLI, web, and desktop, replacing GPT-5.6 Luna, and adds a new Slash command (/reasoning) to control how deeply the model thinks before responding. GLM 5.3 Flash is now unmetered and uncapped, Solar Pro 4 joins the free model picker as a limited-time option, and the desktop referral banner now links directly to your referral status tab for easier tracking. You also get better protection against spend abuse with per-account daily ceilings that adapt based on region, flagged email domains, and privacy-egress signals such as VPN or proxy use, and the CLI copy command now falls back to terminal rendering when native clipboard tools are unavailable. Onboarding no longer uses a bypass cookie, and the trust-based payment system now charges a flat 1 trust point per prompt, making engagement rewards predictable and consistent.

1217a53754489ef6be6257b36a25fcd8d4edb110.text: The assistant can now pick up where it left off if you switch from the default hosted provider to your own personal provider (a bring-your-own-key connection), but only when you explicitly choose to make that switch. This matters to developers building on the Freebuff SDK who resume a prior conversation under a different inference setup: instead of being blocked, they can opt in so the assistant transfers the history onto the newly selected provider and pins checkpoints there for the next call. Nothing happens automatically - the default behavior still refuses to change providers mid-session, and hosts must pass a deliberate flag to allow it, so nobody is surprised by a silent connection change during their development workflow.

a8d0c1a83f4dc3677069dec06aca8a2aa3bdfb20.text: Starting September 13, 2026, Freebuff's Solar Pro 4 model returned to its regular price of 5 Freebucks after a brief period where it was available at no charge. This change only affects people who operate or maintain the Freebuff service itself, since the Freebucks price is set through internal configuration constants that ship with the software. If you use Freebuff, you do not need to do anything, and you will not notice anything different unless you were actively tracking the model's pricing history.

f48d871ed62bc99da5c8486f58e5847750fcb2fd.text: The assistant that thinks through your chat questions before answering has switched to a new AI model, GPT-5.6 Luna, and now reasons harder than before. Anyone using the Freebuff web or desktop chat is affected - that helper now uses the new model and puts more effort into its thinking. You may notice answers take a bit longer to come back but are more thorough, because the thinking step is now working at extra-high effort instead of high. This change went live with this release, and there is nothing you need to do to get it.

89c9dacbe5a3a04c7a4ef59b255eb3f6f6c1ccc4.text: The Freebuff SDK can now manually shrink down a saved conversation's history on demand, using the same mechanical cleanup the assistant already does automatically, and then report how many tokens were saved before and after. This is aimed at developers and integrators who embed Freebuff in other products and keep conversation states on disk between turns, letting them compact a stored run's history whenever they choose instead of only when the assistant's own triggers fire. You won't notice anything new as a regular user today, since the SDK's host applications are what call this; it just gives those builders a knob to reclaim context space right when they need it, rather than waiting for the assistant to decide it's worth doing on its own.

4cb83e770ab4290df3813b4526fcd55978f5a323.text: The CLI's sponsored-run containment for linked git worktrees now mounts the user's real `.git` common dir as a tmpfs with its entries rebound read-only, instead of binding it read-only and covering dangerous paths. This is an internal change for the Freebuff engineering team only (maintainers), and it affects the Linux arm of the SDK's `sponsored-sandbox` tool shared by the CLI via `cli/src/utils/sponsored-run.ts`. You will not notice any difference in daily use: no setting has changed, no command looks different, and no behavior visible to a Freebuff user has changed. It is live today only in code that runs on Linux hosts with bubblewrap installed; macOS behavior is unaffected and the CLI Desktop flow is unchanged.

df46a33ebe7178f9f9a56740f859e846215f982d.text: Freebuff has stopped routing Solar Pro 4 traffic through Upstage's zero-data-retention endpoint and now uses the provider's standard route instead, which lets Upstage access debugging information it needs to keep the service running. This affects anyone who selects Solar Pro 4 as their model from the free picker, since that model is now being sent to a different backend than before. In daily use, there is no visible change to how the model responds or bills, though Upstage may gain operational insight that could improve reliability going forward.

5f45bd81450eb50ba253ec315e067f798771d98a.text: Today the assistant made Solar Pro 4 free to try again, flipping the price back to $0 per session through the rest of the day so you can keep testing it without spending Freebucks. This applies to anyone using the free model picker who runs Solar Pro 4 right now, and you see it immediately when you select that model and start a new session. No action needed on your part: the change is live now, and the assistant simply charges nothing for that model until the promotion ends.

abd1eed4ab8de4111232935a21962b5a03ff5a33.text: A one-time tips screen that explains Freebucks (the free AI credits) was sometimes starting a paid model session by accident when you pressed any key to dismiss it. Now the screen properly stops that single keypress from also confirming a model selection, so dismissing the tips never accidentally charges you. This matters to anyone using Freebuff on the free tier who sees the Freebucks introduction screen. Going forward, pressing a key just closes the tips normally, and the model picker below waits patiently for you to actually choose a model.

04578916f453fcab40ef1d5dac060e94ab126108.text: The model list in the CLI now shows a small badge on models that cost more right now during busy hours, and hovering or focusing it explains in plain text which hours those are and what the lower price will return to. Who it affects: anyone using the Freebuff CLI to pick a model for coding. Everyday impact: you see at a glance when a model is temporarily more expensive and exactly when the cheaper price comes back, in your own time zone, with no need to do the math yourself.

253ee6c497c3d67371a7cddabfeacaebb19e308a.text: The system now automatically reads the price schedule for free model promotions (like the Solar Pro 4 September 2026 weekend deal) and uses it to figure out exactly which dates and times a model was promised to you at no charge. The core change is that the assistant no longer guesses or relies on separate lists to know when to skip counting a free model's cost against your daily usage allowance. This affects Freebuff users on the free tier, who pick models from the free model picker. In everyday impact, if a model is advertised as free for a weekend, using it during that specific time window will no longer consume your daily usage credits, but only during that exact free-promotion period.

fb0ab0941b7c17b23b57e0d950f836d852c4d912.text: When you open the Freebuff assistant in the terminal, the startup screen now shows how much of your Freebucks balance you have left and how long to wait before it refills, instead of showing the old daily session counter for people on the new pay-per-use pricing. If you are on the Freebucks plan, the referral banner now simply points you to the Earn page to claim rewards, and the model picker explains that each model costs a certain amount of Freebucks per hour. No action is needed from you; the screen just reports your current balance and wait time automatically.

e8a3c7930b8024d099e2c2abf75ff582798a73c9.text: The paid-only model list has been split into two groups: one for all full-access surfaces and a separate one specifically for limited web-only users. A new gate, isFreebuffLimitedTierPlanOnlyModelId, now controls which rows only paid accounts at the limited tier can open. The web regional catalog no longer includes Luna for unpaid limited-tier access. This is internal catalog maintenance by the Freebuff engineering team; it reshuffles which models are plan-locked where, but the developer-facing free model picker itself is unchanged, so daily use for you as a developer is unaffected.

c7445e24582aabfa1c2f45c2108982511769385a.text: The AI model called HY3 has been completely removed from the free version of Freebuff. This means that anyone using Freebuff for free can no longer start a new session using HY3, and any existing session running on HY3 will be disconnected the next time the system checks active sessions. This is a breaking change that took effect on August 4, 2026. The model itself still exists for paid users or those using their own API keys, so it is not gone entirely, just no longer free.

a4b3d0fa55c77663581617e15840fb467c110159.text: A new helper was added so sponsor-break headlines can mark exactly one word to appear in a highlight color on Desktop break cards, while every other surface (the CLI dock, inline terminal card, and house-ad width budget) receives the plain headline with the markers removed. The parser accepts only a single *…* span, leaves a stray asterisk untouched, and measures the headline against the 28-character title limit using the plain text so markup never eats into the advertiser's copy budget.

76a5696e5fdd93b9dc8dded8d2d0c8fac82937ab.text: Starting September 5 2026, the assistant picks a different AI model automatically as the first choice: GLM 5.3 Flash now leads the model list everywhere, ahead of DeepSeek V4 Flash. If you use the free CLI, web, desktop, or SDK, the suggested starting model is GLM 5.3 Flash, and that is also how it appears at the top of the model picker in the README and FAQ. Note that on the limited tier (used outside full-access regions or over VPN), the default hero model stays DeepSeek V4 Flash, because GLM 5.3 Flash there is earned meter and not available to a brand-new limited user with no earned sessions.

a3dbf723659094910c2cf7d85ec5535dadc3bd98.text: Freebuff now refuses to run at all if you are connecting through a VPN, proxy, Tor, or a similar anonymized network, instead of quietly giving you a slower experience. This affects anyone using the Freebuff CLI or web app on the free plan. In daily use, you will see a clear message telling you to turn off that privacy tool, and then you can restart Freebuff to use free mode normally; otherwise the assistant will not respond.

5454338099733607d45ae7442117bf2879569637.text: The Freebuff app now leads its list of free-to-use models for users in limited-access regions (such as VPN users) with GLM 5.3 Flash, a cheaper model, while keeping DeepSeek V4 Flash as the automatic fallback when a chosen model cannot be used. This affects users on the limited access tier, which applies to accounts in unsupported regions rather than paying subscribers. Most users will not see a difference unless they are on the limited tier, in which case the recommended model in the picker may now be the lower-cost GLM option when they select a model.

0d8894ca77aef154b2d414afb75c21846988c335.text: Developers who pay for Codebuff can now change their plan directly in the app instead of going through Stripe's checkout page. They see a clear preview of how much they'll pay or get credited for the rest of the billing period, then confirm the switch in one click. This affects subscribers on paid plans when they upgrade or downgrade, and they'll notice the pricing page now shows the new plan names and the subscription area walks them through the cost before they commit. The change is live today.

df596975d3847f148250d348fada73ef08f30465.title: CLI login screen with browser-based authentication
df596975d3847f148250d348fada73ef08f30465.summary: The CLI now gates the chat behind authentication by rendering a browser-based login screen when no valid API key is found at startup. cli/src/index.tsx resolves credentials via getUserCredentials and getUserInfoFromApiKey from @codebuff/sdk, then passes requireAuth and hasInvalidCredentials into App in cli/src/chat.tsx, which returns a LoginScreen component instead of the chat when requireAuth is true. The new login-screen.tsx posts a fingerprint to the backend /api/auth/cli/code endpoint, opens the user's browser, polls /api/auth/cli/status every 5 seconds for up to 5 minutes, and saves the returned user via saveUserCredentials before calling onLoginSuccess; /login and /logout are now handled inline by handleSubmit rather than as slash commands (login was removed from slash-commands.ts). Supporting modules include auth.ts for credential files under ~/.config/manicode, analytics.ts for PostHog tracking, clipboard.ts and terminal-link.tsx for copying the fallback login URL, and the logger now routes through pino with analytics buffering.
df596975d3847f148250d348fada73ef08f30465.evidence: cli/src/chat.tsx wraps the chat UI in authentication gates: App now accepts requireAuth and hasInvalidCredentials props, holds isAuthenticated/user state, renders <LoginScreen> when !isAuthenticated, and intercepts /login and /logout commands in handleSubmit; cli/src/index.tsx calls getUserInfoFromApiKey at startup and passes requireAuth={!authResult} and hasInvalidCredentials={!authResult} to <App>; new files cli/src/components/login-screen.tsx, cli/src/components/login-screen-utils.ts, cli/src/components/terminal-link.tsx, cli/src/utils/auth.ts, cli/src/utils/analytics.ts, cli/src/utils/clipboard.ts, and cli/src/utils/suppress-console.ts wire up browser-based login, credential storage, PostHog analytics, the clipboard helpers, and console suppression; cli/package.json adds open, pino, posthog-node, and zod; cli/src/data/slash-commands.ts removes the login command; sdk/src/index.ts adds export * from './constants' (no behavior change to the SDK).
df596975d3847f148250d348fada73ef08f30465.unknowns: The diff does not show when initAnalytics is called or who populates NEXT_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_API_KEY and NEXT_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_HOST_URL for end users. A second read of the same diff did not confirm that a migration step is required.

changes.what: App now accepts requireAuth and hasInvalidCredentials props, tracks isAuthenticated/user state, renders <LoginScreen> when !isAuthenticated, and intercepts /login and /logout in handleSubmit.
Startup resolves credentials via getUserCredentials and getUserInfoFromApiKey and passes requireAuth and hasInvalidCredentials to <App>.
New login-screen.tsx, login-screen-utils.ts, and terminal-link.tsx implement the browser login UI and URL copy fallback.
New auth.ts stores/loads credentials, clipboard.ts and suppress-console.ts back the login and analytics modules.
New analytics.ts initializes PostHog and provides trackEvent, identifyUser, and logError.
Logger rewritten onto pino with analytics buffering and flushAnalytics integration.

verifyClaims.claim: posts a fingerprint to the backend /api/auth/cli/code endpoint
The new login-screen.tsx posts a fingerprint to the backend /api/auth/cli/code endpoint
verifyClaims.reason: Diff shows POST to ${WEBSITE_URL}/api/auth/cli/code with { fingerprintId }, not BACKEND_URL or /api/auth/cli/code on backend.

e6c61f451394b49df437af776c496a0365474fd6.title: Solar Pro 4 promo price and Freebucks price-change watcher
e6c61f451394b49df437af776c496a0365474fd6.summary: A Labor Day weekend promotion makes Solar Pro 4 freebucks-priced at zero through Sep 7 PT, then reverts to the regular $5 offer on Sep 8, with the schedule carried in the server's announced priceChanges payload so idle clients resync on their next poll. The CLI now wakes an open model picker at each quote's next price transition and applies scheduled changes at fetch time, including on delayed responses, so an open picker leaves the holiday price at the cutoff and submits at the new price. The shared price-change helpers also gate the session poll delay so a client sleeps until the next scheduled transition rather than a stale fixed interval.
e6c61f451394b49df437af776c496a0365474fd6.evidence: New file common/src/util/freebuff-price-changes.ts exports applyFreebucksPriceChanges, nextFreebucksPriceChange, and watchFreebucksPriceChanges; new file common/src/constants/freebuff-solar-promo.ts exports SOLAR_REGULAR_OFFER, SOLAR_PRICE_CHANGES, and solarOfferAt; freebuff-models.ts imports SOLAR_REGULAR_OFFER and sets SOLAR_PRO_4_MODEL tagline from it; freebuff-session.ts adds FreebuffPriceChange interface and calls applyFreebucksPriceChanges in getFreebucksInfo; freebuff-session-pools.ts calls applyFreebucksPriceChanges in getFreebuffModelMeter; cli/src/components/freebuff-model-selector.tsx calls watchFreebucksPriceChanges and uses taglineFor; cli/src/hooks/use-freebuff-session.ts imports nextFreebucksPriceChange and folds it into the poll delay.
e6c61f451394b49df437af776c496a0365474fd6.unknowns: The diff does not show the server-side producer of priceChanges or the rollout boundary for Solar Pro 4's full-access entitlement. A second read of the same diff did not confirm that a migration step is required.

changes.what: Added SOLAR_REGULAR_OFFER, SOLAR_PRICE_CHANGES, and solarOfferAt describing the Sep 5-7 freebucks-zero Labor Day promo for Solar Pro 4 reverting to the $5 offer on Sep 8, and wired SOLAR_REGULAR_OFFER.tagline into the Solar Pro 4 model definition.
Added applyFreebucksPriceChanges, nextFreebucksPriceChange, and watchFreebucksPriceChanges to apply the server's announced schedule at fetch time and wake open pickers at the next transition.
Added the FreebuffPriceChange interface and priceNotices/priceChanges fields to FreebuffFreebucksInfo, and route getFreebucksInfo through applyFreebucksPriceChanges.
Imported watchFreebucksPriceChanges to re-render the picker on price transitions, added taglineFor to resolve row labels from priceNotices, and fed it into the width layout deps.
Imported nextFreebucksPriceChange and folded the next transition into the poll delay so the session loop wakes at the upcoming price change.

4ac0d8ab8584d5ada8c2f0bda35ab6b7c974e02f.title: CLI picker routes rows through the Freebucks model meter
4ac0d8ab8584d5ada8c2f0bda35ab6b7c974e02f.summary: The CLI model selector and active session summary now read the Freebucks meter via `getFreebuffModelMeter` (`common/src/util/freebuff-session-pools.ts`) and render a row's price and balance as price Freebucks · balance available instead of a legacy session quota when the server prices that model. freebucks is now carried through the landing synthesis in `toLandingSession`, the `ended` and `none` states in `use-freebuff-session.ts`, and across compact polls in `mergeCompactActiveSession`, so meters survive the frame between a synthesized landing and the refreshing GET. `FreebuffFreebucksInfo` gains `quotaExempt?: boolean` and a docblock stating that for models in `prices` the balance takes precedence over `rateLimitsByModel` and referral balances when starting a session. A new test fixture `freebucksFixture` in `common/src/testing/freebuff.ts` supplies a currency snapshot with no plan or spend for client boundary assertions.
4ac0d8ab8584d5ada8c2f0bda35ab6b7c974e02f.evidence: new file `common/src/testing/freebuff.ts` exporting `freebucksFixture`; new `getFreebuffModelMeter` in `common/src/util/freebuff-session-pools.ts`; `cli/src/components/freebuff-model-selector.tsx` importing and calling `getFreebuffModelMeter`/`getFreebucksInfo`; `cli/src/components/freebuff-active-session-summary.tsx` using `getFreebucksInfo` and `getFreebuffModelMeter`; `cli/src/hooks/use-freebuff-session.ts` carrying freebucks through `toLandingSession`, the `ended` state, the `none` probe merge, and `markFreebuffSessionEnded`; `cli/src/utils/freebuff-session-api.ts` preserving freebucks across compact polls in `mergeCompactActiveSession`; `common/src/types/freebuff-session.ts` adding `quotaExempt?: boolean` and a meter-precedence docblock to `FreebuffFreebucksInfo`; `common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts` adding `FREEBUFF_GLM_V53_FLASH_MODEL_ID` to `LIMITED_FREEBUFF_MODEL_IDS` and clarifying `isRewardModelRedeemableAtLimitedTier`.
4ac0d8ab8584d5ada8c2f0bda35ab6b7c974e02f.migration: If you embed `FreebuffModelSelector` or call `startFreebuffSession` directly, update your integration to pass a `startSession?: (model: string) => Promise<void>` prop, since the picker no longer hard-wires `startFreebuffSession`.

changes.what: Added `getFreebuffModelMeter` to `common/src/util/freebuff-session-pools.ts`, added `quotaExempt?: boolean` and a meter-precedence note to `FreebuffFreebucksInfo` in `common/src/types/freebuff-session.ts`, and added `FREEBUFF_GLM_V53_FLASH_MODEL_ID` to `LIMITED_FREEBUFF_MODEL_IDS`.
Routed the model selector and active session summary through `getFreebuffModelMeter` so priced rows show `price Freebucks · balance available` and Freebucks snapshots survive compact polls.
Carried `freebucks` through `toLandingSession`, `markFreebuffSessionEnded`, the `none` probe merge, and `mergeCompactActiveSession` so the meter persists across state transitions.
Added `freebucksFixture` for client boundary tests with a currency snapshot and no plan or spend.

b8a55e9b61345917b0f8b470e4c02ab4f4956d4f.title: Sponsored compute contract gates model and campaign allowlists
b8a55e9b61345917b0f8b470e4c02ab4f4956d4f.summary: A new module `common/src/ads/sponsored-compute-contract.ts` introduces `readSponsoredComputePolicy`, which gates sponsored execution on three env vars (`FREEBUFF_SPONSORED_COMPUTE_ENABLED`, `FREEBUFF_SPONSORED_COMPUTE_MODEL_ID`, `FREEBUFF_SPONSORED_COMPUTE_CAMPAIGN_IDS`) and only admits compute when the model matches `FREEBUFF_DEEPSEEK_V4_FLASH_MODEL_ID` and every campaign id is a UUID. The same file exports `SponsoredComputeGrant` and `SponsoredComputePolicy` types so callers can consume the public response shape and the frozen policy defaults ($2 acceptance fee, $0.50 internal compute cap, 1h ttl). Separately, `sdk/src/impl/database.ts` strips the `apiKey` field from every `logger.error` call in `getUserInfoFromApiKey` so bearer credentials no longer appear in diagnostic logs, and `common/src/ads/sponsored-proposal-view.ts` adds an optional `conversationId` field to `SponsoredProposalRow` to carry the conversation that produced an offer.
b8a55e9b61345917b0f8b470e4c02ab4f4956d4f.evidence: New file `common/src/ads/sponsored-compute-contract.ts` exports `SponsoredComputeGrant`, `SponsoredComputePolicy`, `SponsoredComputePolicyEnv`, and `readSponsoredComputePolicy`, which gates sponsored compute on `FREEBUFF_SPONSORED_COMPUTE_ENABLED` === 'true', validates `FREEBUFF_SPONSORED_COMPUTE_MODEL_ID` against `FREEBUFF_DEEPSEEK_V4_FLASH_MODEL_ID`, and enforces a UUID allowlist on `FREEBUFF_SPONSORED_COMPUTE_CAMPAIGN_IDS`; `sdk/src/impl/database.ts` now omits the `apiKey` field from all `logger.error` calls in `getUserInfoFromApiKey`, and `common/src/ads/sponsored-proposal-view.ts` adds an optional `conversationId` field to `SponsoredProposalRow`.
b8a55e9b61345917b0f8b470e4c02ab4f4956d4f.unknowns: The change does not show who consumes `SponsoredComputeGrant` or `SponsoredComputePolicy` or when the sponsored compute path is wired to an agent loop.

changes.what: Added the sponsored compute policy module with `readSponsoredComputePolicy`, the `SponsoredComputeGrant`/`SponsoredComputePolicy` types, and env-driven allowlist gating.
Removed the `apiKey` field from all `logger.error` calls in `getUserInfoFromApiKey` to avoid logging bearer credentials.

6c846b9d1e27bda1da35cfbe900f062eefb7e2b2.title: CLI ships Freebucks meter and one-time intro card

b816aed976efe357204d4878122710062c89ec89.text: The assistant now recognizes when a Desktop session tied to a paid purchase is being released, taken, or at capacity, and stops spinning the refresh timer so you are not stuck polling an occupied slot. This only affects the Desktop app's view of your purchased sessions and refunds, so CLI and web users see nothing change and need to do nothing. The Desktop app can now show you the remaining capacity for a model you have bought time with and tie any refunds back to the original debit and the active claims it retired, all without altering how you join a session today.

78d1eebe0a27ffa9f8d4d3b6d38261f19d5acd11.text: This release adds a new /export command so you can save your full conversation to a markdown or JSON file, and it makes the model picker show your free-allowance budget as a currency balance instead of a session counter. GLM 5.3 Flash is once again the default free model, and Muse Spark 1.3 (a Meta coding model) is now available across the CLI, desktop, web, and cloud pickers. You get clearer near-limit warnings, day-scale countdowns for monthly resets, and a one-time 'Meet Freebucks' intro card the first time you launch. Referral rewards now give extra premium sessions to full-tier users, and sponsored-proposal runs use git worktrees with a fresh consent dialog before any code executes. Upgrading brings the new export command, the currency-based model pricing display, and the reinstated GLM 5.3 Flash default.

cc9069e251e8fedd5784c688ce78ccfecd76815f.text: When you run a sponsored task in your terminal, the assistant now receives the advertiser's landing page URL (with a signed conversion token) as a separate, non-instruction prompt section, but only if the procedure explicitly contains a placeholder for it. The terminal card also now displays this advertiser CTA as sanitized copyable text when a run is committed, landed, or merged, and the system verifies the actual code changes against declared outcomes like API key wiring or MCP installation. This affects Freebuff CLI users who accept and run sponsored proposals, and you will notice a new advertiser link line on completed task cards and a guaranteed-clean insertion of the campaign URL into the procedure when the placeholder is present.

e6c61f451394b49df437af776c496a0365474fd6.text: Solar Pro 4 will cost nothing in Freebucks during this Labor Day weekend, then go back to its normal price the following week, and the price shown in the model picker now updates on its own while the picker stays open so users never see a stale price right after a change. Anyone using the Freebuff CLI, web app, or desktop app who opens the model picker during the sale will see the correct holiday price, and if they take longer to confirm their choice, the picker switches to the new price at the right moment instead of keeping the old one. This price change is live today for the duration of the announced offer window.

4ac0d8ab8584d5ada8c2f0bda35ab6b7c974e02f.text: The model picker in the Freebuff CLI now shows your remaining balance in Freebucks (the free pay-as-you-go credit) directly on each model row, alongside the price, instead of just counting daily sessions. This affects anyone who uses the free CLI, web, desktop, or SDK versions of Freebuff and is now seeing prices and balances on rows for models that cost Freebucks (like GLM 5.3 Flash), while unlimited rows keep their existing session count. In daily use you will notice model rows displaying something like '5 Freebucks · 12 available' for paid models, and the active session summary now uses the same pricing logic so the quota shown stays accurate when Freebucks credits are in play; quota-exempt accounts see no meter and no balance line.

88e05db4b26f8e58eca99dbae7cf8ef26f22d0a5.text: Freebuff has added the tracking rules that will let its reporting system measure full-screen, interrupt-style ads called sponsor breaks, which take over the screen instead of sitting quietly in the transcript like ordinary inline ads. The new code defines exactly which data gets recorded when a sponsor break appears, how a user closes it (for example by clicking a button, hitting escape, or clicking through), and how long it was on screen, then feeds only those safe fields into the company's internal analytics store. This is internal tracking infrastructure for the Freebuff service operator, so everyday users will not notice any change unless and until sponsor breaks are actually turned on for delivery.

6c846b9d1e27bda1da35cfbe900f062eefb7e2b2.text: The Freebuff coding assistant CLI now shows a clear balance of your Freebucks (the credits used to pay for model usage) instead of just counting sessions, so you can see exactly how much you have left when picking a model. Only accounts the service has switched to this pay-per-use system will see the new meter and the one-time "Meet Freebucks" explanation card, which appears once on your first metered launch. For everyone else - accounts still on the old session-count system - nothing changes in how the model picker or session-ending messages look. The gate is whether your account receives this new billing block from the service, so the CLI never guesses your billing type and stays in sync with what you are actually charged.

b8a55e9b61345917b0f8b470e4c02ab4f4956d4f.text: Freebuff added an internal gate that decides whether a sponsored coding task is allowed to run, requiring the service operator to turn it on with a configuration flag and to name exactly which AI model and advertiser campaigns are permitted. Only a specific Freebuff model and campaign IDs that look like proper identifiers are accepted, with a fixed acceptance fee and a capped internal compute budget, and if any setting is missing or invalid the feature stays off. This is live for anyone running their own copy of Freebuff today, but does not change anything you can see in your free coding sessions.

d4ee9ca285c94e9348a7da806a9d2b7ecc69807b.text: If you are on the free tier of Freebuff and you are using the desktop or terminal app, the ad shown above your chat input now has a small keyboard hint (Ctrl+O) that lets you open a detail panel with more of the sponsor's message, and pressing Escape (or clicking, or sending a message) closes it again. This does not change how you chat or which models you can use; it only gives the sponsor ad a way to show a bit more detail without leaving your terminal. The behavior is gated per-user by a server-side setting, so only some free-tier accounts see the new panel, while everyone else continues to see the same ad as before.

9f81f91397709452f3b757a035fb9e93d0ab9454.text: The assistant's web version now hides two of the most expensive AI models (GPT-5.6 Luna and Gemini 3.8 Flash) behind the paid plan, so free users browsing at freebuff.ai can no longer start a session with them and are sent to the plans page instead. This only affects Freebuff Web; the desktop app and command-line tool still let everyone use those models for free, because those apps were already released with them and a server-side change cannot take a model away from someone who already has it installed. If you are a subscriber you will now see a price next to those two models on the web, and if you are on the free tier you will see them listed but locked until you upgrade. No action is needed from anyone today, and the change is already live.

3de218cfbec42f26a76cf460205d0a5727735c10.text: When a sponsored proposal (an advertiser-funded task shown to you in the terminal) can't be reached because your connection to Freebuff has dropped, the card no longer disappears or shows stale buttons that might open something outdated. Instead, it stays visible as context, shows a clear message that Free needs to reconnect before its controls will work again, and refuses any tap you give it until a fresh poll succeeds. This affects Freebuff CLI users who see these sponsored task cards in their chat, and the everyday impact is that you won't accidentally accept or act on a stale proposal while offline, since the card simply pauses its controls and waits.

d573b4d0977a99b5bea28768a03e3731c51343f5.text: Engineering added the scaffolding for a controlled test comparing two ways of showing free, ad-style messages inside the assistant experience: one that appears inline in the conversation feed, and one that pops up as a separate side panel. The code assigns each logged-in user to a stable group once, based on their account, so the same person always sees the same style across sessions and devices, and only shows them an ad if it matches their current task and the format their group is allowed to receive. The reporting logic computes the agreed key result (whether a user completed the advertised action) with safeguards so a verdict only appears after the experiment's window, postbacks, and coverage are signed off, and flags late-arriving outcomes separately.

f25d4059b88ff4bdca2e120522d0970fb8d2d103.text: The Freebuff assistant's landing screen now shows a 'this month' option alongside 'this week' and 'today' when users hit their session limit, reflecting a new monthly allowance the service can track. This affects Freebuff CLI, web, and desktop users who reach rate limits, giving them accurate wording for when a monthly reset applies. In daily use, if you're blocked from starting a new session because you've hit a limit, the message now correctly tells you whether to retry later today, later this week, or later this month, instead of always guessing. Developers using older client versions will still see a fallback 'today' message rather than a crash, so the change is safe even without an immediate upgrade.

8870810f21a3f99ee8e7f349bd10e1dce92488d2.text: In regions where Freebuff is offered at a reduced level, web users can now pick from a much broader list of AI models, including the cheapest option available, while a specific premium model stays locked behind a paid plan. The change affects free web users in those limited regions. They will notice more model choices appear when selecting which AI to use in their browser.

0f33961336a021a0fe9943aa72144fec1183c3ab.text: Freebuff added three new outcome labels to its sponsored-proposal tracking system: when a user rejects a proposal, when an agent run fails without producing commits, and when an agent run commits its own branch. These labels let advertisers see how their sponsored coding tasks drop off, so future campaigns can be priced from measured results. This is internal telemetry for advertisers and campaign reporting dashboards; it does not change what you see in the app or affect your coding sessions.

7bdce0946bbc83e804efd99fca98fa2d99b90e19.text: Solar Pro 4, a powerful new AI model, has now been added to Freebuff's free model list (the models you can use at no charge) and, when you have full access to Freebuff's catalog, it will not count against your daily session limit. Users in limited regions (those outside the supported areas or using a VPN) now see Solar Pro 4 as a third option alongside DeepSeek V4 Flash and MiMo 2.5, each with six one-hour sessions per day that can be earned up to seven. This is live today: everyone using Freebuff sees the updated model list and session rules in their regular and limited-mode pickers.

7c5cc043fcad67cd82f362c61bc4c82cae553a78.text: The first-month discount on paid plans now scales with the plan size instead of being a flat amount across all tiers: the entry plan drops about three dollars, the mid plan about six, and the top plan about fifteen off its first charge, while the regular monthly price for each plan is unchanged. This is an internal catalog-only edit read by Freebuff's engineering team, not a change Freebuff has wired up to billing yet, so the actual checkout still charges the old discount until the matching payment record is confirmed. You will not see this in your billing today and no action is needed on your account.

df4b9aa599930aa2b2b9b2bd283089261c4d445d.text: When a Freebuff ad finishes loading in your browser or desktop app, the assistant now also silently triggers the advertiser's own tracking tools (tiny hidden images and small background frames) right on your device, with a built-in 3-second cleanup that removes the hidden frames after they load, because tracking pixels must fire from a real browser on a real person's machine or they get ignored as fake traffic; this only affects the web and desktop versions (the terminal app is left out since a text terminal can't load images or frames), and it is live today, so you won't notice anything different except that the ads have an extra step that confirms to advertisers the ad really appeared, plus the logs now record whether each ad came with tracking tools at all.

7faa16471f65d093f3535980864182ff79dac50a.text: When a sponsored task asks you to run, the Freebuff CLI now shows a single clear sentence instead of a long list of technical details. The advertiser's name is shown in bold, followed by one standard question, and the two buttons are simply labeled 'No' and 'Yes' instead of the old wording. The name is also carefully cleaned up so it cannot hide tricks or take up too much space. You see the new dialog today when a sponsored proposal is offered, and the wording matches what the desktop app shows.

6470ff421860de64df4196f6891f11470625bce0.text: When an ad is fetched for you in the Freebuff CLI, the client now stamps the moment the ad response is received, so the system can measure how long passes before that ad is actually shown on your screen. Every ad impression and click you trigger is now tagged with its own unique id and, where measurable, this new render-delay value, so the server can match the two and spot duplicate submissions without guessing. The engineers added strict validation rules so that any ad event reaching their logs must carry these identifiers in a clean, bounded form, and malformed events are dropped rather than recorded as real traffic. This is internal advertising telemetry hygiene work, so you will not notice a change in how ads appear or behave in your session.

13c3ba7d0b36a754116bac24f76957a3eebb9f64.text: Freebuff has added a new tracking number to its internal ad-request logs so engineers can follow a single ad request across the different steps it goes through, from the initial HTTP call to the later auction and decision storage. This is purely a behind-the-scenes logging change that only the Freebuff engineering team reads, so it does not change what developers see in the assistant, what ads are served to users, or how accounts work. You will notice nothing different when coding; it just gives the team better ability to debug ad fetching later.

df596975d3847f148250d348fada73ef08f30465.text: Starting the assistant now opens a login screen in your terminal: it shows a screen that asks you to press Enter to sign in with your browser, opens your browser so you can authenticate, and then returns you to the terminal where your conversation can begin. If your saved account token is missing or no longer accepted, you see a notice about invalid credentials and are asked to log in again, and typing /logout while in a session signs you out and returns you to that same login screen. This applies to anyone who runs the Freebuff CLI in the terminal and has no valid saved credentials; you do not need to take any extra step now, since the login screen simply appears the next time you start the CLI if a valid token is missing or rejected.

872fc2305848cdcdd0e5d4199e211b9f82831fe1.title: Advertiser reason redaction adds country exclusion codes in v2
872fc2305848cdcdd0e5d4199e211b9f82831fe1.summary: The advertiser reason redaction vocabulary versioned as advertiser_reason_redaction_2026_09_v2 now classifies country_excluded and country_unresolved eligibility reasons as show rules, surfacing them in the ADVERTISER_SAFE_REASON_CODES set without altering the generalize or hide boundaries for other reasons. These additions let the CAPI projection layer report country-based refusals as distinct, advertiser-owned facts rather than folding them into a generic temporarily_unavailable fallback. The change is confined to the operator eligibility projection table in common/src/constants/advertiser-reason-redaction.ts.
872fc2305848cdcdd0e5d4199e211b9f82831fe1.evidence: In common/src/constants/advertiser-reason-redaction.ts, ADVERTISER_REASON_REDACTION_VERSION changed from advertiser_reason_redaction_2026_09_v1 to advertiser_reason_redaction_2026_09_v2, and the ADVERTISER_OPERATOR_REASON_CODES and ADVERTISER_SAFE_REASON_CODES arrays plus the ADVERTISER_VISIBLE_REASONS map gained new country_excluded and country_unresolved entries with 'show' kind.
