f2ddf900349a34acf802d7645accc70840d0a4f3.text: The web search tool now has an optional deep-research mode that runs a team of AI agents to research a question and return a written answer with sources, instead of just listing search results. When you ask a research question, the assistant can choose to run this deeper search, which takes longer (tens of seconds to minutes) and costs more to run, but returns a synthesized answer with citations rather than raw links. The assistant shows the cost of deep research in its reply so you know what it spent. This feature is now available to developers using the Freebuff CLI, web app, and desktop app, but the assistant controls when to use it rather than running automatically.

77a74b9437db605159cf13c57b72d52293a6f17b.text: Freebuff 1.0.686 makes GLM 5.3 Flash the default AI model you get when you start a new chat or write a new app, and adds a new /dashboard command that opens your account page so you can check streaks, tokens, and settings across the web, desktop, and command-line versions. The release also adds the /reasoning command so you can set how deeply Freebuff thinks about your request, and it withdraws DeepSeek V4 Pro and MiniMax M3 from the free model picker, leaving GLM 5.3 Flash, Solar Pro 4, and the remaining unlimited rows as the available free choices. For daily use, upgrading means your next session starts on GLM 5.3 Flash by default, a new /dashboard slash command gives you one-click access to your account hub, and the model picker now leads with the new default so you always reach the recommended free model first. Note: some items in the changelog mention models and caps that the final catalog at the end of the release says are not in the picker, so treat those as superseded by the final state.

78d1eebe0a27ffa9f8d4d3b6d38261f19d5acd11.text: This release adds a new Export command so you can save your entire conversation to a file, and it makes Freebucks the main way the CLI talks about usage, showing your credit balance and prices right in the model picker. Solar Pro 4 is now available to limited users and no longer capped, while GLM 5.3 Flash is back in the default picker lead and Muse Spark 1.3 is added to every surface. Sponsored proposal ads now run in their own worktree in your terminal with a one-sentence consent prompt before they start, and the CLI landing screen shows upgrade prompts when you hit session limits instead of a dead end. You also get better month-scale wait-time display on rate limits, a once-only Freebucks intro card, and clearer model switching so the planner falls back to MiMo for limited builds. Upgrading gives you the Export shortcut plus visible credit balances, the Muse Spark and Solar Pro 4 model updates, the consent-gated local ad runs, and a smoother path from a walled free session to a paid plan when you run out of sessions.

1470aa4e189c2d0347843109e5ec86dbab395402.text: Freebuff's internal database monitoring system used to go completely dark whenever it lacked a specific database permission, reporting false all-clears instead of real problems. Now it runs anyway, clearly reporting exactly which database sessions and statements it could and could not see, and surfaces hidden activity as anonymous buckets so it can still detect a runaway query without naming it. This affects only the Freebuff engineering team, who now get accurate alerts instead of silent blind spots. You, as a user, will not notice this change in your daily use.

6c1591f8a5caf4b189e75bea718139d506c0b121.text: Freebuff quietly switched the model new sessions start on from GPT-5.6 Luna back to DeepSeek V4 Flash, and it also made MiniMax M3 count as an unlimited model instead of one of the rate-limited slots. Anyone using the Freebuff CLI, web app, desktop app, or SDK sees these two models behave differently the next time they start a new coding session, with no restart or command needed on your part. Freebuff V4 Flash is now the recommended default that every surface points to, and MiniMax M3 no longer uses up a shared daily allowance, so it stays available regardless of how many sessions you have left. This is live today.

ebb4deb34adc86dfaa1b4584d98edaf6db889f3d.text: When you start an AI coding run through the SDK, the assistant has to make two quick checks before it begins: confirming your account details and registering the run with the service. Previously, if you cancelled the run while those checks were waiting on a slow or unresponsive server, nothing would stop the requests in flight. The retry logic would keep waiting, the connection would hang, and you would be stuck there until the full timeout played out, unable to escape. Now, those checks listen for your cancellation command, so aborting will cut the request short and return right away instead of forcing you to wait. This means cancelling a run, especially when a server is sluggish, now actually works the moment you ask it to instead of leaving you stranded in limbo.

35eec19e84f06cc0bfef213d204165ac1e9867a4.text: When the AI model provider charges higher rates during busy hours, your free daily usage limit is automatically lowered during those same hours, so the same amount of money buys fewer tasks. A new message now tells you the limit is temporary, shows the reduced amount you still have, and says exactly when your full limit returns instead of making you wait until the next day. This only affects free-tier usage during the defined peak windows and does not change anything about your account, your paid work, or any ad placement.

2fa82f2e26c68a2e750dcdd3515855e661d05577.text: The team replaced several copies of the same day-counting logic with a single shared helper used by their billing and reporting scripts and dashboards. It only affects Freebuff's internal engineering team; the helper is now in place and wired into the rollup jobs and dashboards, but the remaining consumers still need to be migrated to import from it. You will not notice anything different in your terminal or account today, since this is plumbing that keeps the numbers consistent behind the scenes rather than a change to how you use the assistant.

161b864dd4f665957ded8250837935b5f8612cfc.text: The assistant gained a shared rulebook that decides exactly which buttons, messages, and links a sponsored task card can show at each stage of its life, such as when a task is running, finished, or when a pull request exists. This rulebook lives in the central code so both the web app and any future terminal version stay in sync, and it keeps dangerous raw addresses from being turned into clickable links by quietly refusing anything that isn't a safe web address or recognized logo. It also makes each stage report its own result rather than suggesting the next action, so the wording is consistent everywhere. This is internal infrastructure: nothing new is visible to users yet, because no part of the app reads these new rules today.

c200e2d4f1c2dbc77bdd889971d83fb755fb0f53.text: The Freebuff team added a shared set of database health checks that watch for four specific problems the database had run into before: transaction IDs getting too close to a dangerous limit, a long-running query holding back cleanup, a broken or stuck index build, and one slow query hogging too many database connections at once. Each check only triggers an alert once a problem passes a conservative safety threshold, so routine database activity does not set off false alarms. This is internal tooling used only by the engineers who keep Freebuff's infrastructure running. You do not need to do anything, and you will not see any difference in how the assistant behaves.

6c49e12dc09c72d510ee13940ea543ef19b418e5.text: The Freebuff Desktop auto-run feature, which silently picks what a tab does next during idle moments on Auto mode, has been formally recognized as an official free-mode root agent in the system, ending a previous gap where it was incorrectly routed through metered billing and would either fail or show an out-of-credits error to free users. This change applies to Freebuff Desktop users on the free tier (most of them). When you leave Auto mode idle, the assistant now reliably produces a next step instead of silently doing nothing or erroring out.

2afc2b2dfac9a0bcb48e18ccc0c1f720f6f2e6a7.text: The assistant used to be forced to talk to one specific company for a certain AI model, and now it can pick from that company first but still fall back to others safely. Because that company blocked Freebuff's account on August 16, 2026, the system now makes sure you are never charged too much by refusing to use the model if any provider tries to charge more than the set price cap. You do not need to do anything different, and your coding sessions should now better tell you when a model provider refuses to answer rather than stopping quietly like it did before.

f97ca5511b01eba2552e9be7d7332194f5118ca3.text: Freebuff's abuse-detection system used to treat popular privacy-focused email addresses such as ProtonMail, Tutanota, Apple Hide My Email, DuckDuckGo Email Protection, and Firefox Relay as suspicious signals that could trigger a spending limit, even though they are mainstream primary inboxes. As of August 14, 2026, the system reclassified those big-brand privacy mailboxes into a new category so they are still visible to fraud and trust-scoring tools, but no longer cause the spending ceiling to be applied to them. This change only affects how the Freebuff service detects and scores referral abuse internally. You will not notice this in your day-to-day use of Freebuff.

ae35b542f1b2cc0e6e455ef9effa1cdb9ad4c818.text: Freebuff, the free coding assistant, stopped treating Singapore as a high-risk country that gets a tiny daily budget, and now gives Singapore users the normal daily allowance that most users in supported regions receive. This applies only to free-tier accounts whose requests are identified as coming from Singapore, and nothing else about their account changed. If you are a free user in Singapore, you may now be able to start more coding sessions in a day before hitting the daily limit, instead of running out after just one small session.

7c219be7ef6d60e088fcfa9fcd566a798153d57b.text: When you use Freebuff for free and the system has already spent its daily budget on your account, you used to get a generic message saying capacity was limited. You now get a clearer message that explains in plain terms whether the limit was hit because of VPN or proxy use, a restricted location, or an email provider often linked with automated traffic. It only affects free users on the restricted caps, not paid sessions, and it is live today, so no action is needed on your part.

5db7a544be7c5ec414b833a4cb295fa8511b1b8c.text: Free mode now applies a stricter daily spending cap that can cut off an active session, but only for accounts already being closely watched because of their country, internet connection, or email domain. It affects the engineering team that runs and maintains Freebuff, since the change only adds internal limits and session-tracking fields. You will not notice anything new in your daily use, because the code that actually enforces this cap is not turned on yet; the limits are defined but not yet wired into the sessions.

79d6a9de6e44b00e4d484725b74991122ae257ab.text: Freebuff has switched the default and Lite modes in the CLI to run a newer base3 harness for every model in the free picker. This applies to developers using the Freebuff CLI on the free tier, and the change is live today. You may notice faster, single-loop runs instead of the previous multi-step base2 process when working within your free daily allowance, with no action required from you.

871d75810e6732f65067d4bd6faec927c529332d.text: Freebuff used to give every free user the same daily budget, but now it sets different limits based on the region a user is in, with users in certain regions (SG and CN) getting a smaller allowance. Users whose email comes from disposable domains, who use third-party clients, or whose trust level is low also get a smaller allowance. The new limits are lower than the old flat limit, so some users may see their daily usage run out faster than before, but existing sessions are never cut off, only new ones are blocked once the limit is hit.

a0a9a4c80ae8b8aba38b449aa29ad9e214633c43.text: Freebuff has added wiring for three new extended-context model variants - deepseek-v4-pro-max, deepseek-v4-flash-max, and gpt-5.6-luna-max - into its internal root-agent and model-id tables. These entries register the new roots so the orchestrator recognises them as top-level free-mode agents (instead of treating them as subagents that fail the hierarchy check), and map each root to exactly one matching model id. The change is internal configuration only: nothing in this commit reads these constants yet, so there is no new command, picker row, or quota visible today. It affects only Freebuff maintainers preparing per-account provisioned-tier support; end users and the public model picker are deliberately untouched, per the inline comments.

0029f0a29f01837307120b1212694ffaa2899474.text: Freebuff now applies a stricter daily limit of fifty cents (previously one dollar) to any account that appears to be masking its real location or using an anonymizing network like a VPN or Tor. This lower ceiling joins the same cap already applied to traffic from certain regions and disposable email domains, and because the rulebook picks the lowest applicable limit, a masked account can only ever get a cheaper allowance, never a higher one. Live coding sessions are never cut off mid-use; the limit only decides whether a new session can be started that day, so an account that hit the half-dollar cap just cannot open another session until the daily reset. The new rule is live now for free-tier users who connect through anonymizing services or VPNs.

afc8351b5b724273614569816b30691f1fecf536.text: The assistant can no longer run deep, agent-powered web research: the web search tool dropped its research mode, and now always returns a standard keyword search powered by Serper. If you previously asked the assistant to research a hard, multi-source question, it will now give you quick search results instead of a synthesized, cited deep answer. This is live today for anyone using the Freebuff CLI, web, desktop, or SDK, and there's nothing to change on your end except stop sending the now-unsupported research options.

a29a854c99017a698e7c8c673e870465919ec957.text: A new 'agents' command lets Freebuff users browse, create, and switch between custom AI assistants directly from the terminal, guided by an interactive menu that walks you through naming your agent, choosing its role, and assigning its skills. You can also edit existing custom agents or hand off a task to a specialist helper agent you or another Freebuff user has built. This is live today for Freebuff CLI users who work in the terminal; no configuration or update is needed beyond using the new menu.

01bf3cd467fb1a2700c866b3097fff745b3c0f5b.title: Free tier shows three usage windows in picker
01bf3cd467fb1a2700c866b3097fff745b3c0f5b.summary: The Freebuff model picker now renders a free-tier usage line (`FREE · today/week/month`) when a non-subscriber's session response carries a `freeWindows` block, reusing the shared `freebuffPlanSummary` layout so free users see the same three-ring shape subscribers already do. The `FreebuffFreeWindowsInfo` interface and `getFreeWindowsInfo` accessor were added to `common/src/types/freebuff-session.ts`, wired onto the pre-join, active, and ended response variants, alongside `freebuffFreeWindowsSummary` in `common/src/util/freebuff-plan-summary.ts`, which maps `dayUsed/dayLimit`, `weekUsed/weekLimit`, and `monthUsed/monthLimit` onto the plan's `FreebuffPlanWindow` shape. A new `getZonedMonthBounds` helper in `common/src/util/zoned-time.ts` computes the calendar-month boundaries that drive the free tier's monthly window reset. The block is absent for quota-exempt accounts, limited-access users, and older servers, in which case callers fall back to the daily ring alone, and the week/month counts are display-only today with no enforcement.
01bf3cd467fb1a2700c866b3097fff745b3c0f5b.evidence: The diff adds `getFreeWindowsInfo` to the imports from `@codebuff/common/types/freebuff-session` and `freebuffFreeWindowsSummary` to the imports from `@codebuff/common/util/freebuff-plan-summary` in `cli/src/components/freebuff-model-selector.tsx`, then computes `freeWindows = freebuffFreeWindowsSummary(getFreeWindowsInfo(session))` and renders it as a muted `FREE · ...` text row only when `freeWindows && !planSummary`. In `common/src/types/freebuff-session.ts`, the new `FreebuffFreeWindowsInfo` interface and `getFreeWindowsInfo` accessor are defined, and `freeWindows?: FreebuffFreeWindowsInfo` is added to the pre-join, active, and ended response variants. In `common/src/util/freebuff-plan-summary.ts`, `freebuffFreeWindowsSummary` is added, mapping `info.dayUsed/dayLimit`, `weekUsed/weekLimit`, and `monthUsed/monthLimit` to the shared `FreebuffPlanWindow` shape with `dayResetAt`. In `common/src/util/zoned-time.ts`, `getZonedMonthBounds` is added to compute calendar-month boundaries in a time zone for the free tier's monthly window.
01bf3cd467fb1a2700c866b3097fff745b3c0f5b.unknowns: The diff does not show the server-side payload that populates `freeWindows` or when the feature flag for it ships to which rollout audience.

changes.what: Imports `getFreeWindowsInfo` and `freebuffFreeWindowsSummary`, computes `freeWindows` from the session, and renders a muted `FREE · ...` usage line only when `freeWindows && !planSummary`, also folding it into the height estimate.

Adds the `FreebuffFreeWindowsInfo` interface, the `getFreeWindowsInfo` accessor, and a `freeWindows?: FreebuffFreeWindowsInfo` field onto the pre-join, active, and ended `FreebuffSessionServerResponse` variants.

Adds the shared `freebuffFreeWindowsSummary` helper that projects a `FreebuffFreeWindowsInfo` into the same `{ windows, dayResetAt }` shape used by `FreebuffPlanSummary`, importing `FreebuffFreeWindowsInfo` from the session types.
Adds `getZonedMonthBounds`, a calendar-month bounds helper used for the free tier's monthly window reset instant.

bab9f2907dff6c3f090b3ba645f64c91e95e997e.title: Subscription tracking, legacy rewrites, write-in classification
bab9f2907dff6c3f090b3ba645f64c91e95e997e.summary: The post-signup onboarding questionnaire adds a subscriptions question that records competitive products (Claude Code, Cursor, opencode, GitHub Copilot, Codex, Gemini, Lovable / Replit), with the `none` row flagged exclusive so validation rejects it alongside other picks. New exports `ONBOARDING_LEGACY_OPTION_IDS`, `ONBOARDING_OTHER_TEXT_RULES`, and `classifyOnboardingOtherText` reclassify retired option ids and raw write-in text at read time during the admin tally, keeping stored answers intact while folding Discord/blog/newsletter write-ins into `other` and Instagram/AI-assistant text into their real options. Validation now enforces the exclusive flag and the `kind` field (introducing `scale` rendering for the proficiency question) without rewriting stored data.
bab9f2907dff6c3f090b3ba645f64c91e95e997e.evidence: common/src/constants/freebuff-onboarding.ts adds the subscriptions question with exclusive `none` option and the `ONBOARDING_LEGACY_OPTION_IDS`, `ONBOARDING_OTHER_TEXT_RULES`, and `classifyOnboardingOtherText` exports, along with new exclusive and `kind` field handling in `validateOnboardingSubmission`.

4da4570dc9d90c75467c5d5541882cd919481bf0.title: Add Human Behavior session replay env vars to client schema
4da4570dc9d90c75467c5d5541882cd919481bf0.summary: Two optional environment variables were added to the shared client env schema: `NEXT_PUBLIC_HUMANBEHAVIOR_API_KEY` and `NEXT_PUBLIC_HUMANBEHAVIOR_INGESTION_URL`. The API key authorizes ingestion for Freebuff Web session replay and the ingestion URL overrides the SDK default host to point a deployment at a non-default Human Behavior endpoint. Both default to undefined, so a dev checkout without them boots with replay switched off.
4da4570dc9d90c75467c5d5541882cd919481bf0.evidence: Added `NEXT_PUBLIC_HUMANBEHAVIOR_API_KEY` and `NEXT_PUBLIC_HUMANBEHAVIOR_INGESTION_URL` entries to `clientEnvSchema` and `clientProcessEnv` in `common/src/env-schema.ts`.
4da4570dc9d90c75467c5d5541882cd919481bf0.unknowns: The diff does not show which service or module consumes these variables at runtime.

e43fdc88870d851ec92b669dbba00bd5ffe17d0d.title: DeepSeek V4 Pro 08/13 becomes Freebuff Web default and Muse Spark
e43fdc88870d851ec92b669dbba00bd5ffe17d0d.summary: DeepSeek V4 Pro 08/13 now replaces GPT-5.6 Luna as the default model for Freebuff Web, Cloud, and Chat sessions, set via `DEFAULT_FREEBUFF_WEB_MODEL_ID` in `common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts`. The same `FREEBUFF_DEEPSEEK_V4_PRO_MODEL_ID` is wired into `MUSE_SPARK_FALLBACK_MODEL_ID`, so rate-limited Muse Spark turns now reroute to Pro instead of Luna, and `MUSE_SPARK_FALLBACK_NOTICE` and the picker copy in both READMEs were updated to name Pro. GPT-5.6 Luna stays fully selectable in the picker but gains a `supersededBy` notice steering users to Pro, and it is deliberately excluded from `FREEBUFF_WEB_DEEMPHASIZED_MODEL_IDS` because the per-token price comparison between Luna and Pro does not cleanly favor either side. The shared daily premium pool is counted in sessions, so quota limits for end-users do not move as a result of the reroute target changing.

In `README.md` and `README.zh-CN.md`, the 'Best for' cells for DeepSeek V4 Pro 08/13 and GPT-5.6 Luna are swapped so Pro is described as the default for Web, Cloud, and Chat. In `FREEBUFF_WEB_DEEMPHASIZED_MODEL_IDS`'s doc comment, Luna is explicitly called superseded but NOT muted.

d0c7b069051a45044d107598a2ce98ef80d63100.summary: Comments in `common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts` documenting `DEEPSEEK_V4_PRO_MODEL` and `DEFAULT_FREEBUFF_WEB_MODEL_ID` were rewritten to reflect DeepSeek's 16:00 UTC 2026-08-16 family repricing that split the model into off-peak and peak pricing tiers (double at peak), removing the previous single-tier note. The Pro default (`DEFAULT_FREEBUFF_WEB_MODEL_ID`) was left unchanged, but its docblock now records that the repricing flipped Pro from cheaper-than-Luna to dearer-than-Luna on cache reads, and notes the cost argument behind Pro being the browser default no longer holds and should be revisited. `FREEBUFF_WEB_DEEMPHASIZED_MODEL_IDS` was left empty and the docblock explicitly states muting is a product-steering decision the repricing alone should not silently overturn.

The comment above `DEFAULT_FREEBUFF_WEB_MODEL_ID` (around line 1279) was likewise updated to state that the repricing inverted the cache-read cost comparison versus GPT-5.6 Luna and to leave the default on Pro while flagging the cost half of the argument as no longer holding.

90ca26c0745bcbbcd40ea7ac385c031977d328cc.title: Add Cloudflare Worker egress detector for resold free capacity
90ca26c0745bcbbcd40ea7ac385c031977d328cc.summary: A new module in `common/src/constants/cf-worker-signals.ts` defines a pure `detectCfWorker` function that keys on the `cf-worker` header stamped by the Cloudflare edge, requiring the companion `cf-ray` header to corroborate that the request traversed Freebuff's own edge before flagging a zone. The verdict type, `CfWorkerEvidence` record shape, `parseAllowedWorkerZones` allowlist parser, and `looksLikeProxyClientId` helper are defined and exported, along with the `CfWorkerMode` action ladder of `off`, `observe`, `block`, and `ban`, but no reader imports or enforces them in this commit. The detector exists to catch third-party Workers like `pingmike2/freebuff2api-wokers` that pool harvested tokens and resell free-mode capacity, while the zone allowlist is meant to spare Freebuff's own Workers such as `app-preview-proxy`.

fe30ebff1d8856788874e037cf2b741f95b6ead3.title: Onboarding requirement gate for Freebuff accounts
fe30ebff1d8856788874e037cf2b741f95b6ead3.summary: Freebuff now enforces a blocking onboarding requirement for new accounts, surfaced to non-web clients as the `onboarding_required` error after a 403 response, with `getFreebuffOnboardingRequiredMessage` falling back to `ONBOARDING_REQUIRED_MESSAGE` when the server omits one. The gate is scoped by a cutover instant parsed from `FREEBUFF_ONBOARDING_REQUIRED_AFTER` via `parseOnboardingCutover`, so only accounts created at or after that moment are ever required, and the roughly 203,000 pre-existing accounts remain permanently exempt. d0c7b069051a45044d107598a2ce98ef80d63100.text: A developer updated the internal notes that describe how much the assistant's main model costs, after DeepSeek changed its pricing on August 16, 2026, splitting it into cheaper off-peak hours and pricier peak hours. This is an internal documentation change only, aimed at Freebuff's engineering maintainers, so nothing about the assistant or your experience changes today. Your sessions, model defaults, and available choices are exactly as they were before, since no live pricing or behavior was altered in this change.

01bf3cd467fb1a2700c866b3097fff745b3c0f5b.text: The Freebuff model picker now shows free-tier users a three-part usage line labeled FREE that tracks their daily, weekly, and monthly usage in the same layout subscribers already see. It applies to users on full-access free accounts, and does not appear for quota-exempt accounts, limited-access users, or older servers. If you are on the free tier, you will now see your three usage windows displayed together; if this data is missing from your session response, the picker falls back to showing the daily ring alone.

78d1eebe0a27ffa9f8d4d3b6d38261f19d5acd11.text: Freebuff 1.0.687 ships a new model picker and billing meter for free users, adds a /export slash command to save conversations, and tightens sponsorship sandboxing with worktree isolation and consent prompts. The free model picker now shows Muse Spark 1.3 across CLI, desktop, web and cloud while GLM 5.3 Flash returns as the default model, and Solar Pro 4 gains limited-access availability with a per-day spend cap. You can export any conversation to a markdown file or raw JSON with the new /export command. The CLI now routes free-tier sessions through a Freebucks credit meter that displays per-model prices and remaining balance instead of a legacy session counter. Sponsored proposal runs now execute in an isolated worktree with a one-sentence consent screen and per-model campaign allowlists gating compute. Upgrading to this version lets free users track credit-style pricing, pick from Muse Spark 1.3 on every surface, and keep conversations portable via /export, while sponsorship runs stay sandboxed.

77a74b9437db605159cf13c57b72d52293a6f17b.text: This Freebuff release brings a new default AI model, GLM 5.3 Flash, to the free model picker across the CLI, web, and desktop apps, replacing the previous default. It adds a new /reasoning slash command so Freebuff users can read or set how deeply the selected model thinks per model, with the choice saved in your settings. A new /dashboard slash command opens your account hub showing streaks, activity, tokens, sessions and settings across surfaces, and the desktop product row is no longer labeled Beta. The ad rail moves to first-party delivery planes that serve real advertiser inventory with sanitized creatives, and CLI copy now falls back to OSC 52 rendering when native clipboard tools are unavailable, aborting stale copy operations so broken display servers cannot freeze the terminal. Upgrading gives you the new GLM 5.3 Flash default model and per-model reasoning control, a one-click account hub, safer copy-and-paste in the terminal, and real first-party ad inventory served in the chat.

e43fdc88870d851ec92b669dbba00bd5ffe17d0d.text: Freebuff has switched the AI model that new browser sessions (on the Web, Cloud, and Chat products) start on from GPT-5.6 Luna to DeepSeek V4 Pro, and this is live today for all new threads. The change affects anyone who just starts a new session in the browser-based products, who will now be using Pro unless they pick another model. In daily use, you should notice the strongest model available now powering your first project in the browser, while GPT-5.6 Luna remains a fully usable pick in the model menu, just no longer the first one selected.

4da4570dc9d90c75467c5d5541882cd919481bf0.text: A switch was added to Freebuff's web settings that lets the service turn on real-user session replay, powered by a provider called Human Behavior. Only operators running the Freebuff service see or use this, since it is just deployment configuration tucked into the shared settings file. Nothing changes for you today: the new settings default to off, so a dev copy without them still boots normally and no recording happens.

bab9f2907dff6c3f090b3ba645f64c91e95e997e.text: The sign-up questionnaire now asks which AI coding tools you already use, so Freebuff can see who it competes with. If you pick 'None', you cannot also pick other tools at the same time. You can still type a channel or tool that is missing, and the system will quietly count your spelling under the closest existing option without changing what you actually typed. This is live for anyone filling out the questionnaire today.

44212cc2816aedc01e2239edb193a18909727871.text: Freebuff now recognizes when the third-party AI provider running a free coding session runs out of money or compute credits and tells you in plain language that the problem is on Freebuff's side, not yours. You are a developer using Freebuff for free coding help. When this kind of billing error happens, you will see the message instead of confusing wording that tries to sell you paid credits, so you know no action is needed on your account.

c235ded0aec8696b8af0e9fbb9e7fe1529e8bf1f.text: The title bar at the top of your message queue panel and the composer area where you type can now be clicked to open the queue panel directly, rather than needing a keyboard shortcut. If you already had messages waiting or running, you can click the preview text at the top to expand and review your queued messages. The composer area shows a clickable label when there are items queued, and clicking it opens the queue panel for you to edit or reorder your messages.

00e5fa83a7e86d744e826cef0021ee41b4ccce17.text: The assistant now quietly tracks and reports how much computing power each request uses and whenever it shrinks a long conversation to fit within limits. Developers who embed the assistant into their own tools can now receive these usage and conversation-shrinking events as they happen, without the reporting ever slowing down the work. Nothing looks different in the normal chat experience, but hosts using the SDK can now display token usage or respond to conversation trimming, and any error in their custom handlers is logged rather than crashing the run.

b9810f1556b1ad235441f5bea1278b948d119973.text: A new, well-explained set of plain-language messages was added so that when someone's attempt to create an account is turned away, they are told exactly why and how to fix it, rather than just seeing a generic failure. It affects developers and other people signing up for the Freebuff coding assistant through the login pages. When you try to sign up and are blocked, you will see a clear, non-blaming reason (such as an account already existing for that email, or a VPN being detected) and a next step to retry or contact support, instead of an unhelpful error.

90ca26c0745bcbbcd40ea7ac385c031977d328cc.text: Freebuff has added a new internal check that detects when someone is using a Cloudflare Worker to secretly pool free accounts and resell access to Freebuff's free-tier capacity. This check looks at headers that Cloudflare itself stamps on worker-generated requests, which third parties can't fake or remove. The system is designed so Freebuff's own workers are never flagged, and it only applies to the free tier, not paid accounts. This detection is now in the code and ready, but it does nothing yet since no part of the system is actually using it to block anything today.

a6f9f6f9f36afe33900b80d4df2d61d646a8460f.text: The assistant now tells you when it didn't get a final, exact usage report from the AI model after a response finished. When a response ends abruptly - like a dropped connection, the assistant stops mid-thought, or you cancel - the software lets whatever host is running it know that the usage numbers it can share afterward are incomplete rather than silently guessing. It also now separately tracks 'reasoning tokens' (the behind-the-scenes thinking effort) so those are reported alongside regular input and output counts. If you build on top of the Freebuff tools, your code can opt into a new callback that fires for each incomplete receipt, while existing integrations that don't use it keep working unchanged.

85fe163fd7843afe7dc3d07df57d2ac8eade07c4.text: The internal list of experimental models that only Freebuff staff can test with has been cleaned up: two old test models (Ling 3.0 Flash and Greg 2 Ultra/Super) were fully removed from the system, and a new test-only model called Kimi K3 Eco (from CrofAI) was added in their place, metered like the other internal-only models. This affects internal staff who test new AI models before any public release; it is not a change to the models free or paid users can pick. You will notice nothing different in your daily use of Freebuff, Codebuff, the web app, or the desktop app, because this change only touches a catalog used exclusively for behind-the-scenes testing by the engineering team.

f7d35db5a5e064e98c9f12739e68f1583ced9c5d.title: Admission counting and per-model pool labels land in session quota

9ddaa67d28223f14873db3c78e8fd0fbf98608c1.summary:

A new `REGRESSION_FLOOR_BUDGET_SHARE = 0.375` constant scales the absolute floor down per lane using the lane's own budget, so light lanes like `cli_auth_status` (p95 10-15ms) still get a proportionate, pageable floor rather than being blind to a 10x regression.

The change leaves the reporting-only over-budget lane in place and does not promote it to a pageable signal; the commit comment keeps absolute budgets reported only and states they are promoted only after a week clean, following the noise table measured from nine post-private-endpoint hours. The `breach` flag continues to gate paging on `regressed.length > 0`, now excluding p50 entirely so the typical-request percentile can no longer fire a page.
9ddaa67d28223f14873db3c78e8fd0fbf98608c1.evidence: The diff modifies `common/src/util/database-request-cost.ts`, raising `regressionRatio` from 1.5 to 2.0, `minClientSqlWallRegressionMs` from 20 to 150, and `minRoundTripRegression` from 2 to 8 in `DEFAULT_DATABASE_COST_EVALUATION_OPTIONS`, and adding the `REGRESSION_FLOOR_BUDGET_SHARE = 0.375` constant used in `evaluateFamily` to scale the absolute floor down for light lanes via `Math.min(minRegression, limit * REGRESSION_FLOOR_BUDGET_SHARE)`.
9ddaa67d28223f14873db3c78e8fd0fbf98608c1.unknowns: The diff does not identify who consumes the recalibrated thresholds outside `evaluateDatabaseRequestCosts` or confirm when a week of clean over-budget traffic triggers promotion to a pageable signal. A second read of the same diff did not confirm that a migration step is required.

bb7dbadf40439cd9a5159185a4d1a242b68f74ac.title: Root agent no tools signal joins the foreign client detection
bb7dbadf40439cd9a5159185a4d1a242b68f74ac.summary: A third signal, `root_agent_no_tools`, is added to `ForeignClientSignal` and to the detection flow in `detectForeignFreebuffClient`, which now takes an `isRootAgent` parameter threaded through `resolveForeignClientDowngrade`. When a root agent offers no tools, it reports the `root_agent_no_tools` signal, but because enforcement is deliberately avoided over real agentic traffic, only `foreign_toolset` still sets a `downgradeTo` value, which resolves to the `FREEBUFF_DOWNGRADE_MODEL_ID` constant already defined in the module.
bb7dbadf40439cd9a5159185a4d1a242b68f74ac.evidence: The diff adds a `root_agent_no_tools` member to the `ForeignClientSignal` type union and an `isRootAgent` parameter to both `detectForeignFreebuffClient` and `resolveForeignClientDowngrade` in `common/src/constants/foreign-client-signals.ts`; a new branch in `detectForeignFreebuffClient` returns the `root_agent_no_tools` signal when `isRootAgent` is true and no tools are offered. The `downgradeTo` expression stays gated on `verdict.signal === 'foreign_toolset'`, so only that signal selects the `FREEBUFF_DOWNGRADE_MODEL_ID` constant.
bb7dbadf40439cd9a5159185a4d1a242b68f74ac.unknowns: The diff shows no call-site changes wiring `isRootAgent`, so it is not visible which consumer passes that argument yet.

d800f61ca0291aa9270a75e454fb1a4a8ce09712.title: Database cost alert pages only on regressions, not over-budget
d800f61ca0291aa9270a75e454fb1a4a8ce09712.summary: The database request cost evaluator now separates the over-budget signal from the regression signal so that a percentile can be flagged over budget and still compared to its baseline in the same pass. evaluateFamily returns { overBudget, regressed } instead of a single array, and the over-budget branch no longer short-circuits with continue. evaluateDatabaseRequestCosts sets verdict.breach to regressed.length > 0, meaning over-budget percentiles remain reported in the new verdict.overBudget array but never page the alert, while verdict.reasons stays regression-first via [...regressed, ...overBudget] for callers that want a flat blob.
d800f61ca0291aa9270a75e454fb1a4a8ce09712.evidence: common/src/util/database-request-cost.ts: evaluateFamily now returns { overBudget, regressed } instead of a single array; the over-budget branch no longer continues so a percentile can populate overBudget and still be compared to its baseline in the same pass; evaluateDatabaseRequestCosts sets verdict.breach to regressed.length > 0; DatabaseCostVerdict gains explicit overBudget and regressed arrays with reasons built as [...regressed, ...overBudget].
d800f61ca0291aa9270a75e454fb1a4a8ce09712.unknowns: The diff does not show which consumer reads the new overBudget and regressed fields or how the paging integration consumes verdict.breach.

68d9a88c81cfd8b1b1de979ca99eb3468290f961.title: Foreign client signal now derives signature tool set from tool names
68d9a88c81cfd8b1b1de979ca99eb3468290f961.summary: The Freebuff signature-tool discriminator is rebuilt in `common/src/constants/foreign-client-signals.ts`: `FREEBUFF_SIGNATURE_TOOL_NAMES` is now derived from the shared `toolNames` list, minus the new `GENERIC_TOOL_NAMES` exclusion set, plus `FREEBUFF_CUSTOM_TOOL_NAMES` (set to `['decide']`). The `mode` parameter and `ForeignClientDowngradeMode` type are removed from `resolveForeignClientDowngrade`, so `foreign_toolset` is always enforced and `sampling_params` is always reported but never acted upon. This moves the signature from a brittle hand-maintained list to one that updates automatically whenever a new tool is added to `toolNames` or forgotten in `GENERIC_TOOL_NAMES`, with the `decide` tool covering Freebuff Desktop's autorun agent.
68d9a88c81cfd8b1b1de979ca99eb3468290f961.evidence: Modified `common/src/constants/foreign-client-signals.ts` (commit 68d9a88c): the hand-maintained `FREEBUFF_SIGNATURE_TOOL_NAMES` literal array is replaced with a derived set built from the imported `toolNames` in `common/src/tools/constants`, filtered to remove the new `GENERIC_TOOL_NAMES` exclusion list and combined with the new `FREEBUFF_CUSTOM_TOOL_NAMES = ['decide']`; the `mode` parameter and `ForeignClientDowngradeMode` type on `resolveForeignClientDowngrade` are removed, so the function now always enforces `foreign_toolset` and always reports `sampling_params` without acting on it.
68d9a88c81cfd8b1b1de979ca99eb3468290f961.migration: Requests to the Freebuff free endpoint that do not carry a distinctive Freebuff tool name will now always be served `inclusionai/ling-3.0-tiny:free` instead of the originally requested model.
68d9a88c81cfd8b1b1de979ca99eb3468290f961.unknowns: The diff does not show the consumer of `resolveForeignClientDowngrade` updating to the new parameterless signature, or how the `mode` removal is reconciled downstream.

6ace1d00c9409518218bbf90225391e9002a5b21.text: A new timing rule has been added to the ad delivery system that spaces out how often promoted posts appear to a user during an hour, turning big bursts into a steadier drip. This is internal machinery for the advertising side of the service, not something that touches your coding assistant sessions or Freebucks credits. You won't notice it directly, and there's no action needed from you.

e5d41741aeca4ae11989042f2af1647b94c11e41.text: The assistant's built-in way of thinking before it replies can now be tuned for one model (an AI called GLM 5.3 Flash that's free to use): you can ask it to think less for faster, simpler answers, or more for deeper, more careful ones. This affects anyone using the free version of the assistant. If you choose that model, a new set of depth options appears automatically, with the deeper setting matching how the model already worked, so most people won't notice day-to-day unless they explicitly pick a different level.

77a74b9437db605159cf13c57b72d52293a6f17b.text: This release makes GLM 5.3 Flash the default AI model across the Freebuff CLI, web, and desktop, replacing GPT-5.6 Luna, and adds Solar Pro 4 as a new option in the free model picker. A new /dashboard slash command lets you open your Freebuff account page to view streaks, activity, tokens, sessions, and settings in one place. The /reasoning slash command lets you control how hard the selected model thinks on a low-to-max scale, persisted per model in your settings. DeepSeek V4 Flash is now available all day instead of pausing during peak hours, and Luna sessions can run up to 3 per day instead of 2. Time-gated model refusals now show a named timezone label and the exact local return time rather than a bare wall-clock string. The ad rail now fills Freebuff slots with first-party inventory when no paid campaign is active, and GLM 5.3 Flash gains a reasoning-effort ladder you can dial in from the picker.

105640d21d124ff1dd6a7ccd7df06fffb9a5c34f.text: When you ask the assistant to help you sign up for a third-party service like a database or email provider, it can now create the account for you directly and hand back the login credentials, as long as you explicitly approve it first. Previously the assistant could only recommend a service and give you a signup link to visit yourself. This affects anyone using the Freebuff CLI, web app, or desktop app who asks the assistant to integrate a supported service. You will notice that after a recommended service, the assistant can offer to set up the account in place and write the credentials straight into your project's environment file instead of making you copy them from another page; if the service does not support this, the assistant will still fall back to the signup link as before.

a5b6b0cf4ef9fbf7f6cf529e803601f243cd1b0f.text: Freebuff has raised the daily project-creation limits for outer-region Freebuff Web users and blank Cloud projects to 10, up from 3 and 5 respectively. The new limits apply to users who use the Freebuff CLI, web assistant, desktop app or SDK, particularly those on limited-tier plans. In daily use, you can now create up to 10 projects per day on both Web and Cloud platforms without hitting a cap, with failed builds not counting against the quota.

d9ee7bfc3e52b9156522bc86250fc7376f9fe955.text: The assistant now uses DeepSeek V4 Pro 08/13 as the recommended starting model across the CLI, desktop, web, and SDK surfaces (taking effect today, 2026-08-12), replacing the previous default of DeepSeek V4 Flash. This affects Freebuff users, who will see Pro selected automatically in the model picker unless they had already chosen another model. In everyday use, the picker now highlights Pro as the recommended hero, and when your daily premium sessions are spent it automatically switches the recommendation to the unlimited DeepSeek V4 Flash so the highlighted option is always one you can actually start. The documentation across the English, Chinese, and release README files was also updated to match.

b07e38d987cc4aa41a1c0fea1a2502a462f0f50f.text: The new-account setup step is no longer a hard stop inside the command-line tool. Instead, it now appears only as a single, skippable form once when you sign in through the website, and only if the team has turned the step on (an unset switch means nobody sees it). If you use the app in your terminal, nothing changes for you and you will not see any new prompt; the step is being tried out on the website only.

190ac96c3428bfbd1ea3ffbdeaf77659f088a902.text: The Freebuff CLI now stops an old clipboard copy whenever you select new text, so a slow or stuck copy can no longer overwrite the newer one with stale content, and over remote sessions any transcript too large for the standard remote-copy method is automatically trimmed before sending. A 5-second safety net also kills any clipboard helper that hangs, so a broken display server can no longer freeze the editor. If you use /copy over SSH with a very long conversation, the largest tool outputs are removed first with a clear note until it fits, and the smallest summary you'd still want is kept. You don't need to change anything. The fix is live now.

fe30ebff1d8856788874e037cf2b741f95b6ead3.text: Freebuff has added a new step that some new accounts must complete before they can use the service. If you try to use the assistant and haven't finished this setup, it will tell you to complete it first rather than retrying automatically. Only Freebuff user accounts created after the activation date are asked to do this, so if your account already existed before then, you will not be affected. About 203,000 pre-existing accounts remain permanently exempt. In daily use, eligible new accounts will see a brief multi-question form pop up the first time they try to run an assistant task. Once each question has been answered, the assistant proceeds normally, with no further action required.

702b43bf6fbd41be7405bc3e02773f21a7888d37.text: The Freebuff team decided which of two possible ways the assistant can plan and run tasks should be the default for its free users. One way (base2) coordinates a team of helper agents and double-checks the work, the other (base3) does everything itself in a single pass. In tests over 10 small coding tasks, the single-pass version finished faster but left more of the work undone on Freebuff's weakest (free) model, DeepSeek V4 Flash, so the multi-agent way won and is now locked in as the default for both the normal free experience and the lightweight free mode.

bb7dbadf40439cd9a5159185a4d1a242b68f74ac.text: The team added a new, more precise way to notice when someone is routing Freebuff's free service through their own tool instead of using an official Freebuff app. This is for Freebuff's operators, the people who run the service itself. You do not see any change in your daily use, and nothing is blocked or limited as a result of this update.

fe7b8fad52fa2ea67a8d2cbb86638e7e0cbb7cf8.text: The launcher now recognizes a specific Windows startup crash pattern (NTSTATUS 0xC0000409) as a likely sign of a CPU missing AVX2 support, applying this check only within the first 10 seconds of launch so that crashes during normal operation are not misclassified. Affected users on x64 Windows who encounter the baseline fallback will see a tailored diagnostic message, and if the baseline build also crashes on startup, they are prompted to include the captured stderr output in their bug report. There is no user action required; the baseline fallback is triggered automatically when the heuristic matches, and the persistent CPU limitation is only recorded for confirmed illegal instruction exits.

da1f340a36ff033086086da3fe1411e796af2bc3.text: The assistant now offers a single, shared 'reasoning effort' ladder (low, medium, high, and so on) that every model picker uses, so the CLI, web, and desktop app all speak the same language when you ask for a quicker or slower response. It affects you if you pick which model the assistant uses - for example, the DeepSeek V4 models and GPT-5.6 Luna now expose a pickable ladder, capped at the effort the model already runs at, so you can spend less thinking time but never more than the model was built to do. Today, when you switch a model in the picker you will see the effort levels line up across surfaces, and if a turn gets rerouted to a different model it drops down to that model's ceiling instead of jumping up to a rung it was never meant to reach.

68b34fa74dd1efa2451b9a4a6df7f5a15ba2a2b3.text: The assistant used to look for instructions in a file named knowledge.md first, but now it prioritizes AGENTS.md instead, falling back to CLAUDE.md. This affects anyone who uses the /init command to set up project documentation or who maintains their own instructions files. If you have an existing knowledge.md file, rename it to AGENTS.md so the assistant continues to read your project instructions automatically.

68d9a88c81cfd8b1b1de979ca99eb3468290f961.text: Freebuff now figures out whether an incoming request is genuinely from one of its own tools by starting from the full list of tools the assistant defines, and only excluding the handful of names that competing tools also use, so the protection stays accurate as new tools are added. This detection runs on requests made to the free tier of the service, where developers use the CLI, web assistant, desktop app, or SDK to get code completion and agentic coding for no charge. You will not notice anything different in your daily use: the system now enforces the protection consistently on tool-based traffic and stops serving it for borderline cases, while continuing to report (but not act on) the separate measurement about sampling parameters. The change is live today as part of the shipped code.

9ddaa67d28223f14873db3c78e8fd0fbf98608c1.text: On August 10, 2026, the team that runs the Freebuff service quietly retuned the alarm that watches database speed, so it stops phoning engineers about everyday traffic spikes. Who it affects: the small on-call group that keeps Freebuff's servers humming (not you, the end user). What you notice: nothing, unless you happen to be on call, in which case your phone finally stops buzzing at 3 a.m. over noise that was not actually a problem.

d800f61ca0291aa9270a75e454fb1a4a8ce09712.text: Freebuff's internal monitoring system keeps two separate scorecards when checking database performance: one that tracks whether a metric simply exceeds a target budget (which is always reported but never triggers an alert), and another that tracks whether that same metric got materially worse than usual compared to its normal baseline (which is the only thing that actually triggers a paging alert). Because the budget targets were set aspirationally and every operation was already running above them, mixing the two signals previously meant an alert fired constantly even when performance was stable.

f7d35db5a5e064e98c9f12739e68f1583ced9c5d.text: Each model's usage limit now reports how many separate sessions you started ("starts") versus how much total time you consumed ("used"), so the row for a capped model reads "2 of 2 starts" instead of "2 of 2 used". This only affects free-tier users who see per-model caps in the model picker; if you do not use Freebuff or do not hit a capped model, nothing changes for you. No action is needed: your client fetches the new label automatically on its next session, and the FAQ now describes caps as starts per day rather than sessions per day.

204d98237e29a1004f52c2d7d6beac9cfbb9f694.text: The SDK's chat message converter now correctly handles image data that is already in a usable form, so it no longer wraps an existing web address or self-contained image string inside another data prefix that the receiving provider would reject as malformed base64. This keeps image-bearing messages flowing through OpenAI-compatible provider paths without error when the upstream AI SDK passes tagged file data shaped for version 4 of its protocol. This is an internal SDK fix for maintainers of the Freebuff engineering team; it changes only how provider request payloads are assembled and adds no new behavior you can see or act on. You will notice nothing different in daily use, and no action is required.

21d3b7668e7f43c2bcfbcd065b1915ae4329f6d3.title: GLM 5.2 referral reward moved to GLM 5.3 Flash, now tier-shaped
21d3b7668e7f43c2bcfbcd065b1915ae4329f6d3.summary: The GLM 5.2 daily referral-reward pool is repurposed as a tier-shaped reward: at limited access it unlocks the reward model (now FREEBUFF_REWARD_MODEL_ID, aliased to FREEBUFF_GLM_V53_FLASH_MODEL_ID), and at full access it adds one extra session to the shared daily premium pool instead of a model. The grid selector no longer filters the reward model out, the referral banner's unlocked card is limited-tier only, and every GLM 5.2 predicate (isFreebuffGlmV52ModelId, isGlmRedeemableAtLimitedTier, getFreebuffStreakGlmWeeklyUnits) is renamed to its reward counterpart. Because the reward model is now an ordinary unmetered full-access row, full access no longer launches it from the banner; GLM 5.2 (FREEBUFF_GLM_V52_MODEL_ID) is added to FREEBUFF_PAUSED_FREE_MODEL_IDS so it is only remembered by already-running sessions. README drops the 'GLM 5.2 is available through earned sessions' line, and the streak utilities drop their GLM-specific wording.
21d3b7668e7f43c2bcfbcd065b1915ae4329f6d3.evidence: Diff hunks in common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts rename the GLM 5.2 referral-reward machinery to a tier-shaped reward: FREEBUFF_GLM_V52_MODEL_IDS becomes FREEBUFF_REWARD_MODEL_IDS, FREEBUFF_GLM_V52_MODEL_ID is aliased to FREEBUFF_REWARD_MODEL_ID (which equals FREEBUFF_GLM_V53_FLASH_MODEL_ID), isFreebuffGlmV52ModelId becomes isFreebuffRewardModelId, getFreebuffModelsForAccessTier no longer filters the reward model out of the grid, and the referral banner now keys its unlocked card on the limited tier only. README.md and README.zh-CN.md swap the 'GLM 5.2 is available through earned sessions' line for a generic referrals/bounties note. freebuff-streak.ts and freebuff-streak-line.ts rename the GLM 5.2 references to reward references.
21d3b7668e7f43c2bcfbcd065b1915ae4329f6d3.unknowns: The exact server-side wiring that resolves the earned balance into an extra premium session at full access is not shown in the diff; the diff only carries the client-side rename and gating.

changes.what: Renamed the GLM 5.2 referral-reward constants and predicates to reward counterparts and made FREEBUFF_REWARD_MODEL_ID alias the GLM 5.3 Flash id, then paused GLM 5.2 from free mode.
Stopped filtering the reward model out of the grid and renamed the banner's startable-selection check to isFreebuffRewardModelId.

Keyed the unlocked referral card on the limited tier only and rewrote its copy to offer the reward model instead of naming GLM 5.2, importing FREEBUFF_REWARD_MODEL_DISPLAY_NAME and FREEBUFF_REWARD_MODEL_ID.
Updated the referral-info docs so the full tier is described as an extra premium session rather than GLM 5.2, and clarified the rate-limit comment to read 'reward referral pool'.
Renamed the GLM 5.2 stint constants and predicate to reward stint counterparts.
Renamed the GLM 5.2 bonus wording to reward bonus wording.

6a7669dddb1114ca0408761d28ca816510effac8.title: CLI ads:enable and ads:disable commands show and rotate Gravity ads
6a7669dddb1114ca0408761d28ca816510effac8.summary: Adds the /ads:enable and /ads:disable slash commands, backed by handleAdsEnable, handleAdsDisable, and getAdsEnabled in cli/src/commands/ads.ts, which persist an adsEnabled setting to settings.json. The chat UI now renders an AdBanner when an ad is available and ads are enabled, using useGravityAd to rotate ads every 60 seconds, pre-fetch the next ad 5 seconds ahead, stop after 3 ads without activity, and report activity on input and submit. The usage banner now shows ad-derived credits alongside free and paid balances. The web layer gains Next.js route handlers that serve ads from the Gravity API and grant credits on impression, with server-side storage in a new ad_impression table and a serverEnvSchema entry for GRAVITY_API_KEY.
6a7669dddb1114ca0408761d28ca816510effac8.evidence: New file cli/src/commands/ads.ts exports handleAdsEnable, handleAdsDisable, getAdsEnabled; command-registry.ts imports and registers ads:enable and ads:disable commands; slash-commands.ts adds 'ads:enable' and 'ads:disable' entries to SLASH_COMMANDS; chat.tsx imports getAdsEnabled and AdBanner, filters slash commands based on adsEnabled, calls useGravityAd and reportActivity on input and submit; cli/package.json adds @gravity/api dependency; web/src/app/api/v1/ads/route.ts and web/src/app/api/v1/ads/impression/route.ts postAds, postAdImpression handlers added.
6a7669dddb1114ca0408761d28ca816510effac8.migration: No migration is required, but existing users can run /ads:enable to start seeing contextual ads and earning credits from impressions.
6a7669dddb1114ca0408761d28ca816510effac8.unknowns: The diff does not show the Gravity API response shape details or how the ad revenue share is configured server-side.

changes.what: Added ads:enable and ads:disable slash commands with handlers that toggle the adsEnabled setting, register them in command-registry.ts, list them in slash-commands.ts, and filter the suggested command list based on current ads state.
Introduced useGravityAd hook and AdBanner component to fetch, rotate, and render ads above the input, including activity-based pausing and credit display.
Added Next.js route handlers postAds and postAdImpression to serve Gravity ads and grant user credits on impression via processAndGrantCredit.
Added ad_impression table and migration to log served ads with payout and credit tracking.
Added 'ad' grant type and priority plus AnalyticsEvent for ad auth errors and usage display support.
Added required GRAVITY_API_KEY to serverEnvSchema and serverProcessEnv for ad serving.

851f10f5262ed0de613c360e7724ff58e450f0ad.title: Freebuff GLM 5.2 referral reward now selectable on both full
851f10f5262ed0de613c360e7724ff58e450f0ad.summary: The `freebuffCliOfferedModelIds` export in the CLI model selector now appends `FREEBUFF_GLM_V52_MODEL_ID` to the offered model list regardless of `accessTier`, where it previously only appeared for the 'full' tier. The companion validity guard in the landing-screen `useEffect` lost its `accessTier === 'full'` guard too, so a limited-tier user who pressed the banner's earned-GLM action is no longer judged invalid and swapped for the recommended model on the next render. The comment attributes the change to bounty grants being redeemable at limited access, making the referral balance - not the tier - what gates the row.
851f10f5262ed0de613c360e7724ff58e450f0ad.evidence: In `cli/src/components/freebuff-model-selector.tsx`, the `freebuffCliOfferedModelIds` function now returns GLM 5.2 (`FREEBUFF_GLM_V52_MODEL_ID`) for both 'full' and 'limited' access tiers, removing the previous `accessTier === 'full'` guard. The `selectionIsValid` check in the landing-screen `useEffect` likewise dropped its `accessTier === 'full'` condition so a limited-tier user who selected GLM via the referral banner is no longer silently swapped to the recommended model.

fbf092f424327cab5a5086a0cf209d9199dcac73.title: Model selector shows reasoning effort and adds reasoning Effort
fbf092f424327cab5a5086a0cf209d9199dcac73.summary: The Freebuff model catalog now carries a `reasoningEffort` field per model, surfaced as a `Reasoning: <level>` suffix on every picker row in `cli/src/components/freebuff-model-selector.tsx`, next to the existing Images badge and NEW badge. The CLI renders the same value the completions layer sends via `applyFreebuffReasoningDefaults` in `common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts`, so picker labels and server-side request defaults read from one source. `getFreebuffModelReasoningEffort(id)` joins the other id helpers as an exported resolver that tolerates dated snapshot suffixes, and the base2 Free Luna orchestrator updates a comment to reference the shared `applyFreebuffReasoningDefaults` function. DeepSeek V4 Flash 07/31 and V4 Pro run at `high` effort, while Luna reads `FREEBUFF_GPT_5_6_LUNA_REASONING_EFFORT`.
fbf092f424327cab5a5086a0cf209d9199dcac73.evidence: `common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts` adds reasoningEffort?: 'low' | 'medium' | 'high' to `FreebuffModelOption` and the `getFreebuffModelReasoningEffort(id)` helper, and sets `reasoningEffort: 'high'` on the `DEEPSEEK_V4_FLASH_MODEL` and `DEEPSEEK_V4_PRO_MODEL` rows. `agents/base2/base2-free-luna.ts` updates a comment from `applyOpenRouterReasoningDefaults` to `applyFreebuffReasoningDefaults`. `cli/src/components/freebuff-model-selector.tsx` adds `reasoningSuffixLen`, `reasoningSuffix`, and renders `reasoningSuffix` alongside the existing `imagesSuffix` and `NEW` badge in both compact and column label layouts.
fbf092f424327cab5a5086a0cf209d9199dcac73.unknowns: The web pickers are noted as not rendering the field yet, and it is unclear which consumers will read `getFreebuffModelReasoningEffort` beyond the completions layer.

changes.what: Added `reasoningEffort?: 'low' | 'medium' | 'high'` to `FreebuffModelOption` and the `getFreebuffModelReasoningEffort(id)` resolver; set `reasoningEffort: 'high'` on DeepSeek V4 Flash 07/31 and V4 Pro rows and `reasoningEffort: FREEBUFF_GPT_5_6_LUNA_REASONING_EFFORT` on the Luna row.
Added `reasoningSuffixLen` and `reasoningSuffix` helpers and appended `reasoningSuffix` to both compact and column label layouts alongside the Images and NEW badges.
Updated a comment referencing the shared reasoning defaults function from `applyOpenRouterReasoningDefaults` to `applyFreebuffReasoningDefaults`.

55258aabc4592ed2e90fc5d99fd7ae1e8a7bf10b.title: Windows terminal watchdog opt-in env var and gating logic
55258aabc4592ed2e90fc5d99fd7ae1e8a7bf10b.summary: Added the `CODEBUFF_ENABLE_TERMINAL_WATCHDOG` env var to `CliEnv` and `getCliEnv()`, and `terminal-watchdog.ts` now refuses to spawn the PowerShell watchdog on Windows unless that variable is truthy, after still honoring `CODEBUFF_NO_TERMINAL_WATCHDOG`. 80bc9c895dd73f9996ae18af67432e9ae1b09181.text: The assistant used to keep tool calls that never got an answer, which could make strict providers reject the whole conversation later. It now drops any unanswered tool call when the conversation reaches a new user message or system message, keeping the history clean and valid. This is internal maintenance for the engineering team; it does not add a visible feature for users. Nothing changes in your daily use today, though it quietly prevents certain errors from stacking up in agent conversations.

78d1eebe0a27ffa9f8d4d3b6d38261f19d5acd11.text: This release adds the ability to export your conversations to a file with a new /export command, makes DeepSeek V4 Flash the default model for new sessions, and gives you clearer Freebucks pricing and limits directly in the CLI model picker. The Freebucks system now shows prices and your wallet balance when choosing an AI model, so you can see exactly what a session will cost before you start. The /export command lets you save a full conversation as Markdown or JSON, and the landing screen now offers an upgrade path when you run out of free sessions. Several advertiser and billing controls were added or tightened behind the scenes, and the CLI now shows day-scale wait times for rate limits plus a one-time Freebucks intro card on first metered launch.

21d3b7668e7f43c2bcfbcd065b1915ae4329f6d3.text: The referral reward you earn by inviting friends is no longer tied to a single older model. At full access, inviting friends now grants you one extra session in your regular daily pool, and at limited access it unlocks a newer, better model as your reward. The old model is withdrawn from free use, and the on-screen banners and picker now use your earned balance to decide what the reward actually is. This is live today, and it applies to Freebuff users everywhere regardless of region. You will notice a different label and a different reward in the referral banner, but you do not need to do anything.

77a74b9437db605159cf13c57b72d52293a6f17b.text: Freebuff 1.0.686 makes it easier to see how much of your free allowance you have used and adds a new default AI model, GLM 5.3 Flash, across the CLI, Web, and Desktop. A new /dashboard slash command opens your account page so you can check your streaks, activity, tokens, sessions, and settings, while onboarding no longer traps you in redirect loops after a failed save. The model picker leads with GLM 5.3 Flash and removes MiniMax M3 from the free models, and the /reasoning command lets you set how hard the selected model thinks before each turn. For users in restricted regions or on VPNs, spend limits now apply per region with clearer refusal messages, and clipboard copies abort stale operations so a broken display server no longer freezes the terminal. Upgrading gives you a working usage dashboard, a fresh default model that is unmetered, and steadier behavior when network or region limits kick in.

92a6961b894204c5620f9dd77cd2606e54b9a397.text: The command palette now reads directly from what you're typing instead of a slightly delayed copy of it. Developers using the assistant in the terminal, web app, or desktop app who type slash commands or mentions will no longer have the highlighted suggestion jump to the wrong spot when the screen is busy. No action is needed from you, and nothing is renamed or removed. This fix is live today.

fbf092f424327cab5a5086a0cf209d9199dcac73.text: The model picker now shows how thoroughly each AI model thinks before answering, displayed as a 'Reasoning: high' label next to models like DeepSeek V4 Flash and GPT-5.6 Luna. Developers using the Freebuff CLI will see this extra line when choosing a model, helping them pick one that matches how much detail they want. The web and desktop apps already use the same reasoning settings internally, so this mainly just makes what's already happening visible in the terminal picker.

851f10f5262ed0de613c360e7724ff58e450f0ad.text: When you look at the list of AI models you can pick in Freebuff, the GLM 5.2 model earned through referrals is now offered to you no matter which access tier you are on (free or full), instead of only being available on the full tier. This change affects Freebuff users at the limited access tier, who previously could not select their earned GLM 5.2 reward from the model picker. If you are a limited-tier user who earned GLM 5.2 through a bounty referral, you will now be able to choose it directly from the model list instead of having your selection silently switched to the recommended model.

6059b884a999ffb281a0c15913c659f9bc6f5308.text: The Freebuff assistant will now automatically retry starting a session when it hit certain network or capacity errors (timeouts, being rate-limited, or the service being temporarily busy), instead of giving up. You are a Freebuff developer who runs the assistant from the terminal, uses the web or desktop app, or integrates via the SDK. You'll notice that when a takeover was interrupted by one of these transient errors, you now get a 'Retry now' option on the screen and can start again right away rather than being told to restart or being blocked until a scheduled retry.

55258aabc4592ed2e90fc5d99fd7ae1e8a7bf10b.text: The Freebuff CLI gained a new hidden switch that lets operators explicitly choose whether a background safety net runs on Windows machines. That safety net is a helper program that cleans up the terminal if the CLI crashes without shutting down properly; on Windows it was previously always turned off to avoid tripping antivirus software, and now it stays off by default but can be turned on with a simple on/off flag. If you are a Freebuff service operator running the CLI on Windows, you can now enable that helper for targeted CI runs and debugging sessions by setting the new flag to on. If you are not such an operator, this setting does nothing for you: you will not see this option, you do not need to touch it, and nothing about how your sessions behave changes.

3a8cc3135b1201b6403abb26762a309b269c8119.text: The Freebuff CLI now remembers exactly why a session failed and whether it will try again on its own, instead of just showing a vague error. This affects Freebuff developers who use the terminal or desktop app with a free account. You will see clearer, more specific messages when a session request times out or hits a server issue, plus a countdown when the app is retrying for you, and the assistant will no longer repeatedly try the same action when it is not allowed to.

e455a7f11d4caa461b258678a9a3bb975da44860.text: The CLI used special hidden data pipes to talk between its own processes on Windows, but those pipes could fail silently and crash the whole terminal session. The change replaces those pipes with a small temporary file the parent process reads after the child command finishes, which is far more reliable. This affects Freebuff CLI users, especially on Windows, who run terminal commands through the assistant. You should notice fewer sudden crashes when the assistant runs shell commands for your project, and no action is needed because the change happens automatically as part of the upgrade.

d62db1eebd81b366812817ac479860ba7ab066e9.text: The release notes that come with Freebuff were rewritten to list the AI models you can pick from right now, including GPT-5.6 Luna and a refreshed DeepSeek V4 Flash, and to mention GLM 5.2 as something you can unlock. This is a plain documentation update for the public release README, so it doesn't change what the assistant does or what any model can do. You won't notice any difference while coding; the only effect is that the printed list of available models is now accurate.

95f7ba2869aed9e0bd0ef259d86becf75a4ac23e.text: Freebuff's engineers added a new internal safety system that watches how long the assistant's database lookups take and whether they ever cross pre-set speed limits. It only affects Freebuff's own operations team, who use it to spot slowdowns before you notice them, so there is nothing new to click or configure on your end today. These limits are intentionally generous launch guardrails, meant to be tightened later once the team has seen a week of real-world traffic patterns.

372bcb13336cfa7eb8060b1b80208c8a9884fb9f.text: Freebuff has added a new AI model, Meta Muse Spark 1.2 Contributor, that is only available through the Freebuff web app, not the command-line or desktop versions. This model is capped at 60 requests per minute across all Freebuff users, so it requires a special queue to manage access fairly. Nothing you do in your coding sessions is affected unless you use the web app, and even then, you will only see it if the service has it turned on for your account.

e93edfe8d2d61a6b285ed4e7614d50a8c9de8e29.text: The Freebuff CLI's background check for keeping your session alive now asks the server for a slimmer update when you're already actively coding, so it doesn't needlessly re-download information about your usage limits that it already knows. This reduces unnecessary network traffic while your session is active, and if a compact response ever comes back for a different session (like after a model switch), the CLI will automatically fetch a full update next time to make sure your usage counts stay accurate. You get a smoother, less chatty experience while a session is in progress, with no visible action required on your part. Live today.

956dcf938814d5da8af5f2c1c1216f14d1bcd769.text: A new AI model called GLM 5.2 can now be used by people in restricted regions. If you live somewhere where Freebuff limits which models you can pick, and you earned a special reward (like from referring friends), you can finally spend that reward on GLM 5.2 instead of being forced to use the default model. Nothing changes for people who don't have that reward, and you only see this option if you're in one of those limited areas and actually unlocked the model through a bounty grant.

76020951df33514036c99751ccb03abd92b47274.text: Freebuff added a small piece of analytics plumbing that turns each incoming web request's browser/device label into a single, safe, short token before it is recorded. It is aimed at the Freebuff engineering team only, since it only feeds internal dashboards and is not yet attached to any user-facing event. You will not see it behave any differently today; the code sits in place and does nothing until a later step wires it into an analytics call, so there is no visible effect or action for you right now.

7005d45cc1116a842069903738371fc3c64f2c92.text: Freebuff consolidated the logic that decides which configuration files its assistant is allowed to look at into shared, reusable pieces. Instead of each part of the app having its own copy of the rules, the CLI and the developer kit (SDK) now both use the exact same checklist to figure out if a file is a real secret file, a harmless template that shows the format, or something it should ignore completely. This means the assistant is now much less likely to accidentally treat an example file like `.env.example` as if it were your actual credentials file. This is internal maintenance work for Freebuff's engineering team.

a47be121a650358f747794cf743870e75d35e6b3.text: Two helper scripts that run the assistant on sample browser and repository-analysis tasks were renamed so the test-runner no longer mistakes them for actual tests; previously, running the project's tests could crash because those scripts tried to connect to a real assistant account and then quit early when it was missing. This only affects the engineering team's local development tools: everyday users, subscribers, and free-tier users will notice nothing different in how the assistant works. Nothing in this update changes what you can do with the assistant today.

60dd01fe109f976b0e1e7eea23b9bd0e3ba67b6e.text: Limited-tier users can now launch GLM 5.2 sessions, but only when they have a bounty grant that is redeemable across every region, so the unlock is keyed on their session balance rather than their access tier. In daily use, a limited-tier user who earned a bounty grant sees the GLM card as usable and can start a session, while everyone else without a grant still sees the regular referral bonus line. This is live today for anyone whose account holds a bounty-eligible GLM grant, and no action is required from other users.

f28ecce37f526a75beecd2e0c8d82da50630abba.text: Freebuff removed the older, pricier MiMo 2.5 Pro option from its free helper lineup, so the assistant no longer spins up that model automatically when helping you for free. You might notice it's no longer offered as an automatic choice in the free list of helpers, though if you were already mid-task with it, that session finishes as normal. New free requests simply skip it and use the other free models instead.

6a7669dddb1114ca0408761d28ca816510effac8.text: The CLI now has two new slash commands, /ads:enable and /ads:disable, that let you turn on or off contextual ads shown above your input box. When ads are enabled, a small ad banner appears with a link to an advertiser's site, rotates to a new ad roughly every minute, and quietly pre-loads the next one just before it's needed so there is no delay. Each time an ad is shown to you, the system records an impression and credits a small number of free compute credits to your account, which you can see listed separately on the usage banner. The feature is now live, requires no setup beyond running /ads:enable once, and you can turn it off at any time with /ads:disable.

c799255a7afc9de583e6fed26712c5a5ec2c48fd.text: The default AI model offered to people using the Freebuff web and Cloud versions has been switched from DeepSeek V4 Flash to GPT-5.6 Luna. This affects Freebuff users who start new conversations in their browser, not those using the desktop or command-line apps, which still default to Flash. For most users this is a no-action update: GPT-5.6 Luna loads automatically on the next page load, though it draws on a shared daily pool so heavy demand could steer you back to Flash.

a6571b01b1383c6806b1344375d38525846701ac.text: Freebuff removed the 'Beta' tag from its Cloud product, showing it is ready for everyday use, and added a new Enterprise row for organizations that want a custom setup. These updates appear in the Freebuff product list you see when deciding which version to use. If you are evaluating Freebuff for your team or company, you can now see Cloud as a stable option and contact the team about Enterprise plans.

25d69d5854023aae6361a9dbe09ab23090638563.title: Muse Spark fallback to GPT-5.6 Luna and tagged Queue model
25d69d5854023aae6361a9dbe09ab23090638563.summary: Three new constants in common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts define the runtime fallback path for a rate-limited Muse Spark request: MUSE_SPARK_FALLBACK_MODEL_ID reroutes to FREEBUFF_GPT_5_6_LUNA_MODEL_ID, MUSE_SPARK_FALLBACK_AFTER_MS = 10_000 caps the wait before rerouting, and MUSE_SPARK_FALLBACK_NOTICE carries the picker copy. The Muse Spark 1.2 Contributor model row is retitled with tagline 'Queue' and gains a taglineTooltip field on FreebuffModelOption so the picker can carry that promise without adding a second line, and the isNew flag is dropped. Because the fallback must be a model the caller is already entitled to, Luna is chosen as it shares the same shared daily premium pool as Muse Spark.
25d69d5854023aae6361a9dbe09ab23090638563.evidence: The diff adds four new exports and a new interface field in common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts: MUSE_SPARK_FALLBACK_MODEL_ID = FREEBUFF_GPT_5_6_LUNA_MODEL_ID, MUSE_SPARK_FALLBACK_AFTER_MS = 10_000, MUSE_SPARK_FALLBACK_NOTICE = 'Falls back to GPT-5.6 Luna if the queue is too long.', and taglineTooltip?: string on FreebuffModelOption. The Muse Spark Contributor model row changes its tagline from '1M context' to 'Queue' and sets taglineTooltip to MUSE_SPARK_FALLBACK_NOTICE, and isNew is removed.
