A second read of the same diff did not confirm that a migration step is required.

405bf49baa05e2abf854e5c051b36ad54a35002f.title: Windows terminal health reporting and watchdog arming telemetry
405bf49baa05e2abf854e5c051b36ad54a35002f.summary: The CLI introduces a new windows-terminal-health module that centralizes Windows terminal-failure reporting for both the command broker and the terminal watchdog, routing events through PostHog when analytics is initialized and otherwise queuing them directly into the Axiom shipper before draining. cli/src/index.tsx now drains queued client logs right after the APP_LAUNCHED event on Freebuff Windows launches, so a health row ships before the PowerShell watchdog is armed and survives an endpoint-security kill of that spawn for rapid-resume on the next --continue launch. The watchdog is no longer opt-in via CODEBUFF_ENABLE_TERMINAL_WATCHDOG on Windows; it is armed by default and suppressed only by the existing CODEBUFF_NO_TERMINAL_WATCHDOG escape hatch, with a 10-second WINDOWS_ARM_TIMEOUT_MS arming monitor reporting a timeout if the armed marker is never written. A new TERMINAL_WATCHDOG_FAILED event joins TERMINAL_BROKER_SPAWN_FAILED in the always-track analytics set, and the broker's old sanitizeTerminalBrokerVersion helper is replaced by sanitizeWindowsCliVersion in the shared health module.
405bf49baa05e2abf854e5c051b36ad54a35002f.evidence: The diff adds cli/src/utils/windows-terminal-health.ts, which defines `reportWindowsTerminalFailure`, `deliverWindowsTerminalFailure`, `sanitizeWindowsCliVersion`, and the `WindowsTerminalHealthDeliveryDeps`/`WindowsTerminalFailure` types, and is imported by cli/src/utils/terminal-command-broker.ts and cli/src/utils/terminal-watchdog.ts (both replacing their old inline reporting). cli/src/index.tsx now calls `drainClientLogs()` for IS_FREEBUFF on win32 after APP_LAUNCHED. cli/src/types/env.ts and cli/src/utils/env.ts drop `CODEBUFF_ENABLE_TERMINAL_WATCHDOG`. common/src/constants/analytics-events.ts adds `TERMINAL_WATCHDOG_FAILED = 'cli.terminal_watchdog_failed'`, and common/src/util/analytics-sampling.ts adds it to `ALWAYS_TRACK_EVENTS`.
405bf49baa05e2abf854e5c051b36ad54a35002f.migration: No action is required; Freebuff Windows users now get the watchdog armed by default instead of needing CODEBUFF_ENABLE_TERMINAL_WATCHDOG, and those who rely on the opt-in variable to avoid it should keep setting CODEBUFF_NO_TERMINAL_WATCHDOG.
405bf49baa05e2abf854e5c051b36ad54a35002f.unknowns: The diff does not show the consumer that reads the new always-track TERMINAL_WATCHDOG_FAILED events in dashboards, or the rollout state of arming the watchdog by default for all Freebuff Windows users.

81bb087616c1eebb0516d8c74562cd6c4cd3cdbf.title: Block 30 throwaway email domains flagged as referral farm activity
81bb087616c1eebb0516d8c74562cd6c4cd3cdbf.summary: Thirty new domains are appended to `DISPOSABLE_EMAIL_DOMAINS` in `common/src/util/disposable-email.ts`, the array consumed by referral-abuse detection. The list was compiled from prod on 2026-08-03, with each domain meeting a threshold of >=20 Freebuff accounts and >=75% already banned, covering 7,129 accounts of which 6,699 were banned before the list existed. Matching is by exact domain or any subdomain, and the comment notes many new entries are deliberate Gmail lookalikes or single-day mints like gmito.my.id's 288 accounts.

32b7907dfe18e9fd79fac194172c07fcc816edda.title: Terminal broker performs bounded self-cleanup instead of waiting
32b7907dfe18e9fd79fac194172c07fcc816edda.summary: The terminal command broker now reaps its own process group immediately after writing the protocol result, rather than waiting for the parent CLI to disconnect first, which prevents Windows taskkill from blocking the parent renderer thread after every successful command. defaultBrokerInvocation now resolves the CLI entrypoint via path.join(import.meta.dir, '..', 'entry.ts') instead of reading process.argv[1], and createTerminalCommandBroker accepts an injectable terminate function plus wraps spawn and pipe failures in brokerFailure with the new TERMINAL_COMMAND_BROKER_RECOVERY guidance. The SDK's direct spawn path replaced its infinite cleanup loop with the bounded waitForProcessExit helper (KILL_ESCALATION_MS) for both SIGTERM and SIGKILL, so detached background descendants from SYNC commands are reaped within a capped window instead of risking an infinite wait, and the abort/timeout path now finishes tracking after the same bounded post-kill observation.
32b7907dfe18e9fd79fac194172c07fcc816edda.evidence: In cli/src/utils/terminal-command-broker.ts, the broker no longer waits for parentDisconnected before calling reapOwnProcessGroup() after writeProtocol; instead it immediately runs its own cleanup, and defaultBrokerInvocation now resolves its own entrypoint via path.join(import.meta.dir, '..', 'entry.ts') rather than process.argv[1]. In sdk/src/tools/run-terminal-command.ts, the infinite while-loop in spawnDirectTerminalCommand was replaced with the bounded waitForProcessExit helper, and the abort/timeout cleanup now stops tracking after a KILL_ESCALATION_MS post-kill window. In cli/src/smoke/terminal-command-broker.ts, the broker-failure smoke path now constructs a real broker via createTerminalCommandBroker({ invocation }) that points at a missing exe and asserts the resulting 'Failed to start terminal command broker' / 'Restart Freebuff' guidance.
32b7907dfe18e9fd79fac194172c07fcc816edda.unknowns: Whether the smoke-test harness fully exercises the new entrypoint resolution across non-binary and binary builds.

17d6db8ba087352b631923ba3e14852fcbc18b9d.title: Self-update test script and freebuff CLI 0.0.137
17d6db8ba087352b631923ba3e14852fcbc18b9d.summary: A new `test-published-self-update.ts` Bun script exercises the published self-update flow end to end. The script installs a prior freebuff npm launcher via npm install --global --no-audit --no-fund, seeds the prior binary from a GitHub release asset, writes a `freebuff-metadata.json` record, launches the old binary, then polls that metadata file until it reports the new version, asserting a successful handoff and a Tree-sitter smoke run; the CLI release package in `freebuff/cli/release/package.json` was bumped from `0.0.136` to `0.0.137`. The script is a maintainer-facing release verification tool covering the npm-to-binary update handoff, not a runtime path change. It validates the launcher's update-detection, relaunch message, and Tree-sitter smoke path after an in-place binary swap.

f56844fd118df56422c40c55968c247d6253c562.title: CLI guards Windows terminal mouse and focus reports during spawned
f56844fd118df56422c40c55968c247d6253c562.summary: The CLI installs a Windows terminal command guard (`installWindowsTerminalCommandGuard`) right after the renderer is created and tears it down on renderer 'destroy', so spawned command descendants cannot paint unsolicited mouse/focus reports like `^[[<35;187;32M` over the alternate screen. The SDK's `run-terminal-command.ts` now tracks active commands via `beginTerminalCommandTracking` and exposes that state through `subscribeToTerminalCommandState`, attached as `runTerminalCommand.subscribeToState`, with a re-entrant abort check closing the gap between listener notification and `spawn`. The guard only disables focus reporting on `win32` and restores previous mouse/focus protocol state once the last overlapping command exits.

32405d54b26ef83e80be7c091a8c9610c6bf3b8a.title: CLI adds terminal protocol controller for command isolation
32405d54b26ef83e80be7c091a8c9610c6bf3b8a.summary: Replaced the old `installWindowsTerminalCommandGuard` (`cli/src/utils/windows-terminal-command-guard.ts` removed) with a `TerminalProtocolController` in `cli/src/utils/terminal-protocol-controller.ts` that owns focus-event parsing and mouse/focus protocol transitions, plus an exported `terminalCommandIsolation` whose `acquire()` delegates to `acquireTerminalCommand()`. The SDK now accepts `terminalCommandIsolation?: TerminalCommandIsolation` in `CodebuffClientOptions` (`sdk/src/run.ts`) and calls `terminalCommandIsolation?.acquire()` synchronously before `spawn()` in `runTerminalCommand`, rejecting the spawn when acquisition throws and releasing the lease after the whole process group exits via `finishTerminalIsolation`. The CLI router and codebuff client pass this same capability, and a new `--smoke-terminal-isolation` flag in `cli/src/index.tsx` drives the `cli/src/smoke/terminal-command-isolation.ts` acceptance test through a real Windows console.

13b1cfee56ea86d90e68a05afbb0399cc5c062a5.title: GPT-5.6 cache-aware step prompt placement
13b1cfee56ea86d90e68a05afbb0399cc5c062a5.summary: A new `ephemeralTrailingMessageBreaksCache` gate in `common/src/constants/model-config.ts` returns true for `gpt-5.6` models, whose OpenAI prompt cache is destroyed when a trailing message is deleted on the next step. When the gate is true, `run-agent-step.ts` stops appending a per-step ephemeral step prompt and instead places a single resident STEP_PROMPT once at the turn's start via `loopAgentSteps`; for all other models only the ephemeral form is appended per step as before. The shared `stepPromptMessage` builder in `util/messages.ts` distinguishes the two forms by omitting `timeToLive` for resident prompts and keeping `timeToLive: 'agentStep'` for ephemeral ones. `agents/context-pruner.ts` was updated alongside to carry a resident STEP_PROMPT through summarization instead of dropping it. The change keeps GPT-5.6 history append-only so its prefix cache stays warm, at the cost of one extra persistent system-style message per turn for those models only.

31ac8a0f82d45b3a6f82a46a9be1a4c6b8ad3b11.title: CLI lands IP-capped sessions on the model picker and stops polling

25d69d5854023aae6361a9dbe09ab23090638563.text: When you pick the Muse Spark assistant and it is momentarily full, the assistant now silently switches you to the GPT-5.6 Luna assistant within ten seconds instead of making you wait in line. The Muse Spark line in the model picker is now labeled Queue, with a small explanation that it can send you to GPT-5.6 Luna if the line gets too long. This affects Freebuff users who choose Muse Spark, and they will see the new Queue label and tooltip in the model picker. Nothing needs to be done on your end; if Muse Spark is busy, you simply continue with GPT-5.6 Luna without any action from you.

ed26dd9b5f6f9727085a011414d3e8ceb738118f.text: This release introduces new AI model options including GPT-5.6 Luna and DeepSeek V4 Flash as the recommended free model, shifts several models between free and premium tiers, and adds a built-in Cloud project planner tool that lets the assistant design and hand off project plans for your approval before any code is written. The installer now resumes interrupted downloads and works behind HTTP proxies, the agent loop automatically retries when a model response stream is cut off mid-output, and chat sessions properly abort in-flight runs so switching conversations can no longer overwrite transcripts. Users hitting daily usage caps now land on a clear waiting screen that reports the session limit instead of looping, streak bonuses now refill weekly with increasing rewards, and the free model picker hides retired models like Kimi K2.7 Code while surfacing superseded-model replacement nudges directly on the selected row. Upgrading gives you access to the new model lineup, a plan-first Cloud workflow, more resilient downloads and streaming, and clearer messaging around usage limits and plan recommendations.

405bf49baa05e2abf854e5c051b36ad54a35002f.text: The Freebuff assistant now automatically resets the terminal on Windows when the program crashes (hard kill, crash, or force-quit) without any setup, instead of requiring an extra setting to be turned on first. If the watchdog that performs this reset fails to start or times out, a bounded telemetry event (TERMINAL_WATCHDOG_FAILED) is now reliably sent through your analytics pipeline rather than being silently dropped, and the existing broker failure event follows the same reliable delivery path. Who this affects: Freebuff Windows users, with the watchdog on by default; anyone whose endpoint security conflicts with the watchdog can keep using the existing suppression flag.

b5111f885a8e3b737cffff102f353444ea860ada.text: The system that tracks whether an advertiser's promoted post is allowed, blocked, or being reviewed now records a fourth outcome: when a post is outright rejected, it is marked as 'flagged', not just 'rejected'. This status and its label are now defined in the same list the rest of the system reads from, so dashboards and moderation tools can display and filter by it instead of leaving the 'flagged' posts unrepresented. The change is live today and requires no action from you; it only makes the internal tracking of rejected advertiser posts accurate in the places Freebuff operators look at.

f56844fd118df56422c40c55968c247d6253c562.text: When you run a command through the assistant inside the terminal on Windows, stray mouse and keyboard focus signals that the program prints to the screen can now be blocked while that command is running, so they no longer get painted over the interface as garbage text. This only affects the Windows desktop or terminal version of the product; Mac and Linux users see no difference. You do not need to do anything, and there is no visible change for most people, but Windows users who run shell commands inside the assistant will no longer see flickering or garbled mouse/focus output appearing over the chat while those commands execute.

32405d54b26ef83e80be7c091a8c9610c6bf3b8a.text: When you run a command in the terminal through Freebuff, the CLI now uses a new terminal-protocol controller (the old Windows terminal command guard was removed) that turns off mouse and focus reports before the command starts and restores them only after the whole command process tree has fully exited, so those reports stay isolated from your interactive session. This also applies to any code using the SDK to run terminal commands. You may notice the terminal no longer shows stray focus or mouse sequences painted over the interface while a command is running. Developers using the removed `subscribeToTerminalCommandState` or `installWindowsTerminalCommandGuard` should migrate to `terminalCommandIsolation` via CodebuffClientOptions; headless SDK users can omit it.

ae8c38c6a145ee540ec48aea9027714917d9da36.text: The engineering team reorganized how the list of AI models shown in the Freebuff command-line interface is built, so the referral bonus model is added in exactly one place rather than being mixed into the main grid. This is an internal test and build change, it does not add or remove any model you can pick from. You will not see anything new or different in your daily use of Freebuff.

612e2a39e0355c12169f3dd37ce5e3bf09942e02.text: A new helper was added that turns your first message in a conversation into a short, clean title for the tab or chat window, so each chat can be labeled with a quick summary like "Update README file" instead of a long snippet. It is built as a shared piece of code that the desktop app, the web version, and the server can all use, but no part of the app is actually using it yet, so you will not see any new behavior today. The helper also cleans up common mistakes the assistant makes when writing titles, like extra quotes or a trailing period, and shortens anything that is too long to fit in a tab label. This is internal preparation work that does nothing visible until a future update connects it to the actual chat windows.

6e1168a960e83d3c2651c6765b504f45f0d091b9.text: The free project-planning helper that runs behind the Freebuff Cloud interface now uses DeepSeek V4 Flash instead of the previous model, MiniMax M3, and both limited-access and full-access plans use that same model now. Who it affects: Freebuff Cloud users (the web-based AI coding assistant on the free tier). Everyday impact: You don't need to do anything or notice anything different - your free planning sessions keep working the same way, but the assistant now runs its planning step on a different, cheaper, and stronger model. Existing sessions are unaffected, and no action is required.

3e5be71544b2879899a0dea5162bf6f7e8195bcb.text: Freebuff has added a new AI model called Claude Fable 5 as a limited-time trial in the model picker. The picker now shows a new "LIMITED TRIAL" section with a count of how many sessions remain globally and per user; when the shared pool runs out or your personal quota is spent, the row disappears or shows a reset countdown. This is live today for Freebuff users on any plan; if you do not see the trial row yet, the server has not opened the pool, and no action is needed from you since the model is pinned to a dedicated agent that only runs while the offer is active.

a5cb80f3d735b96b63f2fc075689ab4ed9955056.text: When the assistant loads your saved model choice, it now silently swaps any model we no longer recommend for the one we do, every single time, instead of doing it just once. This affects you if you previously selected a model like MiMo 2.5 or MiniMax M3; you will notice that each new session opens on DeepSeek V4 Flash instead, even if you manually re-picked the older one in a prior session. Picking a superseded model mid-session still works for that session, it just will not be remembered as your default next time. No action needed from you; the change is live today.

81bb087616c1eebb0516d8c74562cd6c4cd3cdbf.text: The team added 30 new throwaway email providers to a watchlist used to catch fake sign-ups that try to claim referral rewards. This only affects the system that detects abusive account creation, not your own email, and you will not see or need to do anything different in the app. The change is already live, and it quietly stops new accounts created on those domains from being treated as legitimate referrals.

31ac8a0f82d45b3a6f82a46a9be1a4c6b8ad3b11.text: When too many people on the same internet network try to use Freebuff at once, you now see a clear message telling you how many others are ahead of you and how long to wait, rather than the app silently retrying or acting confused. Anyone who has hit the Freebuff model picker recently (and anyone running an older client that already learned the new status code on a 429 response) will see this landing message the moment their network is too busy. The change is live today in the Freebuff CLI/web/desktop clients: picking a model that returns the new ip_capped condition stops the assistant from polling the server every few seconds and instead shows your spot in line with a short retry timer, so you aren't left staring at a frozen or looping screen.

8553a9efe9d42dc01079c1f7a63907ea55ec77d0.title: OpenTUI native bundle install gets recovery and staging logic
8553a9efe9d42dc01079c1f7a63907ea55ec77d0.summary: The CLI build now sources its OpenTUI native bundle from a staging directory written to by ensureOpenTuiNativeBundle, which seals the bundle with a .freebuff-native-bundle.json receipt of sha256 file hashes and swaps it atomically so a stale split install fails before the binary step. prepareOpenTuiNativeBundle resolves both @opentui/core and @opentui/react up front, runs bun install with --os and --cpu flags into the staging root, and replaces the old patchOpenTuiAssetPaths and tar-based fetch path in build-binary.ts.
8553a9efe9d42dc01079c1f7a63907ea55ec77d0.evidence: cli/scripts/open-tui-native-bundle.ts is a new file that defines the functions ensureOpenTuiNativeBundle, getValidBundleVersion, sealOpenTuiNativeBundle and the type OpenTuiNativeTarget, which cli/scripts/build-binary.ts calls via prepareOpenTuiNativeBundle after resolving both @opentui/core and @opentui/react versions up front in getInstalledOpenTuiPackage.
8553a9efe9d42dc01079c1f7a63907ea55ec77d0.unknowns: The diff does not show which consumer or release flow relies on the new receipt file or how the recovery directory cleanup is scheduled across builds.

ef75fd7a27e09c75d822efcfdaa28b023a03e31f.title: Streak bonus note gates on earned streak and model picker reorders
ef75fd7a27e09c75d822efcfdaa28b023a03e31f.summary: getFreebuffStreakBonusNoteForLayout now short-circuits when the streak is below `FREEBUFF_STREAK_WEEK`, returning null before evaluating the layout height or width constraints, so the perk note only appears once a weekly bonus is actually earned. In the landing screen the bonus note comment was clarified to state it is for an already-earned perk, and the reserved-rows math now treats it as an earned note rather than a pre-milestone copy. Separately, `FREEBUFF_MODELS` in `common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts` was reordered so `GPT_5_6_LUNA_MODEL` sorts before `MINIMAX_M3_MODEL`, and the Mimo 2.5 Pro retirement note was dated 2026-07-31, matching the earlier staged-removal pattern used for Kimi K2.7 Code. The test suite asserts this ordering with 'orders Luna above MiniMax while keeping the saved premium model focused'.
ef75fd7a27e09c75d822efcfdaa28b023a03e31f.evidence: diff in cli/src/utils/freebuff-streak-line.ts adds an early return if (params.streak < FREEBUFF_STREAK_WEEK) return null to getFreebuffStreakBonusNoteForLayout and updates its docstring to 'earned' wording; cli/src/components/freebuff-landing-screen.tsx comment changes to 'this dedicated row is only for a bonus the user has already earned' and renames streakBonusRows comment to 'Earned streak perk note'; common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts reorders FREEBUFF_MODELS so GPT_5_6_LUNA_MODEL precedes MINIMAX_M3_MODEL and adds a 2026-07-31 retirement note for Mimo 2.5 Pro
ef75fd7a27e09c75d822efcfdaa28b023a03e31f.unknowns: The diff does not show the consumer that reads the reordered FREEBUFF_MODELS list or the rollout plan for the streak gating change.

changes.what: getFreebuffStreakBonusNoteForLayout now returns null when streak is below FREEBUFF_STREAK_WEEK before checking layout constraints, and its docstring now says the note is returned only when earned.
streakBonusRows comment renamed to 'Earned streak perk note' and the bonus note comment clarifies it is only for a bonus the user has already earned.
FREEBUFF_MODELS reordered so GPT_5_6_LUNA_MODEL appears before MINIMAX_M3_MODEL, and Mimo 2.5 Pro retirement note dated 2026-07-31.

fe2f293cfec04f7effa3601e4719d8d5583b81a2.title: Windows terminal note now uses bash POSIX commands
fe2f293cfec04f7effa3601e4719d8d5583b81a2.summary: The `windowsNote` constant in `packages/agent-runtime/src/system-prompt/prompts.ts` now tells the assistant that terminal commands run in bash on Windows, using POSIX syntax and forward-slash paths to avoid backslash escaping issues.
fe2f293cfec04f7effa3601e4719d8d5583b81a2.evidence: packages/agent-runtime/src/system-prompt/prompts.ts replaces the Windows terminal advice in the `windowsNote` constant, instructing the agent to use POSIX commands (`ls`, `mv`, `rm`, `cp`, `grep`) and never `dir`, `move`, `del`, `copy`, `findstr`, or PowerShell cmdlets, and to write paths with forward slashes to avoid backslash escaping in bash.

7c831448a6e554c45b87894487ebe7421385045f.title: SDK terminal finds Git Bash before WSL, no WSL fallback
7c831448a6e554c45b87894487ebe7421385045f.summary: `findWindowsBash` in `sdk/src/tools/run-terminal-command.ts` now excludes directories matching the `WSL_BASH_PATH_PATTERNS` ('system32','windowsapps') entries from PATH before probing candidates, then searches `CODEBUFF_GIT_BASH_PATH`, the `GIT_BASH_COMMON_PATHS` entries, bash named in each remaining PATH directory, and `bash.exe` beside any PATH directory containing `git.exe`. Bash is still required, never WSL: the WSL launcher at `C:\Windows\System32\bash.exe` is still filtered out, and `createWindowsBashNotFoundError` now offers only installing Git for Windows or pointing `CODEBUFF_GIT_BASH_PATH` at an existing `bash.exe`. The error message also drops the prior third option to install WSL. Detail: `findWindowsBash` resolves the candidate list with .find((candidate) => candidate && fs.existsSync(candidate)) ?? null after filtering WSL directories, so WSL bash is skipped entirely rather than demoted to a last-resort fallback.
7c831448a6e554c45b87894487ebe7421385045f.evidence: In `sdk/src/tools/run-terminal-command.ts`, `findWindowsBash` filters `WSL_BASH_PATH_PATTERNS` ('system32','windowsapps') out of PATH dirs and probes `env.CODEBUFF_GIT_BASH_PATH`, `GIT_BASH_COMMON_PATHS`, bash names joined from each non-WSL PATH dir, and `bash.exe` beside any `git.exe`-containing PATH dir via `path.join(path.dirname(dir), 'bin', 'bash.exe')`. `createWindowsBashNotFoundError` now lists two fix options: install Git for Windows or set `CODEBUFF_GIT_BASH_PATH`, dropping the prior WSL install option.

f3e3cce8abe081a471cdf9fbd525426f7fba600f.title: CLI model selector stabilizes focus and layout on async access tier
f3e3cce8abe081a471cdf9fbd525426f7fba600f.summary: The FreebuffModelSelector rewrite changes how the recommended model row and focus behave across collapsed, expanded, and asynchronously arriving access tiers. `showStandaloneRecommended` is true only when the list is collapsed or the tier is `limited`, so the hero card is omitted from the sectioned list in expanded full-access views, preventing it from rendering twice. `toggleExpanded` no longer steals focus to the first revealed row on expand, restoring a preview-first model where Enter stays bound to the recommendation; collapsing returns focus to the same recommendation. A `useLayoutEffect` guard forces the list open when `!canCollapse` arrives after mount, and the layout/state mirroring use `useLayoutEffect` to settle state before paint, keeping the landing screen's wordmark promotion in sync.
f3e3cce8abe081a471cdf9fbd525426f7fba600f.evidence: The diff in `cli/src/components/freebuff-model-selector.tsx` introduces `showStandaloneRecommended` (true when `!expanded || accessTier === 'limited'`), rewrites `toggleExpanded` to no longer move focus to `otherModels[0]` on expand, adds a guard in the `useLayoutEffect` to force `setExpanded(true)` when `!canCollapse && !expanded`, and changes `renderedModelIds` to omit `recommendedModel.id` from the standalone list when `showStandaloneRecommended` is false so it is not rendered twice in expanded full-access views.
f3e3cce8abe081a471cdf9fbd525426f7fba600f.unknowns: The diff shows no change to the public CLI surface or model catalog, so the rollout to end users and any server-side access-tier payload versioning are not visible in this commit.

d5ca1376e2a658169fc355905b29159d5af6a85a.title: Freebuff picker nudges Flash 07/31 and one-time-migrates saved picks
d5ca1376e2a658169fc355905b29159d5af6a85a.summary: Freebuff CLI and Web model pickers gain a dated DeepSeek V4 Flash 07/31 row marked NEW, with MiniMax M3 and DeepSeek V4 Pro deemphasized via `supersededBy` and `FREEBUFF_WEB_DEEMPHASIZED_MODEL_IDS`. The superseded notice now renders only on the user's selected row so the nudge targets their pick while list ordering steers other users to Flash, and the picker's width math reserves 6 chars for the NEW badge. A new `FREEBUFF_MODEL_PREFERENCE_MIGRATION_ID` of '2026-07-31-v4-flash' triggers `migrateSupersededFreebuffModelPreference` once per user, moving a saved superseded pick to its replacement while still letting a user pin the old choice afterward.
d5ca1376e2a658169fc355905b29159d5af6a85a.evidence: In `cli/src/components/freebuff-model-selector.tsx`, `supersededNoticeFor` now checks `model.id === selectedModel` before returning the superseded notice, and line-1 width math adds `newSuffixLen` (6) for `model.isNew`. In `common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts`, `DEEPSEEK_V4_FLASH_MODEL` gets `displayName: 'DeepSeek V4 Flash 07/31'` and `isNew: true`, `MINIMAX_M3_MODEL` gains a `supersededBy` block pointing to `FREEBUFF_DEEPSEEK_V4_FLASH_MODEL_ID`, and `FREEBUFF_WEB_DEEMPHASIZED_MODEL_IDS` now includes `FREEBUFF_DEEPSEEK_V4_PRO_MODEL_ID`. In `cli/src/utils/settings.ts`, `validateSettings` imports and runs `migrateSupersededFreebuffModelPreference` once per `FREEBUFF_MODEL_PREFERENCE_MIGRATION_ID` = '2026-07-31-v4-flash', storing the marker in `freebuffModelMigration`.
d5ca1376e2a658169fc355905b29159d5af6a85a.migration: No action is required from users; the one-time preference migration runs automatically the next time the CLI loads settings. If you use the Freebuff web or desktop picker, you may notice DeepSeek V4 Flash 07/31 appears as NEW and MiniMax M3 or DeepSeek V4 Pro are deemphasized.
d5ca1376e2a658169fc355905b29159d5af6a85a.unknowns: The diff does not show how the Freebuff web or desktop pickers consume `isNew` and `supersededBy` beyond the CLI, nor whether `migrateSupersededFreebuffModelPreference` is exercised by server-side profile storage.

changes.what: Superseded notice renders only on the selected row and line-1 width math reserves 6 chars for the NEW badge on models with `isNew`.
One-time model-preference migration runs against `FREEBUFF_MODEL_PREFERENCE_MIGRATION_ID` and stores the marker in `freebuffModelMigration`.
DeepSeek V4 Flash 07/31 is added as a NEW row, MiniMax M3 and DeepSeek V4 Pro are deemphasized and marked superseded by Flash.

0cda526a6c5bbf6cab64dafb874a9774ac1a4299.title: POSIX path normalization and glob truncation warning
0cda526a6c5bbf6cab64dafb874a9774ac1a4299.summary: The file tree now routes relative paths through a toPosixPath helper before the ignore library evaluates them, so Windows backslash paths no longer silently bypass nested .gitignore rules and waste the file budget on build output. The SDK glob tool imports DEFAULT_MAX_FILES and appends a truncation warning when the scan hits its 10,000-file cap, telling the agent the deepest directories were not searched. Together these change how the shared core tree builder and the SDK glob tool surface results on large or Windows projects.
0cda526a6c5bbf6cab64dafb874a9774ac1a4299.evidence: In common/src/project-file-tree.ts, a new toPosixPath helper normalizes paths to forward slashes before feeding them to the ignore library, applied in getProjectFileTree (relativeFilePath) and isFileIgnored (relativeFilePath), replacing earlier inline backslash replacements; sdk/src/tools/glob.ts imports DEFAULT_MAX_FILES and adds a truncated warning to the glob result message when flattenedNodes.length >= DEFAULT_MAX_FILES.
0cda526a6c5bbf6cab64dafb874a9774ac1a4299.unknowns: The diff does not show whether the toPosixPath normalization changes any existing tree output on POSIX roots, and it does not reveal which consumer first renders the new glob truncation warning to the user.

changes.what: Introduced toPosixPath and applied it to relativeFilePath in getProjectFileTree and isFileIgnored so paths fed to the ignore library use forward slashes.
Imported DEFAULT_MAX_FILES and added a truncation warning to the glob result message when the file tree hits its 10,000-file cap.

ab4919394f7cd07cc1f360e48f04b600a1f6d40a.title: CLI re-claims on deliberate model pick instead of silent revert
ab4919394f7cd07cc1f360e48f04b600a1f6d40a.summary: When a user deliberately picks a model from the landing picker and the server responds with model_locked, the tick loop in useFreebuffSession now DELETEs the locked session and re-POSTs on the requested model, surfacing a system message that ends the previous session and switches models. The explicit-pick marker pendingExplicitPickModel, set by startFreebuffSession, distinguishes deliberate picks from background rejoins so only the former triggers the DELETE-and-reclaim path. A failed DELETE falls through to an explanation that the switch was not applied and suggests running /end-session then picking the model again.
ab4919394f7cd07cc1f360e48f04b600a1f6d40a.evidence: In cli/src/hooks/use-freebuff-session.ts, the model_locked branch in the tick function attempts to DELETE the locked session and re-claims on the requested model after a deliberate pick marked by pendingExplicitPickModel, instead of silently reverting; on DELETE failure it falls through to a revert-with-explanation system message.
ab4919394f7cd07cc1f360e48f04b600a1f6d40a.unknowns: The diff does not show whether the server-side DELETE call reliably clears stale rows or only best-effort, and the rollout timing of the new system-message wording to all clients is not visible.

d248ecc5ad5aafd3b80a52ed21c4244e0aa849d6.title: Freebuff skill metadata accepts nested values and clamps long
d248ecc5ad5aafd3b80a52ed21c4244e0aa849d6.summary: The Freebuff skill frontmatter schema in `common/src/types/skill.ts` now accepts `z.unknown()` values in the metadata field rather than only flat strings, allowing publishers and registries to nest their own structures such as the `hermes:` block written by skills.sh. The description field also shifted from rejecting over-long values to clamping them with a `.transform()` that slices the string at `SKILL_DESCRIPTION_MAX_LENGTH`, since an over-long description is a reason to show less of it, never a reason to make the skill unusable. Two new test cases assert this behavior with titles "accepts nested metadata a publisher or registry added" and "clamps an over-long description instead of rejecting the skill".
d248ecc5ad5aafd3b80a52ed21c4244e0aa849d6.evidence: In `common/src/types/skill.ts`, `SkillMetadataSchema` changed from `z.record(z.string(), z.string())` to `z.record(z.string(), z.unknown())`, and the description field shifted from `.max(SKILL_DESCRIPTION_MAX_LENGTH)` to a `.transform()` that clamps via `d.slice(0, SKILL_DESCRIPTION_MAX_LENGTH)`.

changes.what: Relaxed the `SkillMetadataSchema` value type from `z.string()` to `z.unknown()` and clamped the `description` field via `.transform()` instead of `.max()`.

5d8bc0232add269427599ffd4f928ee6a4786f52.title: Referral GLM cached per access tier with cleanup on unmount
5d8bc0232add269427599ffd4f928ee6a4786f52.summary: Referral metadata is now keyed by `FreebuffAccessTier` in `freebuff-referral-cache.ts`, so full- and limited-tier referral blocks are never confused; `getCachedReferral` takes the tier and `clearReferralCache` replaces the test-only reset, called from the session unmount path in `use-freebuff-session.ts`. The landing GET now treats a clean `none` response as authoritative for referral state, dropping the cached value when the server omits it, and preserves cached quota/location fields only when the access tier is unchanged. The model selector accepts an unlocked referral-only GLM selection outside `renderedModelIds`, and `saveFreebuffModelPreference` now rejects referral-only or retired model ids via `isFreebuffModelId`, plus three smaller hardening fixes land in the same change set.
5d8bc0232add269427599ffd4f928ee6a4786f52.evidence: Exports `clearReferralCache` and removes `__resetReferralCacheForTest`; `rememberReferral` and `getCachedReferral` now key on `FreebuffAccessTier`. `use-freebuff-session.ts` imports `clearReferralCache`, calls `getCachedReferral(accessTier)` in `toLandingSession`, clears the cache on unmount, and the landing GET apply merges referral only on a clean `none` response using `response.referral`. `freebuff-model-selector.tsx` validates referral-only GLM as selected while unlocked via `isFreebuffGlmV52ModelId`. `settings.ts` guards `saveFreebuffModelPreference` with `isFreebuffModelId`.
5d8bc0232add269427599ffd4f928ee6a4786f52.migration: No action required; the change is internal, but returning users may briefly lose the cached GLM banner on first landing after the update until the next clean `none` response arrives.
5d8bc0232add269427599ffd4f928ee6a4786f52.unknowns: The exact consumer ordering of full- versus limited-tier cache population on a fresh multi-tier sign-in is not specified.

changes.what: Referral cache now stores and retrieves referral blocks per access tier; renamed test-only reset to `clearReferralCache`.
Imports and calls `clearReferralCache` on unmount, passes the access tier to `getCachedReferral`, and treats a clean `none` response as the authoritative referral signal.
Referral-only GLM selection is accepted as valid while unlocked via `isFreebuffGlmV52ModelId`, so a transient POST retry keeps GLM selected.
`saveFreebuffModelPreference` now validates the model id with `isFreebuffModelId`, refusing to persist referral-only or retired selections.
`resolveFreebuffModelForAccessTier` now returns the referral-only GLM id through a dedicated branch, surfacing its type as a union.

13b1cfee56ea86d90e68a05afbb0399cc5c062a5.text: When you use a specific newer model (GPT-5.6) with the Freebuff coding assistant, the way your conversation history is managed has changed. Previously, a reusable set of instructions was re-sent with every message the assistant processed, which caused that model's internal cache to reset frequently and made it slower. Now, for this model only, those instructions are sent once at the start of your turn and kept in the history unchanged, so the cache stays warm and the assistant can reuse prior work. If you use GPT-5.6, you may notice faster, more consistent responses during longer coding tasks. Users of other models are not affected by this change.

d5ca1376e2a658169fc355905b29159d5af6a85a.text: A newer, better free way to write code with the assistant quietly became the one most people will start with. If you were already using MiniMax M3 or DeepSeek V4 Pro, you may see a note telling you that DeepSeek V4 Flash is now a better default for most tasks, and your next session will start from Flash unless you deliberately switch back. New users are guided to Flash from the start, and it's labeled as a fresh release so you know it's a newer version of that option. No action is needed: the assistant simply starts you on the improved default, and you can still pick the other options any time you want.

32b7907dfe18e9fd79fac194172c07fcc816edda.text: When the assistant runs a terminal command behind the scenes, it spins up a temporary helper process to manage that command and then clean it up. Previously, after a command finished, the helper waited for the main terminal window to disconnect before cleaning up its own leftover pieces, which could freeze the terminal, especially on Windows, every time a command succeeded. The helper now cleans itself up immediately after passing the command result back, so the terminal no longer freezes, and the parent program does not have to wait or worry about orphaned helper processes lingering afterward. This affects everyone using the terminal tools today, and you will notice that running terminal commands feels smoother and no longer occasionally hangs at the end, particularly on Windows systems.

ef75fd7a27e09c75d822efcfdaa28b023a03e31f.text: Weekly freebie unlocked: your perk message now waits until you've actually kept a streak for a full week, instead of appearing too early or crowding a smaller terminal window. Freebuff users on free tiers see this change directly in the landing screen when they open the app. In daily use, you'll notice the extra note only shows up after you've earned the weekly bonus, and the model list now shows Luna ahead of MiniMax so the recommended order matches the latest lineup.

f3e3cce8abe081a471cdf9fbd525426f7fba600f.text: The Freebuff model picker (the menu where you choose which AI model to use) has gotten small but important fixes to how it opens and behaves, especially when your account's access tier loads a moment after the menu appears. It now opens fully when it only has two models to show so nothing gets hidden behind a toggle, keeps the highlight on the recommended model when you expand the list instead of jumping to a different one, and returns to that same recommendation when you collapse it again. Anyone using the Freebuff CLI or web/desktop assistant who sees the model picker is affected, and you will notice the menu simply opens correctly and keeps focus on the model you would likely start with instead of flickering or hiding options.

7c831448a6e554c45b87894487ebe7421385045f.text: When the assistant needs to run a command on a Windows computer, it now looks harder for Git Bash first and no longer falls back to the Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL). The WSL shortcut that Windows sometimes installs gets ignored, so the assistant won't accidentally try to use it. This affects anyone using the Freebuff coding assistant on a Windows machine, especially when running terminal commands. If Git Bash can't be found, you'll get a simpler error message that only suggests installing Git for Windows or pointing to a bash.exe you already have.

ed26dd9b5f6f9727085a011414d3e8ceb738118f.text: Freebuff version 1.0.685 introduces new AI model choices and several reliability fixes for coding with AI. The free list of AI models now includes GPT-5.6 Luna and DeepSeek V4 Flash, with DeepSeek V4 Pro set as the recommended default, while older or costlier models like Kimi K2.7 Code were removed to keep the service sustainable, so users get a clearer, more affordable selection when picking a model. Downloads now retry automatically after network hiccups and resume partial files through HTTP proxies, so installations and updates are less likely to fail on unstable connections. When you start a new or resumed chat, any in-progress AI work from the previous chat is properly stopped before saving, preventing your conversation history from getting mixed up or overwritten. Long-running agent tasks now pause and resume smoothly when interrupted, and the app shows a transient retrying message so you know the assistant is recovering rather than hanging. The desktop app also now displays active session windows, enforces concurrency limits across multiple sessions, and routes premium model access through a shared daily pool so capacity is used fairly.

d248ecc5ad5aafd3b80a52ed21c4244e0aa849d6.text: Skill cards now accept richer information instead of flat text, and overlong descriptions get trimmed rather than breaking the card. The change affects internal skill metadata handling by the publishing tools that assemble skill cards, not the Freebuff service itself. You won't notice anything different today since this is behind-the-scenes work that prepares the system for future skill card updates.

5d8bc0232add269427599ffd4f928ee6a4786f52.text: Freebuff now keeps a separate, correctly-labeled note of each referral reward you've earned, so the GLM 5.2 banner and invite link behave correctly whether you're on the free limited plan or the full free tier, and the cached referral info is cleared the moment your session ends instead of lingering and showing stale rewards. Who it affects is Freebuff users on the free tiers (limited and full access) who see the referral banner in the model picker.

ab4919394f7cd07cc1f360e48f04b600a1f6d40a.text: When you click a specific AI model to switch to while you already have an active session, the assistant now ends your current session and moves you to the model you picked, telling you what happened instead of quietly ignoring your choice. The fix targets anyone using the Freebuff CLI, web, or desktop app who tries to switch models during an active session. You will notice that your deliberate model choice is honored and you get a clear message if the switch could not be completed, instead of silently staying on the old model.

0cda526a6c5bbf6cab64dafb874a9774ac1a4299.text: The assistant's file scanner now treats Windows-style file paths (with backslashes) the same as standard paths (with forward slashes), so hidden folders like build output or installed libraries are correctly skipped instead of accidentally being scanned and slowing things down. When a project has more than 10,000 files, the scanner now quietly stops and tells you it only checked the top part of your project, rather than silently missing files in deeper folders. If you work on large or Windows-based projects, your file searches will be more accurate and you'll get a heads-up when results might be incomplete; everyone else won't notice any difference.

17d6db8ba087352b631923ba3e14852fcbc18b9d.text: A maintainer-only test script was added to verify that the assistant's automatic update mechanism works correctly when publishing new versions, ensuring the old version can smoothly hand off to the new one while keeping the terminal-based code analysis tool functional throughout the swap. This is internal release tooling for the engineering team, not something that changes how you use the assistant today.

fe2f293cfec04f7effa3601e4719d8d5583b81a2.text: When you ask the assistant to use terminal commands on a Windows computer, it now understands that those commands run in bash, the same language used on Mac and Linux, instead of the special Windows-only command tools. This means the assistant will use standard commands like typing 'ls' to list files and 'rm' to delete them, rather than the confusing Windows versions like 'dir' and 'del', and it will write file locations using forward slashes like 'C:/Users/me/projects/my-project' to prevent mistakes. This change only affects you when you are using the assistant on a Windows machine and it needs to run commands in your computer's terminal to accomplish a task.

cef358330ebed218abe3c1d8df88a8d4bb8315db.title: Add limited tier model substitution check for free mode

This splits incoming `toolResults` into `fresh` and duplicates by checking each `toolCallId` against existing `tool` messages in `messageHistory`, so that retried SDK calls no longer double-append the same result. Previously the code pushed `action.toolResults` directly, which produced duplicate `tool_call_id` entries that strict providers rejected with a 400 on every later turn.
c9bdd9c7b58e05b498d296cf64fcaaa3db54890d.evidence: In `packages/agent-runtime/src/main-prompt.ts`, `callMainPrompt` now calls `dedupeClientToolResults` from `./util/messages` instead of pushing `action.toolResults` directly, warning with 'Skipped client tool results for already-answered tool calls'. In `packages/agent-runtime/src/util/messages.ts`, the exported `dedupeClientToolResults` splits `toolResults` into `fresh` and duplicates by matching `toolCallId` against existing `tool` messages in `messageHistory`.
c9bdd9c7b58e05b498d296cf64fcaaa3db54890d.migration: No migration is required; the runtime silently drops duplicate tool results and warns when it does.

3c92d4e7bd963920744771f9af70a7740f5db53b.title: Base-chat spawns context-pruner before each step
3c92d4e7bd963920744771f9af70a7740f5db53b.summary: The `base-chat` conversational agent gains a `handleSteps` generator that spawns the `context-pruner` subagent inline before every step, sizing the prune budget to the model this step will use. It computes `maxContextLength` as floor(window * 0.4) from an inline `CONTEXT_WINDOWS` map that mirrors the exported `FREEBUFF_MODEL_CONTEXT_WINDOWS` table in `common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts`, falling back to `FREEBUFF_DEFAULT_CONTEXT_WINDOW` (131072) for unmeasured models. The runtime now passes `model: template.model` into the handleSteps invocation context, and `AgentStepContext` plus the `StepHandler` type both gained an optional `model` field so serialized generators can read the per-request model instead of closing over request-time state. This lets a thread grown on a large-window model get summarized down on the first step after a mid-thread model switch rather than being rejected forever.
3c92d4e7bd963920744771f9af70a7740f5db53b.evidence: agents/base-chat.ts adds a handleSteps generator that yields `spawn_agent_inline` with `agent_type: 'context-pruner'` and params `{ maxContextLength, cacheExpiryMs: CACHE_EXPIRY_MS }` before each `yield 'STEP'`, reads `model` from the step context, and inlines a CONTEXT_WINDOWS map; common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts exports `FREEBUFF_MODEL_CONTEXT_WINDOWS` and `FREEBUFF_DEFAULT_CONTEXT_WINDOW`; run-programmatic-step.ts passes `model: template.model` into the handleSteps context; agents/types/agent-definition.ts and common/src/templates/initial-agents-dir/types/agent-definition.ts add model?: string to `AgentStepContext`; common/src/types/agent-template.ts adds model?: string to the StepHandler context.
3c92d4e7bd963920744771f9af70a7740f5db53b.unknowns: The diff does not show the context-pruner agent's own definition or parameters beyond `maxContextLength` and `cacheExpiryMs`. A second read of the same diff did not confirm that a migration step is required.

changes.what: Added handleSteps generator spawning context-pruner before each step with model-sized prune budget.
Exported FREEBUFF_MODEL_CONTEXT_WINDOWS reference table and FREEBUFF_DEFAULT_CONTEXT_WINDOW fallback.
Passed template.model into the handleSteps invocation context.
Added optional model field to AgentStepContext.
Mirrored the AgentStepContext model field in the template copy.
Added optional model field to the StepHandler context type.

5b8b58dbe1bc8498ac86a6e8aaa8e6311e86331f.text: The referral program now gives you one GLM 5.2 session per day for every friend you refer, with no upper limit on how many sessions you can earn. Previously there was a 10 session per day cap, but that was removed on July 30, 2026, so you can keep inviting friends and earning more daily GLM sessions. The old premium menu option for GLM 5.2 was also removed from the picker, but if you already started a session on it before that date it will still work and bill against your regular daily allowance until it ends. If you use Freebuff on the free tier this affects how you unlock the GLM 5.2 model, and the change is live today for all users.

77a74b9437db605159cf13c57b72d52293a6f17b.text: Freebuff 1.0.686 makes GLM 5.3 Flash the new default free AI model across the CLI, Desktop, and Web app, and adds a new /reasoning command letting you control how hard the model thinks on a per-model basis. The update also introduces /dashboard, a new slash command that opens your Freebuff account page showing streaks, activity, tokens, and sessions, and it gives you direct links to the referral status and trust engagement pages. Safety-wise, the CLI no longer lets a cloned repository hijack your session by injecting steering environment variables, and clipboard copies now time out and abort properly so a broken display server cannot freeze the terminal. Spend limits and model availability have been reworked so restricted accounts see clearer, consistent refusal messages tied to specific behaviors like VPN or proxy usage rather than generic errors. If you are on a limited region or use privacy email providers like ProtonMail or Apple Hide-My-Email, you will no longer face artificial spend caps, while referral-abuse accounts using disposable mail providers are newly blocked. Upgrading means you get a stronger default free model, a faster way to check your usage, a safer sandbox that resists repo-based CLI hijacking, and clearer messaging when a model or quota is restricted.

cef358330ebed218abe3c1d8df88a8d4bb8315db.text: The assistant no longer offers the Flash model as a free, limited-time option after that model left the program on August 18, 2026, and it now quietly swaps in the correct remaining limited model instead of accidentally charging your account for it. When a free session is sent to a root that was built around Flash, the system checks that the request is carrying exactly that limited model and is being run by a Freebuff-owned agent it actually recognizes, and only then keeps it free; anything else is rejected so it cannot escalate into a paid path. This is internal plumbing only, so you will not see a new menu item or a faster chat, but if you use the free tier and hit a limited model, the switch to its replacement happens without asking you to re-link your account or pick a model by hand.

ed26dd9b5f6f9727085a011414d3e8ceb738118f.text: Freebuff 1.0.685 adds new AI models you can chat with, makes the model picker easier to read, and improves how your chats and sessions stay in sync when you switch between them. New models now available include GPT-5.6 Luna and Ling 3.0 Flash, while the recommended default model on the CLI is now DeepSeek V4 Pro, and the referral-reward GLM 5.2 session pool now resets daily instead of weekly. The landing screen now shows how many sessions you have left this week or today based on your plan, and if you deliberately pick a model that gets locked, the CLI explains why instead of silently switching you back. When you start a new chat or resume one while something is already running, the old run is cleanly stopped so it won't overwrite or corrupt the wrong conversation. The model picker layout was reworked so the recommended model, session counter, and banners all fit neatly together without shrinking your terminal window, and images from multimodal models now show a compact indicator on the same line. Upgrading keeps your existing saved model preferences but automatically moves any picks that point to retired or superseded models (like the removed Kimi K2.7 Code and MiniMax M3) to their current replacements, so your next session uses a supported model without you having to pick it again.

f5526661a4291076b5784de328a4ddb405831935.text: Freebuff changed the GLM 5.2 referral reward from a weekly reset (one set of bonus AI sessions delivered every seven days) to a daily reset (one fresh set of bonus AI sessions delivered every day), so your earned sessions now refill each morning instead of once a week. Anyone who has access to the GLM 5.2 model through inviting friends is affected, and you will notice the countdown on your reward card now says "available today" and refills sooner. No action is required from you; updating your app will show the new daily schedule.

1ba142d747a1c095f2be79abe6b6adefad0c2a28.text: The desktop app now enforces a clear split on how many AI chats you can juggle at once: one for the most powerful models, and up to three for the lighter, faster ones. This applies only to you if you use the desktop app and open multiple sessions at the same time; the web version and terminal tool are unchanged. Today, when you open a second top-tier model it will switch you to an unlimited model or point you back to the running session, so you always know what's available.

075723dbdc661304e710e2b305277f3acfef3101.text: The GLM 5.2 model offered by CrofAI has stopped counting against its own tiny one-session-per-day limit, and now uses the same shared daily allowance that covers all other premium models like MiniMax M3 and Kimi. This makes the model far easier to use each day for Web and Cloud users who have premium access, while the separate referral-only GLM 5.2 route keeps its own weekly limit untouched. Users will no longer hit a wall after a single GLM 5.2 session in a day, instead drawing from the same pool of daily premium sessions they already use. No action is required, and the change applies today to anyone selecting this model from the Freebuff web or desktop picker.

ff0629f1f1b73fec52d0107117f3c27cc46c389f.text: The SDK now lets hosts that run many coding sessions over the same project files build a one-time index of those files instead of re-parsing them on every run. This skips the tree-sitter parsing step, which reduces the CPU and memory work the assistant does per session. The feature is live for hosts that pass projectFiles to the SDK run call, and existing callers need no changes. For you as a developer using Freebuff, it means faster startup and less memory use on repeated runs over the same files, with no action required on your part.

c8e487a6246813b34d1f8a6942bef69352c80bc4.text: The assistant that plans a Freebuff Cloud project now uses MiniMax M3 for the planning conversation, and a separate DeepSeek V4 Pro model for the build step that actually writes the code, with the planning conversation capped at 12 turns. This affects Freebuff Cloud users starting a blank custom-stack project, especially those in limited regions who get their own restricted model variant. You will notice nothing yet, because these constants are defined but not yet wired into the live Cloud build flow, so the plan is in place and does nothing until the build service starts reading them.

65f20efb85fbaa7d2ec42f484fbbf9b39c57f751.text: CrofAI GLM 5.2, a new premium model, is now selectable in the web picker for full-access Freebuff users, and it comes with its own strict daily limit of one session per Pacific day, separate from the normal shared premium allowance. If you are a full-access web user, you can now choose it and get exactly one of its sessions each day on top of your usual premium sessions; if you are on a limited or restricted regional plan, it will not appear for you at all because the model is gated by region and access tier. Nothing changes for the CLI or desktop app, and there is no action for you to take; the model simply shows up as a new premium option in the web picker today.

9b8ffc8ef8c48601dc234a57e45ebc83b498a5f5.text: The Freebuff Cloud custom-stack planner, which helps plan tasks for the assistant, has switched from using MiniMax M3 to DeepSeek V4 Pro. This affects Freebuff's cloud infrastructure that selects and runs the best model for planning complex coding tasks. You don't need to do anything differently; when you start a build in the Freebuff web or desktop app, the planner behind the scenes will now use DeepSeek V4 Pro instead of MiniMax M3, which may result in slightly different planning behavior for your coding tasks.

801a9d02c935e19c2f9529d1330b0de6eac555c4.text: The assistant now skips asking a language model to summarize terminal command output when that output is short enough to read directly, and instead just returns the raw output as-is. This affects developers using the Freebuff CLI, web assistant, desktop app, or SDK who watch the assistant run terminal commands during coding tasks. In daily use, commands with short output appear and finish faster because the assistant no longer wastes a language-model round-trip to compress something you could already read in one glance; long outputs, like full test runs or build logs, are still summarized as before.

3c92d4e7bd963920744771f9af70a7740f5db53b.text: The conversational assistant behind freebuff.com/chat now automatically runs an internal summarization step before every turn, sizing how much of your chat history to keep based on which AI model will handle that specific turn. If you switch models mid-conversation, the assistant trims the accumulated chat to fit the new model's limit on the first step after the switch, instead of failing to continue the conversation at all. This affects you whenever you use the web chat interface. You should notice that long conversations stay usable and don't get cut off or refused when you switch between available models, with no action needed on your part. This is live today.

8e956567928c769287011b3a1b8974d8d646631a.text: The engineering team updated the internal test setup so that running the project's automated checks works reliably in a brand-new copy of the code, fixing a problem where dozens of tests were silently failing to run before they even started. This is purely internal tooling and documentation; it does not change anything you see or do while coding with the assistant. You do not need to do anything differently, and your daily experience remains exactly the same.

25b2071a417f2e28570f4f40d4cfede17d45a0e7.text: The team added a set of math helpers that group how fast the assistant starts replying into buckets, so they can later add up speed samples from different hours and models to compute accurate overall speed numbers on a dashboard. This is internal tooling used by the Freebuff engineering team to build the latency dashboard, and it does not affect anything you see or do in the assistant or CLI today. For now the helpers sit in the codebase and are not connected to anything that writes or reads data yet, so there is no visible behavior change for you right now.

c9bdd9c7b58e05b498d296cf64fcaaa3db54890d.text: The agent runtime now prevents the same tool result from being added to the conversation history more than once, which previously happened when developers retried a failed task through the SDK. This affects developers using the Freebuff SDK to run automated coding tasks and retry them after failures. You will not notice this in daily use, but it stops conversations from breaking mid-task when retries cause duplicate results.

1b28a1b851243771ec6e1433673df5e676496f9c.title: Base3 single-loop roots register per model with windowed reads
1b28a1b851243771ec6e1433673df5e676496f9c.summary: Per-model `base3-free-*` root agent ids are registered for Freebuff Web/Cloud in `free-agents.ts`, each pinned to exactly the model its base3 twin carries, with a test asserting the map and `FREEBUFF_ROOT_AGENT_IDS` agree. The SDK in `sdk/src/run.ts` now forwards the model-supplied `fileWindows` map to `read_files` overrides instead of dropping it, closing the prior TODO that yielded whole files on hosted surfaces; windowing is applied before the local read budget so offset reads do not truncate content. `gravity-index.ts` attributes `base3-free*` traffic to `freebuff_web` for Gravity conversions, matching the base2 prefix. Four distinct changes land across `free-agents.ts`, `file-read-limits.ts`, `gravity-index.ts`, and `sdk/src/run.ts`.
1b28a1b851243771ec6e1433673df5e676496f9c.evidence: Added `FREEBUFF_WEB_BASE3_AGENT_ID_BY_MODEL` map and `base3-free-*` root ids to `FREEBUFF_ROOT_AGENT_IDS` and `FREE_MODE_AGENT_MODELS` (spread-derived) in `common/src/constants/free-agents.ts`; registered the `base3-free-*` roots in `FREEBUFF_ROOT_AGENT_IDS`. Added `FileReadWindows`, `applyFileReadWindows`, `fileReadWindowsOf` to `common/src/util/file-read-limits.ts`; SDK `run.ts` now forwards `fileWindows` to `read_files` overrides instead of dropping it (replacing the prior TODO that returned whole files). `packages/agent-runtime/src/tools/handlers/tool/gravity-index.ts` `gravitySurface()` now returns `freebuff_web` for `base3-free*` ids alongside `base2-free*`.
1b28a1b851243771ec6e1433673df5e676496f9c.unknowns: The diff does not show the `agents/base3.ts` harness definition or the web bundle's `FREEBUFF_MODEL_TO_AGENT_ID`, which are asserted but not modified here; rollout of the base2-to-base3 routing is implied by the FREEBUFF_BASE3_HARNESS_DISABLED kill switch.

changes.what: Registers per-model `base3-free-*` root ids in `FREEBUFF_ROOT_AGENT_IDS` and derives their single-model allowlist from `FREEBUFF_WEB_BASE3_AGENT_ID_BY_MODEL` in `FREE_MODE_AGENT_MODELS`, gating each to its pinned model.

Adds `FileReadWindows` type and `fileReadWindowsOf` / `applyFileReadWindows` helpers so a `windowedFileReads` agent can forward `{path, offset, limit}` read windows that are applied before the read budget.
Extends `gravitySurface()` to map `base3-free*` agent ids to the `freebuff_web` attribution surface, keeping Web/Cloud base3 roots out of the CLI conversion bucket.
Forwards the `fileWindows` map into `read_files` overrides in `readFiles()` (replacing the dropped-field TODO), so hosted surfaces window content before their own limiter truncates it.

d1c94381b39773dbd68e9c7ebbd4909724179110.title: Replace terminal isolation lease with terminal command broker
d1c94381b39773dbd68e9c7ebbd4909724179110.summary: The CLI replaces the synchronous terminal isolation lease with a console-free command broker model: `cli/src/utils/terminal-command-broker.ts` exports `createTerminalCommandBroker`, which spawns a detached helper via the new `--terminal-command-broker` flag and returns a handle owning the complete spawned process tree, while `cli/src/entry.ts` dispatches broker invocations before importing OpenTUI. `sdk/src/tools/run-terminal-command.ts` now accepts an optional `terminalCommandBroker` and calls `broker.start(request)` instead of acquiring an isolation lease before `spawn`, with the SDK types in `sdk/src/index.ts` and `sdk/src/run.ts` renamed from `TerminalCommandIsolation` to `TerminalCommandBroker` (`terminalCommandIsolation` to `terminalCommandBroker`). The CLI surfaces, smoke, and client wiring in `cli/src/commands/router.ts`, `cli/src/utils/codebuff-client.ts`, `cli/src/smoke/terminal-command-broker.ts`, plus the renamed smoke script and docs, pass `terminalCommandBroker` through, and the smoke test was renamed from `terminal-command-isolation.ts` to `terminal-command-broker.ts` alongside `cli/scripts/smoke-terminal-isolation-windows.ts` to `cli/scripts/smoke-terminal-broker-windows.ts`.
d1c94381b39773dbd68e9c7ebbd4909724179110.evidence: New file `cli/src/entry.ts` routes `--terminal-command-broker` invocations to `serveTerminalCommandBroker` and otherwise loads the TUI; `cli/src/utils/terminal-command-broker.ts` defines `createTerminalCommandBroker` returning a `TerminalCommandBroker` with a `start` method that spawns a detached helper over stdin and returns a handle owning the process tree; `sdk/src/tools/run-terminal-command.ts` replaces the `terminalCommandIsolation` acquire/release lease with an optional `terminalCommandBroker` whose `start(request)` is used in place of a direct `spawn`; `cli/src/commands/router.ts`, `cli/src/utils/codebuff-client.ts`, and `cli/src/smoke/terminal-command-broker.ts` import and pass `terminalCommandBroker` instead of `terminalCommandIsolation`; `sdk/src/index.ts` and `sdk/src/run.ts` rename the type to `TerminalCommandBroker` and the option to `terminalCommandBroker`.
d1c94381b39773dbd68e9c7ebbd4909724179110.migration: If you pass terminalCommandIsolation or implement TerminalCommandIsolation in a custom client or SDK consumer, switch to terminalCommandBroker using the new TerminalCommandBroker.start(request): TerminalCommandProcess signature.
d1c94381b39773dbd68e9c7ebbd4909724179110.unknowns: The diff does not show the consumer side or rollout of the new --smoke-terminal-broker smoke flag beyond the renamed smoke script.

changes.what: Adds `cli/src/entry.ts` to dispatch `--terminal-command-broker` invocations to the broker helper before loading the TUI, and adds `cli/src/utils/terminal-command-broker.ts` implementing `createTerminalCommandBroker` plus the exported `TERMINAL_COMMAND_BROKER_FLAG`,.

Renames the smoke entrypoint and script from terminal-command-isolation to terminal-command-broker, and updates `cli/package.json` and `cli/scripts/build-binary.ts` to compile and run `src/entry.ts` instead of `src/index.tsx`.
Swaps the `terminalCommandIsolation` import for `terminalCommandBroker` in the bash command runner, client factory, and smoke test, passing the broker into `runTerminalCommand`.

Renames `TerminalCommandIsolation` to `TerminalCommandBroker` and `terminalCommandIsolation` to `terminalCommandBroker` across the SDK type exports, run options, and the `run_terminal_command` tool, and replaces the acquire/release lease with `broker.start(request)`.
Rewrites `docs/agents-and-tools.md` from a terminal command isolation section to a console-free terminal command broker section describing the new broker contract.

ef5190fe8024ca729df82dfa11c847354a3ca279.title: CLI 1.0.686: AVX2 crash persistence, watchdog opt-out, Windows theme
ef5190fe8024ca729df82dfa11c847354a3ca279.summary: The release launcher now records a machine as lacking AVX2 after an illegal-instruction failure via `recordMachineLacksAvx2()`, which writes `cpu-features.json` so `readCachedAvx2()` answers upfront on the next launch instead of relying on a prior PowerShell CPUID probe. To make the optimistic-then-corrected AVX2 path testable, the launcher's exported `__testing` object exposes `detectMachineHasAvx2`, `recordMachineLacksAvx2`, `readCachedAvx2`, and the other internals, and the `configDirOverride` option lets tests redirect config out of the real `~/.config/manicode`. The terminal-reset watchdog gained a `CODEBUFF_NO_TERMINAL_WATCHDOG` env opt-out for locked-down Windows machines where the PowerShell bootstrap trips EDR/AV, and `detectPlatformTheme` in `theme-system.ts` drops its Windows PowerShell probes so the platform falls through to `dark` rather than reporting an unrelated child host's background color.
ef5190fe8024ca729df82dfa11c847354a3ca279.evidence: diff hunk in cli/release-core/launcher.js adds `configDirOverride` to the destructured config with a test-only comment, and the final return object includes a `__testing` block listing `detectMachineHasAvx2`, `recordMachineLacksAvx2`, `readCachedAvx2`, `isIllegalInstructionExit`, `getDefaultTargetKey`, `getCpuFeatureCachePath`, `getCurrentVersion`, `isTargetAllowedForThisMachine`, and `CONFIG`; the same file adds `recordMachineLacksAvx2()` which writes `cpu-features.json`, and comments state `tryFallbackToBaseline` calls `recordMachineLacksAvx2()` after a recorded illegal-instruction failure; cli/src/types/env.ts and cli/src/utils/env.ts add `CODEBUFF_NO_TERMINAL_WATCHDOG`; cli/src/utils/terminal-watchdog.ts adds `isOptedOut` and checks `CODEBUFF_NO_TERMINAL_WATCHDOG` to skip arming in `startTerminalWatchdog`; cli/src/utils/theme-system.ts removes the `detectWindowsPowerShellTheme` helper and the win32 `HKCU AppsUseLightTheme` read from `detectPlatformTheme`, leaving Windows to fall through to `'dark'`.
ef5190fe8024ca729df82dfa11c847354a3ca279.migration: If you previously relied on the CLI probing PowerShell for Windows CPU features or theme colors, those probes are removed and no action is required.
ef5190fe8024ca729df82dfa11c847354a3ca279.unknowns: The diff does not show the consumer of the new `configDirOverride` option or which package passes it into `createLauncher()`.

254c227edee9d656de7fc74312468062e17f7a1e.title: CLI explains session-locked rejection in chat on deliberate pick
254c227edee9d656de7fc74312468062e17f7a1e.summary: The Freebuff session hook now distinguishes a deliberate model pick from a background rejoin, so when the server rejects a user-chosen model with a session lock, the CLI posts a system message in chat instead of silently reverting. The marker is set at pick time in startFreebuffSession and consumed on the first response, so stale picks can never annotate later, unrelated locks. This turns the recurring confusion of clicked-a-model-but-it-switched to a visible explanation referencing /end-session.
254c227edee9d656de7fc74312468062e17f7a1e.evidence: In cli/src/hooks/use-freebuff-session.ts, the session-locked branch now consumes a new explicit-pick marker (set in startFreebuffSession and cleared on each response) and, when the lock rejects a deliberate user choice of model, posts a system message via useChatStore.setMessages and getSystemMessage naming the current and requested model display names.
254c227edee9d656de7fc74312468062e17f7a1e.unknowns: A second read of the same diff did not confirm that a migration step is required.

6cc0c94c19331c4a4009587d3b698916f00f9f0a.title: Web referral tier ladder removed from referral tiers file
6cc0c94c19331c4a4009587d3b698916f00f9f0a.summary: The web referral tier ladder (1/3/7 referrals scaling daily model limits and removing the deploy watermark) was deleted from `common/src/constants/freebuff-referral-tiers.ts`, along with eight associated exports: `FreebuffReferralTier`, `FREEBUFF_REFERRAL_TIERS`, `MAX_FREEBUFF_REFERRAL_TIER`, `FREEBUFF_WATERMARK_REMOVAL_TIER`, `FREEBUFF_WATERMARK_REMOVAL_REFERRALS`, `getReferralTier`, `getTierLimits`, and `getNextReferralTier`. The file retains only qualification machinery: `MIN_GITHUB_ACCOUNT_AGE_MONTHS`, `MIN_GITHUB_ACCOUNT_AGE_MONTHS_GLM`, `MIN_GITHUB_ACCOUNT_AGE_MONTHS_REFERRAL`, `REFERRAL_CLI_DAILY_SESSION_BONUS_CAP`, `FREEBUFF_WEB_REFERRAL_LIMIT`, `REFERRAL_SIGNUP_WINDOW_DAYS`, `FREEBUFF_REFERRAL_SIGNUP_LIMIT`, and `isGithubAccountOldEnoughForReferral`. Per the file's docblock, the removed ladder's limits were never enforced anywhere and the deploy watermark is globally disabled, leaving the remaining constants as account-age bars, attribution windows, and anti-farming ceilings.
6cc0c94c19331c4a4009587d3b698916f00f9f0a.evidence: Removed exports FreebuffReferralTier, FREEBUFF_REFERRAL_TIERS, MAX_FREEBUFF_REFERRAL_TIER, FREEBUFF_WATERMARK_REMOVAL_TIER, FREEBUFF_WATERMARK_REMOVAL_REFERRALS, getReferralTier, getTierLimits, getNextReferralTier from common/src/constants/freebuff-referral-tiers.ts and deleted the 4-tier web referral ladder array defining standardModelDailyLimit, premiumModelDailyLimit, and removesWatermark fields.
6cc0c94c19331c4a4009587d3b698916f00f9f0a.migration: If you import any of the removed referral tier exports (`FreebuffReferralTier`, `FREEBUFF_REFERRAL_TIERS`, `MAX_FREEBUFF_REFERRAL_TIER`, `FREEBUFF_WATERMARK_REMOVAL_TIER`, `FREEBUFF_WATERMARK_REMOVAL_REFERRALS`, `getReferralTier`, `getTierLimits`, `getNextReferralTier`) from `common/src/constants/freebuff-referral-tiers.ts`, your code will fail to compile and you must remove or replace those.
6cc0c94c19331c4a4009587d3b698916f00f9f0a.unknowns: The commit does not show which consumers previously imported the removed exports or how billing/analytics now source the referral reward behavior previously implied by the tier ladder.

9f80be02582ab23c45aa4fd7adf8370b2613ad92.title: Kimi K2.7 Code retired from client picker, settings now validate
9f80be02582ab23c45aa4fd7adf8370b2613ad92.summary: The Kimi K2.7 Code route (`FREEBUFF_KIMI_MODEL_ID` / `KIMI_MODEL`) was removed from the client-visible model catalog `FREEBUFF_MODELS` and from `FREEBUFF_WEB_DEEMPHASIZED_MODEL_IDS`, but it remains in `SUPPORTED_FREEBUFF_MODELS` and `FREEBUFF_PREMIUM_MODEL_IDS` so existing sessions are not stranded, with a new comment stating it is too expensive to offer as a free model. The README and the release README both updated the model listings to remove 'Kimi K2.7 Code' and the 'Powered by' line to read 'MiMo' instead of 'Kimi'.

0ff93e746badad951717b0a70386bf5b24701517.title: Agent runtime drops orphaned tool calls before each step
0ff93e746badad951717b0a70386bf5b24701517.summary: runAgentStep now runs the message history through filterUnfinishedToolCalls right before building each step prompt, so an assistant message that was interrupted before a tool result is issued no longer reaches the provider. The cleaned history is written back to agentState.messageHistory, which keeps the checkpointed state valid for the next turn and any spawned subagent that replays it. DeepSeek and other strict providers reject a lone tool call with a 400, so this also stops a single orphaned call from failing all later turns.

c731787cd02fea9b5d37c9e5e6fb06c0e3897045.title: Shared polling backoff replaces fixed-interval retries in CLI
c731787cd02fea9b5d37c9e5e6fb06c0e3897045.summary: A new `cli/src/utils/polling-backoff.ts` module centralizes the CLI's retry and cadence logic, exporting `failedPollDelayMs` and `jitterPollIntervalMs` which add equal-jitter exponential backoff (`FAILURE_BACKOFF_BASE_MS = 20_000`, `FAILURE_BACKOFF_MAX_MS = 300_000`) to failed polls and jitter to healthy polling intervals. `useConnectionStatus` now calls `scheduleFailedCheck` plus `failedPollDelayMs`/`jitterPollIntervalMs` instead of resetting a fixed `INITIAL_INTERVAL`, and `useFreebuffSession` feeds `retryAfterMs` (parsed from `response.headers.get('retry-after')` by the new `parseRetryAfterMs`) into `failedPollDelayMs` via the `FreebuffSessionRequestError` type. This removes the hardcoded `POLL_INTERVAL_ERROR_MS = 10_000` path so a shared backend outage no longer synchronizes every CLI into a fixed retry wave.
c731787cd02fea9b5d37c9e5e6fb06c0e3897045.evidence: New file `cli/src/utils/polling-backoff.ts` defines `failedPollDelayMs`, `jitterPollIntervalMs`, `FAILURE_BACKOFF_BASE_MS = 20_000`, `FAILURE_BACKOFF_MAX_MS = 300_000`, and `RandomSource`; both `useConnectionStatus` and `useFreebuffSession` now import and call these helpers instead of the old fixed-error interval, and `FreebuffSessionRequestError` plus `parseRetryAfterMs` were added to `cli/src/utils/freebuff-session-api.ts` and consumed in `callFreebuffSession`'s error throw and the session hook's catch path.

1614c75f6c19c5cd6ee24e0fab2d21382e012e0c.title: SDK rewrites Windows nul redirects to dev null
1614c75f6c19c5cd6ee24e0fab2d21382e012e0c.summary: The SDK terminal tool now rewrites cmd-style `> nul` and `2> nul` redirections to `/dev/null` before running under Git Bash on Windows, preventing commands from creating an undeletable literal file named `nul`.
